ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_Rook_Dolg_Armor_description: Standard-issue attire for rank-and-file Duty members, this suit has been maliciously dubbed the “body bag” due to its perceived inadequacy for mutant hunting — the faction’s main pursuit.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_Rook_Svoboda_Armor_description: Lightweight Freedom group gear set. Usually used by rookies, but also loved by many veterans for its sporty comfort.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_SEVA_Dolg_Armor_description: Compared to the original SEVA suit, the main distinction of the Duty version lies is its integration with the armored vests of the PSZ-5 series. While significantly lowering production and maintenance expenses, this measure comes with trade-offs in certain performance aspects.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_SEVA_Monolith_Armor_descriptio: «Why did you abandon us? We can’t hear you. We’re waiting for your orders.»
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_SEVA_Neutral_Armor_description: A top-notch suit manufactured by a defense company outside the Zone. It integrates a lightweight bulletproof vest, a sealed breathing system, and advanced technologies designed to mitigate the harmful impact of anomalies and radiation.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_SEVA_Spark_Armor_description: A common gripe with the SEVA suit revolves around the insufficient level of protection offered by its integrated bulletproof vest. The upgraded Spark version seeks to eliminate this issue.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_SEVA_Svoboda_Armor_description: The famous and legendary SEVA, exquisitely upgraded by the Freedom craftsman Screw. Some of the solutions are quite surprising, but none of them made it less comfortable to wear.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_SS_PGO7Scope_description: An optical scope designed to magnify the effective range and accuracy of the RPG-7U rocket-propelled grenade launcher.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_Sausage_description: The key advantage of this sausage is its long shelf life. It’s best not to speculate on how this is achieved in order to avoid ruining your appetite and those of others.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_SkinJacket_Bandit_Armor_descri: An inexpensive dark jacket worn by thugs everywhere. It won’t actually protect you, but it makes you look dope as hell.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_UltraLight_Mercenaries_Armor_d: A suit upgraded for the Rostok bar bouncers. High-molecular polyethylene plates reduce weight, along with bullet resistance.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_Veles_description: An improved second-generation detector. Despite its relatively high price, this detector is favored by seasoned stalkers for its user-friendly interface, reliability, and remarkable efficiency.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_Vodka_description: A must-have alcoholic drink produced by GSC, renowned for its ability to flush radiation from the body. It's also an excellent remedy against the tedium of everyday life in the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_Water_description: Finding clean water in the Zone is no easy task, since all natural sources there are contaminated with radiation. Fortunately, this isn't an issue on the Mainland yet.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_X7_Armor_description: A special gear kit developed for working in the conditions of the X7 Lab. Origins unknown.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_Zorya_Neutral_Armor_descriptio: A masterpiece of local craftsmenship, this suit combines two layers of rubberized fabric with a polymer lining and a bulletproof vest effective against pistol bullets. The Sunrise’s reasonable price and upgrade potential have solidified its status as a top-selling item.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_Zorya_Tourist_Armor_descriptio: The former owner of this suit had an excellent understanding of weight distribution and echeloning of equipment. Redesigned pockets, a corset that relieves the back, additional pouches and a travel backpack allow you to carry more weight, which is very handy during long raids into the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_moneyCard_description: A compact data carrier that can be used in PDAs, laptops, and other devices. Stalkers often use such memory cards to store coupons in caches.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_mutpartspack_MutantPartBayun_d: Scientists call them "biogenic superconductors." No one knows what that is, so they drag them to the technicians — still conductors, right? And the techs send the unlucky hunters back to the merchants.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_mutpartspack_MutantPartBlindDo: Scientists believe that these glands help blind dogs navigate much better than their non-blind counterparts. Until this theory is proven or rejected, they will be valuable.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_mutpartspack_MutantPartBloodsu: Rumor has it that the hemostatic agents in the scientists' first aid kits are made from these. Sometimes the less you know, the better.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_mutpartspack_MutantPartBoar_de: A rookie's favorite trophy. Selling it to traders is quite honorable, while smartasses who bought a fang for bragging rights are the laughingstock at any campfire.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_mutpartspack_MutantPartBurer_d: No matter what tricks these mutants play on gravity, they always stand firmly on their feet. To understand why, scientists order their toes, hundreds of them. However, for the merchant to accept the loot, the fingertip must be intact.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_mutpartspack_MutantPartChimera: Collectors are ready to pay an arm and a leg for the mutated ears, but stalkers who have earned this trophy are not ready to part with it. After all, the chimera ear is proof you're a true stalker legend.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_mutpartspack_MutantPartControl: Any psi-effect researcher's dream and the most desired drug of world research institutes. Although scientists hardly think about the price at which it ended up in their lab.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_mutpartspack_MutantPartFlesh_d: Everyone hates swarms of fleshes — especially couriers. That's why traders are willing to pay for their enlarged eye, as proof of kill.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_mutpartspack_MutantPartHornhea: Incredibly light and very sturdy. No one yet understands what mutations made them this way, but growing this kind of “living armor” in a laboratory is a gunsmith's dream.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_mutpartspack_MutantPartPolterg: Scientists are trying to figure out which of the poltergeist's organs gives them invisibility. And until they figure it out, merchants are buying them all up.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_mutpartspack_MutantPartPseudod: There is a theory that pseudodogs' ability to coordinate their phantoms is linked to receptors on their skin. Solving this mystery could be a breakthrough in creating new camouflage.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_mutpartspack_MutantPartPseudog: People on the mainland used to buy rare horns and tusks — now "magical" properties have been given to the nails of pseudogiants. What matters is folks are still willing to pay.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_mutpartspack_MutantPartRodent_: Some stalker in Zalissya used to say rodent paws bring luck — and now merchants buy them as good luck charms. That stalker was mauled by bloodsuckers long ago, though. Looks like the charm wasn't so lucky after all.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_mutpartspack_MutantPartSnork_d: A snork's neck vertebra, mutated to withstand mutant jumps. Word is, dog tags of some stalkers were found grown into in the bones.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_myriflepack_GunKora_HG_descrip: Pistol with a capital “P”. A true classic of firearm engineering. Designed over a century ago, yet still relevant today thanks to its powerful ammunition and near-total reliability under any conditions.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_myriflepack_GunKora_MagIncreas: Extended high-capacity magazine for the Kora pistol. Solves the main issue of the weapon — lack of ammunition in the factory version.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_myriflepack_GunThreeLine_SP_de: This venerable three-line rifle spans both world wars and numerous other military conflicts. Legend has it its bullets can cut through rails — lengthwise.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_myriflepack_Gun_NightStalker_H: A unique variant of the classic pistol. Custom-made components appear to have been precisely fitted during assembly. Chambered in 9mm Parabellum.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nvgpack_Gun_Dragunka_SR_descri: This rifle served Honta for years, and now it has been passed on to his student. It's been well looked after and is still in good working order. Whether you're up against a rhino or a chimera, it won't fail you.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nvgpack_NVG_gen1_description: NVG developed in the 1960s. Based on an ancient image intensifier, they're easily damaged and susceptible to overexposure and interference. Not the most effective device, but better than nothing.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nvgpack_NVG_gen2_description: Classic NVG from the 90s. The Gen 2 image intensifier has better light sensitivity, and the two lenses expand the field of view. A good compromise between cost and effectiveness.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nvgpack_NVG_gen3a_description: Modern night-vision goggles. The quadrocular layout provides a wide field of view, and the powerful image intensifier has a high-brightness matrix capable of 'extracting' light, even from the darkest corners of the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nvgpack_NVG_gen3b_description: A rare upgrade of the Gen 3 goggles. The standard intensifier has been replaced, changing the classic green light to a softer white.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_Binoculars_01_descripti: Field Optical Binoculars with a 45 mm lens diameter. A simple and reliable design. This is the kind of gear that’s hard to wreck even in the extreme conditions of the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_Binoculars_02_descripti: This device was developed specifically for use in the Zone. Its fail-safe design and moderate use of modern technology have earned the "Yastrub" popularity among Zone veterans.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_Binoculars_03_descripti: A modern European binocular. This device leans heavily on the latest digital technologies, which significantly expand its functionality. However, this comes at a price, so the device never found much popularity among stalkers.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_EN_X3Scope_1_descriptio: A classic optical sight manufactured in Great Britain. Originally designed for the IL 86 rifle, it can also be used with other weapon models.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_GunArevPrecise_AR_GS_de: ARev version with modifications to enhance marksmanship capabilities. An 8x sight, heavy stock for comfortable bracing, reinforced barrel with 1:8 twist for better stability, and a silencer – the perfect setup for a precision shooter.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_GunArev_ST_description: A game-changer in the world of guns. A modern assault rifle developed to potentially replace all platforms with intermediate and rifle calibers. Precise, reliable, comfortable. The only disadvantage is the price.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_GunFora230_MagIncreased: High-capacity magazine for the Fora. Initially developed for anti-terrorist operations, but later made its way to army units.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_GunFora230_PP_descripti: Modern Ukraine-produced submachine gun, developed for combat vehicle crews and police special ops units. Thanks to its size and rate of fire, it found its niche in the Zone as well.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_GunGP3A_DMR_description: Classic German Cold War era rifle. Thanks to its overall ergonomics, decent reliability, and sturdy ammunition, this weapon system is still widely used.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_GunGP3A_MagIncreased_de: High-capacity magazine that fits GP3 weapon systems.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_GunGP3A_MagLarge_descri: A GP3 high-capacity drum magazine. Developed within a section firepower enhancement program: the soldier with the drum magazine was supposed to act as a machine gunner without having to re-equip.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_GunSKP_MagIncreased_des: High-capacity magazine for rifle caliber self-loading infantry carbines.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_GunSKP_SP_description: The trend of regular infantry returning to the rifle carbine has finally reached the infantry carbine that was developed way back in World War II. A heavy-duty round and a modern stock allow this platform to be recognized as the same class as modern systems.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_SU_ColimScope_1_descrip: Collimator for rifles and assault rifles, equipped with a dovetail mount. The components of this version are simpler than those of its Western counterparts, but the hardware is good for the job.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_nwpack_SU_X3Scope_1_descriptio: A Soviet infantry sight that fits all weapons with a dovetail mount. Developed as a mass-produced, lightweight, and cheap analogue of the PSO.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_items_supack_Gun_GP37V2_AR_descripti: A rare modification of the GP37, designed for the German Navy. Its key distinction from the base version is the replacement of its automatic fire with a three-round burst mode. It was released in a limited run and failed to find favor.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_DLC01_MQ03_Journal_Name: In the heart of the Iron Forest
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_DLC01_MQ08_Journal_Name: The destructive power of the mind
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_DLC01_MQ11_B01_Journal_Name: The road to the center of the storm
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_E05_MQ05_Name: Like a Moth to the Flame
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_E06_MQ04_Name: To the Last Drop of Blood
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_E07_MQ01_Name: Just Like the Good Old Days
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_E15_MQ02_Name: Through the valley of the shadow of death
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_SQ06_Name: A Light in the End of the Tunnel
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_ALTQuest01_Descr: The Zone overwhelms us sometimes. And sometimes you just have to let some steam off.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC00_ItemHunt_J: It seems that in the Zone, challenges and mysteries await me at every step. I need to be prepared. First, I'll look in my personal Storage box — maybe there's something there to help me on the way.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_FactionWar: After they lost at the CNPP, Freedom is hoping for a rematch by capturing the nearby territories. I have to stop them from assuming advanced positions to seize the plant. I don't know what they're hoping for. Freedom has already lost to Duty once, and it will do so again.

After they lost at the CNPP, Duty is hoping for a rematch by capturing the advanced positions leading to it. We have already lost too many defending the plant – we can't lose now. Duty will have to retreat once and for all, and I will do everything in my power to make sure that happens.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ00_Journ: Word is, a stalker who's been to the Iron Forest came to the Slag Heap. He's willing to share his story in exchange for drinks. Can't hurt to try and stop by, see what he knows. This could be my chance to sneak into the restricted area.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ02_C01_J: I don't know what I was expecting from the Iron Forest, but definitely not this. Anomalies, tons of mutants, strange flashes. What's next? It feels like the more you learn about the Zone, the less you actually know about it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ02_Journ: The union of Freedom and Duty is a lot to process, but there's no time to think about it – we need to deal with the blasts. Zulu, the captain of the Duty squad, believes they can be eliminated. I don't know if the plan will work, but it's worth a try, especially since even the Freedom commander, Harpoon, supports it. The Duty repeaters can locate the source of the blasts, we just need to help Mavka and Nitro install them.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ03_C01_J: We were looking for the source of the blasts, but stumbled upon something much more fascinating – the device that generated them was somehow connected to the legendary healing Oasis. We also found Lukash, an old acquaintance of Mavka. Unfortunately, he died in her arms after we destroyed the device and the Oasis vanished. I need to find out what's happening here, and who's behind Lukash's death.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ03_Journ: Zulu is now completely sure Nitro's theory was correct. The blasts have a technogenic nature, which means it's possible to destroy their source. Mavka managed to find out it's in the Testing Workshop. These two are working together, despite the fact they're in different factions. They're asking for help to get into the Workshop and deal with the blasts once and for all.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ04_Journ: Duty was accused of murdering Freedom in Kurin – but Mavka and Zulu think otherwise. Together, they took on the investigation to find the real culprits, and there are already some leads to chase. It's bold for them to keep working together now that D4 is over. But if we can prove their suspicions are right, it may be possible to stop the war between the factions.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ06_Journ:
The picture is becoming clearer. The massacre in the Iron Forest was the work of Nord and his mercenaries. They made all the noise as cover so that no one would stick their noses into their business. 
They're searching for Project X technology, and seem to know where to look. Their target is the Bubble, a spatial anomaly, and it seems that whatever they're after is still inside it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ07_Journ: It's now clear that the mercenaries didn't just slaughter Kurin, but are somehow connected to Lukash's death. Mavka believes we can find out more if we search his stashes that are hidden around the Zone. I hope the stashes will tell us who Lukash was working with, and what they were after. Then we can figure out what his end game was.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ08_Journ: Nord stole the technology that Tachenko was guarding and Chekhov is looking for. He wants to use it for his own gain. Hardly altruistic. Mavka and Zulu can't let that happen, and I agree. The Zone has enough problems. I need to meet with allies and decide how exactly we'll stop the mercenaries, and how we'll get back what was stolen.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ09_Journ: Mavka and Zulu were looking for the Iron Forest murderers to end the war between factions, but they've now became enemies themselves. I chose Mavka's side, and for that, Zulu left us to die in the laboratory. He's already gone to the CNPP to destroy all remaining specimens of the technology. Mavka wants to talk to Myklukha and find out how we can get to the CNPP faster than Zulu. I hope he can help us.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ10_B01_J: Everything went to hell in the lab. Mavka and Zulu can't work together anymore – she sees salvation in the technology, he sees it as a threat. The clash of factions is now inevitable. Mavka is rushing to the CNPP, while Zulu is heading to Voronin. Without his support, we can't defeat Freedom. But Zulu and Voronin under one roof is a dangerous combination. Either they'll forget past grudges and unite, or we're dead.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ10_B02_J: In the Arena, Myklukha proved he would rather die than let Freedom change, and those winds of change knocked him down. Now that we have the coordinates for the way into the Monorail, we have a chance to reach the CNPP before Zulu does. However, a short way doesn't always mean an easy one.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ11_B01_J: After Voronin's death, Duty has been brought down, but not broken. Thanks to the general's sacrifice, we managed to launch the Monorail and reach the CNPP. Zulu is now even more determined to stop Mavka's plan.
The escape from Myklukha's treasury was successful, and the Monorail took us to the CNPP. Mavka became a true leader, ready to fight till the end. I believe that, now, we can stop Zulu.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ11_B02_J: Duty is preparing to storm the only place at the CNPP that can be called safe – at the very heart of the Flare. Duty has a significant advantage in numbers, but a well-organized defense will help us fight them off.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ11_B03_J: The Freedom members who arrived at the CNPP before Duty managed to occupy a strategic point. Zulu has organized an assault team for a decisive attack. We need to seize Freedom's positions, the only safe place for miles, or else the anomaly and radiation will kill us one by one. But if we have to die, it's better we do it on our own terms.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_MQ12_Journ: Mavka found a way into X19. She believes the technology inside will bring freedom to everyone, even beyond the Zone. Zulu is coming to destroy it. He's close, and he will not stop. We need to beat him to it.

Zulu and Mavka were looking for those responsible for the massacre in the Iron Forest so they could stop the war. Now, they are leading this war. I took Zulu's side, we defeated Freedom, and have secured our positions inside the CNPP. Now we just need to find X19 and destroy what's hidden there before Mavka releases it to the outside world. Zulu is convinced the technologies of Project X are too dangerous, and I agree. But if we're too late, the decision won't be ours to make.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_RRQ_Descri: I’ve stirred up trouble with one of the factions in the Zone. It’s best to lay low until things settle down, then discuss terms with their leader.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_SQ01_Journ: I stumbled upon an IPSF base being attacked by mutants. Looks like these soldiers could use my help. The gate to the Iron Forest is right here, at this checkpoint, so this might be my chance to get in. I better not miss out on it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_SQ02_Journ: The PDA of the dead stalker had the coordinates of the presumed entrance to the Iron Forest. It's worth checking out.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_SQ03_Journ: A couple of Duty members who decided to join IPSF were sent on a test mission. They were supposed to clear the basement and get the tokens from military stalkers who tried to clear it, but never succeeded. It got pretty rough, and one of the Duty members will stay in the basement for good. So this is no easy job.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_SQ04_Journ: Khoryv from Freedom is asking me to rescue his man from the bandits who took him. The meeting place is set on Duty territory, so he needs a mediator. That will be me. As soon as the hostage lets Khoryv know he's free, I'll get my payment.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_SQ06_C01_J: The Duty squad got into trouble at the Dam and requested an evacuation team. Captain Bulat sent me to scout ahead and help the survivors.
A Duty squad on the Dam was hit by psі radiation from an unknown source while clearing mutants. I need to help the survivors and figure out what happened.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_SQ06_Journ: It's best to stay out of sight of the Duty military instructors, as they'll always find a task for you. Captain Bulat asked me to show the new recruits how to shoot.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_SQ07_Journ: Loyalty cannot be gained, it can only be earned.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_SQ09_Journ: Do Mercenary's have a code of honor?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_SQ13_Descr: The dead Freedom member had a PDA with a request for help. His friend claimed their squad found something valuable – something that would ensure a safe exit from the CNPP. It's somehow connected to the Flare. We need to find out what happened to the squad, and what they were looking for.

A group of Freedom fighters got into trouble while searching for something that would let them safely exit the CNPP. It was connected to the Flare. I need to find the group, but I don't know what happened to them. I hope they're still alive.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_SQ14_Descr: Something strange is happening around the CNPP – the whole hub is on edge. Some people are talking about a mysterious 'ghost', others predict the return of the Monolith, while the rest are gossiping about yet another secret technology. It's better to get to the bottom of this as soon as possible, before things take a turn for the worse.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_SQ15_Journ: I found a lone stalker's shelter at the CNPP. It's a strange place – the walls are covered with drawings and notes. The owner ran away when he saw me. What is he hiding? Who is he afraid of? I need to find him and figure out what's going on.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_DLC01_SQ16_Descr: A scientist from the CNPP hub claims that the archanomaly which destroyed the building holds a powerful artifact. But getting close to it is not that easy.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E01_MQ01_Descrip: Seems like a fair trade-off: Hermann gets my special stone, and I get a new home and hope for a new life. All I have to do is cross the Perimeter and successfully activate the Scanner. That know-it-all insists it’s the only way to restore the anomalous properties of my faded artifact. I’m just hoping this little experiment won’t drag on too long, regardless of the tall tales going around about this Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E02_MQ01_Descrip: Now I’ve lost both the Scanner and the artifact, and my head’s still reeling from the blow it took. Hermann has gone off the air, so I’ll have to find those bastards myself. I guess I need to scout the area and find a place where the locals gather to exchange the latest news and rumors.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E02_MQ02_C01_Des: As it turns out, there’s a way to track Squint – or at least his PDA. The Gaffer mentioned that the tower in Zalissya and a technician called Lens can help me out.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E02_MQ02_C03_Des: Squint asked me to retrieve a particular artifact. He claims it could help him escape from the Lesser Zone, even with the Ward’s quarantine in place. I guess I’ll get it for him, and then we’ll see where things stand.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E02_MQ02_Descrip: The residents of Zalissya apparently know Solder, but they’re still reluctant to tell me about him. Their terms are clear: if I want intel on Solder, I gotta find Squint first. Looks like I’ll have to trade a looter for a snitch.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E02_MQ03_C01_Des: There’s an Emission coming. Even from a distance, it looks truly apocalyptic. If I get caught in the open, it’s game over for me. I gotta find shelter before it reaches Zalissya.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E02_MQ03_Descrip:
The plan I made with Hermann has failed because of that slippery guy Solder. Although, I have to admit that one out of three coordinates did turn out to be golden, just not for me.
He sold us out. But to whom? I need to track the bastard down and interrogate him with extreme prejudice. That’s the only way to get the Scanner back.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E02_SQ01_C01_Des: I helped a stalker called Zhorik fight off some bandits at the Post Office. Turns out his partner is being held captive by the same gang. They’re holed up in the Boiler House. Zhorik asked me to rescue Gloomy if I can.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E02_SQ02_Descrip: I’ve heard from the locals that the most important people in the Zone are technicians and traders. I should find both in Zalissya and see what they can do for me.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E03_MQ01_Descrip: Solder turned out to be nothing more than a flunky. Nevertheless, he still served a purpose: he told me that a guy called Nestor was the mastermind behind the entire scanner scheme. Zotov told me to go to the Chemical Plant, the Ward’s headquarters, and talk to Colonel Korshunov. I hope he’ll be willing to help me.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E03_MQ02_Descrip: Solder turned out to be nothing more than a flunky. Nevertheless, he still served a purpose: he told me that a guy called Nestor was the mastermind behind the entire scanner scheme. Richter said his stalker friends at the Detention Center can help me find him.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E03_MQ03_Descrip: Varan claims that Nestor set him up. He says his bandits were also targeted because of the Scanner, and now he’s holding one of the attackers prisoner. He offered to give me some information if I eliminate one of his rivals for Garbage’s throne: Roosevelt, the head of the Commissary, or the Shah, the kingpin of the Brood. He hinted that the Shah has been dealing with Huron from the Slag Heap. As for Roosevelt, I should look for his former comrade Borodulin, who’s often found drinking in Garbage.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E03_MQ04_Descrip: Following Diode’s lead, I found Nestor’s personal notes and uncovered the entire Scanner operation. It’s clear to me now that Varan’s men were behind the attack on the kingpin’s couriers. Looks like it’s time to go to the Plant and ask the bandit a few unpleasant questions.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E03_MQ05_Descrip: This is interesting… Nestor, the kingpin of Garbage, has vanished without a trace. It seems like everyone involved in the Scanner scheme is in trouble. Even Diode, the kingpin’s technician henchman, is in some serious hot water. I should meet him at the Slag Heap and find out what he knows.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E03_MQ06_Descrip: Trusting Varan was a mistake. He was gonna screw me over all along, and his captive will never talk again. Nevertheless, I did uncover something useful after all: the captive had an unusual PDA that the bandits overlooked. I need to show it to Diode. As a tech, perhaps he can tell me who in the Zone might be using these things.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E03_SQ02_Descrip: Star’s men were looking around Nestor’s hideout when the Ward arrived, cutting off all escape routes. The stalkers found themselves trapped, along with the kingpin’s archive. To locate Nestor, I need to get to the Factory’s underground section – and I need to do it as quietly as possible.

Star’s men were looking around Nestor’s hideout when the Ward arrived, cutting off all escape routes. The stalkers found themselves trapped, along with the kingpin’s archive. To locate Nestor, I need to get to the Factory’s underground section – and I need to do it as quietly as possible.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E04_MQ01_Descrip: After a close encounter with Dr. Dalin and Scar, I managed to find out that the unusual PDA recovered from Varan’s prisoner is a device used years ago by a Monolith faction. The trail leads to Wild Island, the headquarters of Noontide – a group made up of former Monolithians. My attackers apparently have some ties to Noontide. I need to find a way there and have a serious talk with their leader.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E04_MQ02_Descrip: Strider is confident that Noontide played no part in the attacks – they’ve renounced their Monolithian past and embraced a new way. I’m inclined to believe him, especially since Strider has offered to help me intercept communications from the Monolith PDA to identify the perpetrators. I’ll have to activate Azimuth Station, which is currently occupied by the Ward, and replace the Inductor there. The Wardens should have the access keys for the station.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E04_SQ01_Descrip: Getting to Wild Island turned out to be far more difficult than I anticipated as the Noontiders are extremely suspicious of outsiders. The only way to get to the Island entails retrieving and delivering an important shipment, since the Noontiders assigned to transport it have gone missing.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E04_SQ02_Descrip: A Noontider called Kvashka inexplicably activated the antenna on the base’s rooftop and succumbed to psi influence. Prof. Lodochka wants me to shut it down and put the zombified Noontider out of his misery – he’s past saving now.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E05_MQ01_Descrip: Now I’m certain that Faust is responsible for orchestrating the attack against me. With the help of Strider, the leader of Noontide, I found out that the preacher has an ally within the Ward’s Camp Icarus. If I can interrogate this man, maybe I can discover Faust’s whereabouts and get my Scanner back.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E05_MQ02_Descrip: Shterev no longer needs Faust’s guidance, but I certainly do. I need to locate the ship he mentioned and find a guide who can show me the way to the Clear Sky Base. I don’t know what the blind zealot is up to, but I’m going to confront him and put an end to his schemes.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E05_MQ03_Descrip: Now that I’ve got Prof. Kalancha’s map, I’m ready to confront Faust and reclaim my Scanner. However, I first need to deactivate the psi-beacons in the Swamps to open the path to Clear Sky. It won’t be a walk in the park – some specialized equipment could come in handy.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E05_MQ04_Descrip: I’ve retrieved the Scanner, but Faust managed to get away again. I still don’t know what he’s after. Is it revenge? I should probably talk to Strider about this.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E05_MQ05_Descrip: Camp Icarus is a restricted facility, which means that Faust’s associate is affiliated with the Ward. I’m sure the men in charge of Icarus will help me root out the traitor in their midst.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E05_SQ01_Descrip: Batalov, the medic from Icarus, asked to find his runaway patients. Looks like their brains got seriously messed up, and the doctor wants to save them from experimental treatment. I need to track them down and wound them just enough for the doctor to invalid them out and send them to the Mainland.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E05_SQ03_Descrip: People are saying that some rare parts have been sighted in Zaton. Securing them would give me an opportunity to upgrade standard suits.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E05_SQ04_Descrip: Captain Senkevych believes that Khoteyev sells Ward equipment on the side. We should check this out. Senkevych wants me to take part in the transaction and find out who’s at the end buying the goods.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E06_MQ01_C01_Des: There’s been some kind of emergency at the Cryptobiology and Psi-Medicine Lab. I’ve got to figure out the cause and deal with it. If I don’t get this sorted out quickly, Dr. Dalin’s experiment and the testing of the Alpha artifact could be in jeopardy. I should check with Dr. Kryvenko, the scientist in charge of the lab, to get the lowdown on the situation.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E06_MQ01_C02_Des: Strider thinks that the Monolith has been transferred to SIRCAA – the same Monolith that stalkers used to call the Wish Granter. He’s concerned that those eggheads might try to activate it. I need to find out if he’s right about this.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E06_MQ01_Descrip: Now that I’ve got the Scanner and the artifact back, I’m relying on Dalin to come through. Hopefully that weird rock is worth something to him. More importantly, I’m about to find out the truth about my home and who’s behind it all. I’m sure I’ll find the answers at SIRCAA.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E06_MQ02_Descrip: Turns out Hermann was the one behind the mayhem at the Cryptobiology and Psi-Medicine Lab – the very same Hermann who led me into the Zone and gave me the Scanner. He’s alive, and this device is his invention. As for Dalin… it was his unbridled ambition that left me without a home. Well, now I know who’s gonna pay the price.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E06_MQ03_Descrip: Dalin’s experiment has gone horribly wrong. Instead of linking with the Generators and gaining control over the Zone, he’s unleashed a slew of new issues – including the re-emergence of Monolith. Hopefully Korshunov and Dalin can figure out how to clean this mess up, but that’s a problem for another day. My immediate concern is escaping from the ruins of SIRCAA.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E06_MQ04_Descrip: You were right all along, Strider! Dalin and his cronies are only good at one thing: destruction. Now their experiment has cost you your life, my friend. But maybe there’s still hope… First things first – I need to find a way out of this damned SIRCAA facility. Then I’ll figure out what to do next.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E07_MQ01_C02_Des: The scientists have detected a sudden spike in psi radiation at the Sphere. Colonel Korshunov wants to know what’s going on there. I need to get to the source and investigate it.
Prof. Lodochka has detected a sudden spike in psi radiation at the Sphere. I need to figure out what’s going on there.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E07_MQ01_Descrip: Monolith is back, awakened by some kind of signal. I’ve got to locate the source of this signal and find out what’s going on.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E07_MQ02_Descrip: The Signal seems to be originating from the Emitter. It’s hard to believe a device so small can bend people’s will so effectively. I need to find someone who knows what to do with it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E07_MQ03_Descrip: The fact that I found the Emitter on Wild Island didn’t surprise Scar at all. I don’t like that he’s keeping me in the dark, but he’s got a plan to prevent the Ward from destroying the Zone, and the Emitter will help make it happen.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E07_MQ05_Descrip:
Dalin suspects outside interference in his experiment. He kept talking about routers and security protocols, but the bottom line is that this whole debacle has rebooted the Monolith’s programming. So there we have it.
Korshunov plans to attack the Duga captured by the Monolithians. I need to rendezvous with Senkevych’s group. It’s time to gear up for the assault.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E07_MQ06_Descrip: Scar wanted me to connect the Emitter to some installation at the Promin CMD Factory. It’s done. All that’s left to do now is to strike at the Ward.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E07_SQ01_Descrip:
The Gaffer is concerned about the ongoing threat to Zalissya – their former guide Uncle Lyonya turned out to be a Monolithian. He led the squad that attacked Zalissya.
Since all of the Gaffer’s seasoned veterans are tied up, I’ve stepped forward to help. It’s time to confront Uncle Lyonya.
Even though Uncle Lyonya is dead and we've fought off another Monolith attack, Zalissya is still in danger.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E08_MQ01_Descrip: That freak Faust is full of surprises! The assault failed. We’ll have to find a way to get through those phantoms of his. Prof. Ozersky from Malachite might know something. I’d better talk to him.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E08_MQ03_Descrip: A mysterious professor collecting mutant collars and running his own moonshine operation... not too long ago, I wouldn’t have given Richter the time of day, but now it seems like he’s our only lead. If what Ozersky said about the Controller Project turns out to be true, this could be the key to neutralizing Faust.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E08_MQ04_Descrip: The Ward is ready to get even with Faust, and they’re counting on me to make it happen. I hope this much-vaunted Suppressor will deliver as promised, otherwise this entire mission will go down in history as a meticulously planned suicide rather than a reckoning for the Duga. But we’ve got no choice – the future of more than just the Zone is at stake.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E08_MQ05_Descrip: I’ve finally got an opportunity to go mano a mano with Faust. Whatever the Spark’s agenda is, Scar knows one thing: if Faust isn’t stopped now, the repercussions could extend far beyond the Zone. Besides, who in their right mind would willingly become one of these zombies? It’s time to make a move!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E08_SQ01_Descrip: It looks like Scherba’s pressing on with his research. He’s after some working collars, and he wants me to procure them. I wonder what he’s cooking up…
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E09_MQ01_Descrip: Faust has fallen, and the Wardens are thrilled. Sure, the victory came at a great cost, but they’ve avenged their comrades and the fiasco at the Duga while showing the Zone they’re still a force to be reckoned with. But I’ve got a nagging feeling that Faust’s legacy isn’t done with us yet, and it won’t be all sunshine and rainbows…

Faust is no more, and the Sparkers are free to pursue their own agenda. But what’s Scar’s next move? I’ve got a nagging feeling that Faust was something more than a mere nuisance, and his death will raise new questions – and cause plenty of trouble.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E09_MQ02_Descrip: To help my allies get to the Center of the Zone, I need Strelok. So far he’s the only man to not only reach the heart of the Zone, but also make it back in once piece. Rumor has it that the legendary stalker has recently resurfaced in the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E10_MQ01_Descrip: According to the Representative of C-Consciousness, eternal life exists in the Noosphere. Whether this is true or not, you can only find out for sure by reaching the Center of the Zone. So far, only Strelok has succeeded, so he must know the way. But to reach him, I first need to find another legend of the Zone – the Doctor. He was last seen in the Red Forest… I hope these are not just fairy tales.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E10_MQ02_Descrip: I found the Doctor. He’s preoccupied with saving Strider and won’t talk about Strelok until the Noontider is stable. Strider can be revived using a special device used by the Monolithians. I might be able to get one from the Monolith infirmary.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E10_SQ01_Descrip: Arkhyp Lichen believes there’s an unusual mutant in the forest. Not only has it scattered the local wildlife, but it also sent a group of Freedom members packing. A stalker called Gray tried to deal with the mutant, but disappeared without a trace. This job won’t be a walk in the park, but at least it gives me an opportunity to hunt some serious game.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E11_MQ01_Descrip: It turns out the Doctor is none other than Dr. Kaimanov, who was slated to enter the eighth pod alongside the other members of C-Consciousness, but backed out at the eleventh hour. He’s willing to help me test the Subtle Matter theory and get to the truth. To do this, I need to find the entrance to Lab X3 somewhere at the Cordon and retrieve the cartridge from the Signature Station.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E11_MQ02_Descrip: With the cartridge from X3 in my possession, I’m now heading to Orbita Station. Beneath it is the underground Laboratory X15, where Kaimanov once tried to establish a connection to the Noosphere. According to the Doctor, what I’ll find there could either prove or disprove the Representative’s claims about Subtle Matter. Although Kaimanov himself saw nothing resembling life in the Noosphere during his tenure in X15, the emergence of the Zone could have changed everything.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E11_MQ03_Descrip: Strelok has figured out how to pinpoint the location of the STALKER Program Control Center. Simply activating the neuroprogrammers in Lab X3 should do the trick. The problem is, the lab’s controlled by the Ward. Naturally, I’m the one who has to make it happen, not him.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E11_MQ04_Descrip: Seems like I’ve stumbled across some secrets the Ward would rather keep hidden. My run-in with Korshunov at the TCS ended with me getting knocked out, stripped of all my gear, and tossed into a cage. I doubt they’re keeping me alive out of the goodness of their hearts. I need to bust out before Korshunov comes back looking for answers – if he gets them, he won’t have any use for me.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E11_SQ01_Descrip: In exchange for the key to the cell, the Sparker told me where they stashed my stuff. It’s gonna be a tough job to get my gear back from right under the Wardens’ noses.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E11_SQ02_Descrip: Like many things in the Zone, the Oasis wasn’t what it seemed to be. I didn’t find the so-called “Klondike of Artifacts” there. Still, it might be a good idea to have a chat with Sidorovich. Dark’s beacon with the coordinates for the entrance to Lab X3 could fetch a pretty penny.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E12_MQ01_Descrip: Looks like the main route to Prypiat goes through Yaniv Station, which is controlled by the Corps. I’ll try going that way, and if they don’t let me through, I’ll track down a stalker called Spirit. He might be able to help me.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E14_MQ01_Descrip: I need to get to the STALKER Program Control Center. The facility can be accessed through the underground tunnels, but, according to Korshunov, only Degtyarev knows the coordinates for the entrance. It’s high time I paid him a visit.

I need to get to the STALKER Program Control Center. The facility can be accessed through the underground tunnels, but Scar says Degtyarev is the only one who knows the coordinates for the entrance. I guess it’s about time I tracked him down.

I need to get to the STALKER Program Control Center. The facility can be accessed through the underground tunnels, but, according to Strelok, only Degtyarev knows the coordinates for the entrance. I guess it’s about time I tracked him down.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E14_MQ02_Descrip: Now that I have the coordinates, all I have to do is get inside the Foundation control center. Once we’re done with Spark and Degtyarev, nothing will stop us from wiping the Zone off the face of the Earth.

Now that I have the coordinates, all I have to do is get inside the Foundation’s control center. Once I’m there, we’ll finally find out what’s needed to successfully complete the Shining plan – and cleanse the Zone of all darkness.
Now that I have the coordinates, all I have to do is get inside the Foundation control center. Once the Ward and Spark cease to be a problem, the Zone can finally be free.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E15_MQ01_Descrip: I’m about to venture into the very heart of the Zone, and the only path forward goes through the Dead Valley. My goal is within reach. I need to get to the Generators alive, at any cost, and restore the broken connection with the Foundation.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E15_MQ02_Descrip: I’m on the verge of reaching my goal. According to the Representative, the realization of the Shining plan requires a stable connection to the Noosphere. Now I need to navigate through the Dead Valley to reach the Generators and restore connection with the Foundation.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E15_MQ03_Descrip: The STALKER program is over. Strelok believes that this is not enough and we need to deal with everyone who has plans to use the Zone in their own interests. And it seems that Kaimanov is the last of them. I’ve got to talk to him.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E16_MQ01_Descrip: All bets are off. I’ve reached the Generators. Now it’s time to set up the teleport device in order to transfer Ward’s expedition squad, reach the X7 lab, and help Korshunov enter the Eighth Pod. The Zone will disappear, but I will get the promised new home in a new world where humanity can use the anomalous energy effectively and safely.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E16_MQ02_Descrip:
I made it. All I need to do now is take care of the teleport device, bring Spark’s expedition squad to the Generators, get to the X7 lab, and help Scar enter the Eighth Pod to initiate the Shining – eternal life in the Noosphere. 
I hope to finally find my bright and peaceful new home out there.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_E16_MQ03_Descrip: I managed to get into the Generators without crossing the Dead Valley. Now I just need to reach the X7 lab’s Eighth pod. The Zone is my new home, and my future is inextricably linked with her, but only the owner of the Heart of Chornobyl will change the fate of the Zone forever.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_EmissionQuest_De: Wait out the Emission in the shelter.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_IrizQuest_Descri: Helping Ashot to find a microscope. Don't know what he needs it for but at least I will make some money.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_JZ_Tutorial_EQ_J: This is the tutorial encounter journal aimed at learning the basic principles of scripting
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_RRQ_Description_: I’ve stirred up trouble with one of the factions in the Zone. It’s best to lay low until things settle down, then discuss terms with their leader.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_RSQ01_Descriptio: It sounds like an easy job – almost too easy, in fact. Still, Warlock seems trustworthy, and a few extra coupons can’t hurt.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_RSQ04_Descriptio: Boozer tossed a gig my way. I just hope he’s got the coupons to cover it. If I do it quick and clean, he won’t have much of a choice.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_RSQ05_Descriptio: Owl’s jobs often seem kinda sketchy – as does Owl himself. I figure it’s smart to keep our partnership under wraps just in case.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_RSQ06_Descriptio: Sidorovich doesn’t pretend to be noble, and that’s fine by me. The only healthy relationships in the Zone are based on fair pay for honest work.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_RSQ07_Descriptio: The source of Duty’s funding remains one of the Zone’s mysteries, but who am I to complain? Especially when some of their money ends up in my pocket in exchange for completing relatively simple tasks.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_RSQ08_Descriptio: The Barkeep’s been in the Zone for longer than most of the regulars who frequent his place. And if he’s managed to survive this long, he’s probably someone I can count on – as long as he doesn’t try to repay me with booze instead of coupons…
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_RSQ09_Descriptio: Needle seems kinda suspicious, but in the Zone, that’s par for the course – especially for a scientist. As long as he doesn’t try any crazy experiments on me and pays well, I’m fine with working with him.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_RSQ10_Descriptio: Harpy’s got a serious job lined up for me, but I’ve got to watch my step, especially around Prypiat. Here’s hoping the payoff is worth the trouble.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ01_Description: Warlock, the bartender over at Zalissya, wants me to do a bit of debt collecting for him. There’s a hothead called Valik Lummox who owes him money. He was last seen north of Zalissya near the Water Tower. If I can manage to squeeze the debt out of him, I’ll get twenty percent.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ02_Description: An Orthodox icon for the price of an artifact! Mityay, a stalker who used to live here before the disaster of ’86, wants to get his family heirloom back. He left it in an old root cellar somewhere in the Poppy Field. That place has a knack for putting folks to sleep, he says, so retrieving the icon won’t be easy.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ03_Description: Lens, the technician from Zalissya, asked me to search for a group of diggers led by Mastiff. He sent them to investigate some old stashes found in PDAs belonging to deceased stalkers. Lens is worried that the diggers might have been ambushed at one of these spots. He suggested starting the search for Mastiff and his team at the location of their last run.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ04_1_Descripti: I made a bet with a hunter known as Nightingale. We’re competing to hunt blind dogs near Zalissya. Whoever bags the most mutants gets all the coupons for the job.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ04_2_Descripti: Nightingale offered to split a hunting job with me. He wants me to collect all the collars from mutants in the Lesser Zone that he’s aware of. Hamster’s willing to buy any collars I can get my hands on. I can’t help but wonder if someone actually tried to tame those freaks…
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ05_Description: Huron’s lost a courier carrying an important shipment for the Brood – well, for their nutjob leader, the Shah. Huron doesn’t want any trouble with the kingpin, so he’s asking for help finding the missing goods.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ06_Description: I need to find an old Monolith gizmo to help start up a trading venture. Ideally, it should be operational.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ103_Descriptio: Diode asked me to bring him the Emitter from the X18 laboratory. Some scientist used to work on that Emitter, following Nestor's order. The project was called the Aggression Suppressor, and I do not like the name one bit.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ10_Description: In the Zone, a distress call is a sign of complete desperation. This Jumper at the waste processing station must be in dire straits if he’s broadcasting openly, risking being overheard by bandits or worse. I can’t let my guard down, though – a call for help like this could easily be a trap.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ13_mat_Descrip: The Warden guard at the Chemical Plant, Mateus, asked me to bring him an artifact from the Chemical Tanks. He said no one would match the pay he offers for it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ18_Description: Beard asked me for help. His men went into the Swamps and got ambushed. Vitko Nasal was the only one who made it back. He says the Sultan’s goons have taken the other guys captive. Looks like I’ll have to rescue them.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ20_Description: Rostok loves bread and circuses. The coveted title of Master of the Arena is on the line, along with respect and a fat reward. I might as well indulge the crowd, especially since their champ hasn’t faced much competition in quite some time.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ20_R1_Descript: To figure out the rules of the Arena, I’ve got to step into the ring for the first fight. For now, the odds are stacked against me.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ20_R2_Descript: My first Arena fight is done, and I clinched the win! Arnie even upgraded my status from “rotten piece of meat” to “ordinary piece of meat.” Not exactly a glowing review, but let’s see what he says after the next bout.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ20_R3_Descript: Things are heating up in the Arena. The mutants were just a warmup. Now Arnie’s ready to offer me a bigger challenge.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ20_R4_Descript: Looks like Arnie didn’t even expect me to make it this far. Now he’s dangling a real surprise in front of me. But the prize for winning is awfully enticing.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ20_R5_Descript: Well, I made it to the finals. It’s all or nothing now.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ25_Description: Cutting ties with certain friends is easier said than done, even when you’re aiming for a fresh start. But in the Zone, you don’t get to pick your pals – you stick with them till the bitter end, even if they’re dragging you down. I just hope Panas knew what he was getting himself into when he asked for their help.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ47_01_Descript: That scumbag Zakhar from the Slag Heap promised me a big score, but it was all just a ploy to set me and Akopyan up for a bandit ambush. Zakhar’s cronies got the drop on Akopyan, and now he’s out for blood — and looking to me for help to settle the score. Stirring this pot might not be the smartest move in the world, but letting Zakhar off the hook just feels wrong.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ47_Description: The bar over at the Slag Heap isn’t just for kicking back, it’s also a hotspot for finding gigs. Taking on a brief stint as a debt collector for Zakhar and his crew to score a share of the debtor’s cash? Sounds like a breeze! Having money and connections can make all the difference in the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ50_Description: The Sultan has given me a job. After the Emission, he found himself unable to reach one of his old stashes – the entire area is teeming with mutants and anomalies now. His goons can’t get anywhere near it, so he wants me to get to the stash and retrieve a briefcase for him. I can’t help but wonder what makes it so valuable…
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ81_Description: Sonya Kalyna hired me to take out both the Sultan and Beard. Their never-ending feud is dragging Zaton down, and neither of them can secure a better future for the Sultansk. At the moment, they’re gearing up for a showdown at the Harbor Cranes. Once they’re out of the picture, Kalina will take the helm of the Sultansk and put things back on track.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ86_Description: Mytryk Genius asked me to recover a gun he lost in the underground area beneath the Concrete Forest. Seems straightforward enough, but something doesn’t add up about the stalker’s tale. A weapon slipping from his grasp as if on its own, strange noises echoing in the dark… I gotta keep my eyes peeled when I go down there. There’s something creepy lurking underground, and I’d rather see it in my crosshairs than have it sneak up on me from behind.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ87_Description: I ran into a bunch of bandits in the midst of a confrontation that quickly escalated into a full-blown shootout. Then I stumbled across a nearby building with a group of loner captives inside. They’ve been locked up there for two days, deprived of food and water. Zhenya Hulk, one of the prisoners, said the key is on the gang leader Adik Pedal, AKA “the scumbag with scars all over his face.” I need to hurry if I want to rescue them.

Back at the Fish Farm, I found that all the captives except for Zhenya Hulk had starved to death. Zhenya himself is barely clinging to life – if I’m going to rescue him, the time is now. I need the key from Adik Pedal, AKA “the bandit with scars all over his face.”
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ88_Description: That Sledgehammer’s one tough SOB. First he interrogates me like I’m a suspect, then he dumps a tough job on my plate: track down some missing IPSF troops. They were set to trade artifacts with him, but vanished into thin air. Sledgehammer suspects some mysterious guitarist he’s been hearing playing around the neighborhood. If his theory holds up, I might need to silence the musician for good.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ89_Description: Sidorovich asked me to deal with a stalker called Wisp. This guy had the audacity to go behind Sidor’s back and reach out to his suppliers, even roping in some village loners without clearing it with Sidorovich first. Sidorovich isn’t one to let disrespect like this slide, so he’s willing to pay good money to make Wisp and any associates he might have disappear.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ90_Description: Barkeep offered me a serious job – to deal with the bandits holed up at the Container Warehouse in the Red Forest. They've become a real thorn in Freedom's side, and now there's a hefty reward on their heads. It's worth the risk, but I need to decide how to play it: go for a bold assault, or take them out quietly. Maybe I should start by looking for the Freedomers that Barkeep mentioned. I'll scout out the area around the base on the way.

Carl Clinch asked me to deal with the bandits holed up at the Containers in the Red Forest. His group tried to reach the bandit nest through an underground tunnel, only to get jumped along the way. Somebody must have ratted them out. The story sounds fishy, but the reward’s fat enough to make it worth the risk. Now do I sneak through the tunnel, or charge in guns blazing?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ91_Description: Duty’s bracing for another Monolith assault on the Cooling Towers. The odds aren’t pretty, but Major Rodetsky’s refusing to abandon the wounded or give up their position. If I want to lend a hand, there are critically injured soldiers on the second floor who urgently need medkits. And if I head up to the roof, there’s a sniper rifle and a panoramic view of the battlefield just waiting for me.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ92_Description: I ran into a Sparker called Mongoose who needs a hand activating two devices simultaneously for a science mission. They’re in different locations, and with the Ward base nearby, he’s willing to pay good money for my help. He claims it’s gonna be a walk in the park. The whole thing sounds fishy, but I’m inclined to give it a shot.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ93_Description: I didn’t expect to find a scientist standing behind the counter, but even in this capacity, Prof. Dorozhnyuk shows her commitment to Malachite’s cause. She asked me to find some stalkers who went missing while collecting research data, and I agreed to help. Her concern for others appears genuine, but even if she’s only helping those stalkers to resolve her issues with Ozersky, it’s still better than leaving them in the lurch.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_SQ94_Description: Saw Honta in Zaton – the guy started a hunting school, sharing his knowledge. Weirdly, it's free, and he's paying for mutant trophies. He seemed smart, and he accepts all students, even the less capable. I wonder if he can actually teach me something, or, as the Zone has taught me, if I should expect a catch?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_TEQ01_Descriptio: !!!ATTENTION!!! THAT'S A TEST QUEST. ALL THE ASSETS WILL BE DELETED BEFORE FEB.20, 2025. Khorundzhy asks Skif to find his friend Honta, who has decided to go to the ruins nearby to find the notes of Prof. Nesterenko.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_TST_Description_: Description Description Description Description Description Description
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_Test_EQ_NZolotov: Найти бандитов и отомстить. Они отправились в сторону старой вертолетной базы.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_Test_SQ_NZolotov: Разобраться с бандитами, которые напали на сталкера. Они должны быть где-то неподалеку в лесу.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_WhoLetPetyrOut_D: That is such a sweet building out there. What kind of adventures await you there?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_loopSSQ_bel_01_D: An ordinary day brought you a new acquaintance - a slightly confused Stalker, looting a dead body. He asked you to trade an Old Clock at a nearby meeting point, and out of the feeling of fellowship (or just a greed) you decided to help him. What could go wrong?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_supack_ANCQ_27_D: Received SOS signal. Someone named Kartaush is requesting immediate assistance. Worth investigating.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_supack_SQ100_Des: Banzai's equipment is not strong enough to record and decipher the whole transmission that's making people crazy. If I manage to find the right amplifier, the group will finally be able to solve this mystery.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_supack_SQ101_Des: I don't believe for a second that the bandit encounter at Volkhov was a coincidence. Someone from Kazkovyi ratted me out to Skull. I need to find the rat before the mercenaries figure out where the camp is.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_supack_SQ102_Des: Turns out Banzai ratted me out to the mercenaries to get their frequencies. He also turned the amplifier on, so now Skull knows where the camp is. Our only option now is his crazy plan: Medulin creates an interfering signal to protect us from the brain-frying transmission, Banzai transmits it to the mercenaries, while Scoutmaster and I defend the camp, hoping they can pull it off before we run out of ammunition.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_supack_SQ95_Desc: I found Banzai, the technician, captured by the bandits in the Old Mine. He says their group was attacked, and he doesn't know what happened to the others. He asked me to free him from the bandits and get his things back – Banzai refuses to run away without them. I wonder what could be so precious.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_supack_SQ96_C01_: I saved Banzai, the technician, from the bandits, but it turns out his troubles were far from over. There's a manhunt for him and three others: Rascal, Scoutmaster, and Medulin. Banzai asked me to get his tools so he could study some strange radio signal, and promised to tell me more if I bring them to him.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_supack_SQ96_C02_: To repair gear and equipment, Banzai from Kazkovyi camp needs calibrating tools. He gave me the coordinates to his colleague's stashes, and the tools should be in one of them.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_supack_SQ96_C03_: Banzai, the technician from Kazkovyi, needs precision tools, for more complex gear repairs. He's trying to prove himself useful after what he pulled. He gave me the coordinates to the stash in Boiler Room C-2. Hope there are no mysteries this time.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_supack_SQ96_Desc: Banzai has some work back at the hub, and he needs tools. He managed to locate a couple of radio beacons in the stashes that were made by someone who owes him from way back. Now I need to use the spectrum analyzer, find the stashes, and take whatever's inside.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_supack_SQ97_Desc: I brought the tools to Kazkovyi to give them to Banzai, like we agreed, and found his wounded friend Scoutmaster. While the two of us are waiting for Banzai, Scoutmaster asked me to help around the camp.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_supack_SQ98_99_D: Banzai and Scoutmaster told me they were part of a group of researchers. They were studying a strange radio frequency and got ambushed by bandits. Scoutmaster asked me to find the two other group members – Medulin, the scientist, and Rascal, the quartermaster. Maybe together they can figure out why they're being hunted down.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_supack_SQ98_Desc: I need to find the medic called Medulin, he's one of the researchers. According to Scoutmaster, he might be hiding in the railway depots of Malachite.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_journal_description_testquest_AL_Des: A strange melody drifting through the Zone at night. They say it pulls you in, won't let you go. I don't know what's out there yet, but something in that song... it's calling to me.
