ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_DLC01_hub_kurin_desc: Kurin is a Freedom camp where everyone is welcome! Even... Duty. It's where everyone has to drop their beef for the sake of surviving in the Iron Forest. Seriously, who cares who's right or wrong when all you have is a few bullets between you and a mutant pack?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_DLC01_hub_water_purificati: The single place within the entire CNPP where you can take a breather, get some decent sleep, and acquire something useful. Those lucky enough to reach this spot alive make sure they don't venture outside unless absolutely necessary.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_DLC01_loc_31_chiefs_bunker: A scientific bunker that was never delivered to its destination—the helicopter crashed with its cargo in the middle of the Iron Forest. But the bunker itself survived and became home to Chief, an eccentric hermit obsessed with learning about the Zone. He spends his days listening to the radio, catching scraps of stories from other people's radio broadcasts.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_advicespack_region_CNPP_ne: In the aftermath of the 1986 catastrophe, the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant garnered global attention, and the Second Disaster transformed it into the unreachable center of the Zone. Years ago, only the legendary stalker Strelok managed to make it to the station. But times change, and now people have a chance to take back what the Zone put out of reach.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_advicespack_region_iron_fo: Filled with anomalies, shattered pylons, and torn wires still humming with current from nowhere, the Iron Forest has lured many a curious stalker to certain death. Some are attracted by the enigma, others by the challenge, and others still by the promise of massive loot. Which means many more will pay the ultimate price to uncover its secrets.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_advicespack_region_sircaa_: SIRCAA has assembled the most brilliant minds seeking to uncover the Zone's mysteries for the betterment of humanity's future. But that which stands as a monument to the triumph of human intellect can also become a reminder of human error and hubris.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_archanomaly_wandering_ligh: A mysterious swamp anomaly that suppresses light sources.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_hub_asulym_desc: This is the base of Noontide, a group comprised of ex-Monolith soldiers who found new purpose under the leadership of Strider following the events of 2012. Given the general aversion towards former Monolithians in the rest of the Zone, this stronghold on Wild Island has truly become their shelter.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_hub_chemplant_desc: The Chemical Plant serves as the primary headquarters for the Ward. Accessible only with special passes or permission from a high-ranking officer, this area is off limits to outsiders. From this strategic location, the Ward seeks to assert control over the Zone and other factions.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_hub_concreteplant_desc: The Cement Factory functions as Duty’s command center. This is where they train new recruits, guard the passage to the Cooling Towers, and outfit groups assigned to clear the Zone of mutants.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_hub_enerhetyk_desc: A remote Corps ourtpost in Prypiat, the last little safe haven in the town the Monolith has returned to. No matter what comes next, the Corps will guard this place with their lives: surrendering it means giving up all of Prypiat.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_hub_ikar_desc: Occupying an abandoned Young Pioneer camp in the Swamps, Icarus is a Ward base originally established to safeguard SIRCAA from external threats. As SIRCAA implemented an independent security system of its own, Icarus gradually lost its strategic importance and fell into a state of visible decline.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_hub_malahit_desc: The Malachite Science and Technology Center was launched as a Zone research facility under the UNA, marking the next phase after field laboratories. After the establishment of SIRCAA, Malachite lost its former prominence, but gained increased autonomy and room for experiments, including those viewed as pseudoscientific by the international community.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_hub_rookievillage_desc: Once a haven for newcomers, this village has now fallen into disrepair. Despite its proximity to the Zone’s border and well-preserved buildings and basements, rookie stalkers opt for Zalissya nowadays. Nevertheless, Sidorovich, the local dealer in equipment and information, refuses to accept this state of affairs and remains determined to restore the Cordon to its former prominence.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_hub_rostok_desc: The Rostok Factory acts as Freedom’s central hub, embodying the most cherished dreams of all traders throughout the Zone. Here, the biggest deals are struck and the most fascinating curiosities change hands. Even a brief rest here is a delightful experience, for, apart from their trading expertise, Freedom members are renowned for their remarkable ability to enjoy themselves.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_hub_shevchenko_desc: The forlorn and deteriorating remains of a cargo ship that has miraculously withstood the ravages of Emissions. While the Shevchenko may provide a refuge to wait out inclement weather or pick up odd jobs, anything of importance in Zaton happens aboard the Sultansk.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_hub_sultansk_desc: Once known as the Skadovsk and now rechristened the Sultansk, this old cargo ship stands as a beacon for all those conducting business in the Swamps and Zaton. Regardless of whether bandits or Stalkers are at the helm, this vessel offers a place to rest and numerous work opportunities for everyone. Despite her name changes, she remains a fixture that will never sail away.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_hub_terricon_desc: Sheltered by a landfill on one side and a mound of industrial debris on the other, the Slag Heap stands as the sole neutral ground in Garbage. It attracts members from rival gangs, loners, and all manner of Zone inhabitants, including diggers scavenging for valuables amid the mountains of discarded technology, all converging here to rest and trade.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_hub_yanov_desc: This former train station is a gateway to the Boundary, a railcar barricade constructed by Degtyarev’s Corps to cut Prypiat off from the broader Zone to the south. It serves as a resting spot for stalkers willing to brave the deserted city.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_hub_zalesie_desc: Serving as the heart of the Lesser Zone, Zalissya offers plenty of residential buildings and bunkers that double as shelters against Emissions. It’s the prime location for newcomers to purchase weapons and equipment upon entering the Zone for the first time. Zalissya is the place from which rookies venture deeper into the Zone, while seasoned stalkers pass it on their way back home.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_loc_01_transformer_box_at_: Transformer Box at the Old Wall
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_loca1_desc: The Test Location is said to be a new, uncharted area within the Zone. No one has ever explored it and lived to tell the tale. Regardless, it’s no more substantial than other booze-fueled tall tales like the vanished city of Lymansk or the mythical Wish Granter.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_CNPP_desc: In the aftermath of the 1986 catastrophe, the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant garnered global attention, and the Second Disaster transformed it into the unreachable center of the Zone. Years ago, only the legendary stalker Strelok managed to make it to the station. But times change, and now people have a chance to take back what the Zone put out of reach.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_cement_factory_desc: Constructed to help deal with the aftermath of the first Chornobyl disaster, the Cement Factory and its surroundings now fall under the jurisdiction of Duty. Although its influence has diminished, the group remains steadfast in its struggle against the Zone and everything it begets.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_chemical_plant_desc: Formerly the headquarters of the renowned Spark group, the Chemical Plant is now the central hub of the Ward’s activities in the Zone. Korshunov has the entire area under control, and stalkers and bandits are a rare sight here nowadays, having been replaced by Warden patrols and the occasional Duty soldier.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_cooling_towers_desc: These cooling towers and new power units once embodied the promise of the third stage of the CNPP, a symbol of hope from a bygone era. Now, only echoes resonate within the lofty concrete evaporator towers. Instead of a new reactor, the rusty walls of the Red Fortress bear witness to the last war waged between the stalkers and Monolith.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_cordon_desc: In the past, all roads into the Zone passed through the Cordon. However, with most rookies now opting for Zalissya as their starting point, the Cordon has become a retreat for veterans who are stuck in the past. Although thoroughly explored by stalkers, the Cordon still harbors plenty of dark secrets yet to be uncovered.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_dead_valley_desc: The way to the Generators is blocked by the forbidding Dead Valley, a desolate expanse haunted by phantoms, constantly shrouded in an enduring grayness. The landscape is strewn with the remnants of destroyed equipment and the corpses of those who have dared to traverse it. Venturing here means signing your own death warrant.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_duga_desc: Persistent rumors about the old over-the-horizon radar station include stories of experiments on the population, bizarre radio interference, and brain-scorching radiation. Now that the route is no longer hindered by anomalous fields, certain daredevils frequently try to explore the enormous antenna. Their attempts are usually thwarted not by mysterious signals but by ordinary bullets fired by IPSF snipers. The military diligently guards the Duga, preventing anyone from discovering its purpose.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_garbage_desc: This old graveyard for radioactive equipment is a hotspot for diggers and bandits alike. Diggers sift through the mounds of discarded junk, hoping to uncover valuable parts and artifacts, while bandits exploit those fortunate enough to make a discovery.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_generators_desc: The original purpose of this facility remains shrouded in mystery, but the Generators have now become the beating heart of the Zone, unleashing devastating Emissions.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_industrial_zone_des: The Industrial Zone is teeming with production facilities, military installations, and old labs. This region is a prime destination for stalkers who eagerly delve into the abandoned buildings, scavenging for valuable parts and looking for stashes left by their peers.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_iron_forest_desc: Filled with anomalies, shattered pylons, and torn wires still humming with current from nowhere, the Iron Forest has lured many a curious stalker to certain death. Some are attracted by the enigma, others by the challenge, and others still by the promise of massive loot. Which means many more will pay the ultimate price to uncover its secrets.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_jupiter_desc: Being the entrance to Prypiat, the vicinity of Jupiter has always attracted stalkers. A labyrinth of stone walls and ruined roads leads to the now inaccessible plant. No one knows what the Zone decided to hide in it after the last Emmission, but individuals and even entire groups of stalkers, fueled by curiosity, are trying to get inside. To this day, they’ve still been unsuccessful .
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_lesser_zone_desc: Nestled on the outskirts of the Zone, the Lesser Zone is one of its quieter regions. It often serves as a starting point for rookies making their first forays into the Zone from Zalissya. The military tends to overlook their presence as long as the stalkers keep their distance.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_malachite_desc: The area around STC Malachite is the domain of scientists. Unlike their SIRCAA counterparts, who maintain no direct link to the Zone, Malachite scientists eagerly employ the services of stalkers, purchasing artifacts and enlisting their assistance in field experiments.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_orbita_desc: Peering through the recently-grown trees of the Burnt Forest reveals massive military structures and the remnants of deserted residential buildings. A lingering scent of burning perpetually hangs in the air.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_prypiat_desc: Renowned as one of the most perilous areas in the Zone, Prypiat remains under constant guard by the Corps for a reason: the abandoned city harbors a multitude of dangerous secrets. Yet, despite the immense danger, every real stalker dreams of braving the place and uncovering its mysteries.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_red_forest_desc: As radiation enveloped the Lymansk Nature Preserve, it gave rise to the Red Forest. Half of it is bathed in perpetual sunlight, while the other half is cloaked in fog and rain. Nevertheless, both halves of the dead forest are filled with deadly radiation and vicious mutants, making it an almost insurmountable obstacle on the journey to the center of the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_rostok_desc: Following the signing of the treaty, Freedom claimed the Rostok Factory as its headquarters. The factory’s workshops have evolved into a free trade zone, with the iconic 100 Rads Bar and Arena drawing in gamblers from all over the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_sircaa_desc: SIRCAA has assembled the most brilliant minds seeking to uncover the Zone's mysteries for the betterment of humanity's future. But that which stands as a monument to the triumph of human intellect can also become a reminder of human error and hubris.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_swamp_desc: This ominous, seemingly endless marsh rife with dangerous mutants and anomalies both frightens and attracts stalkers. Some dream of finding a new Klondike of Artifacts there, while others want to unravel the mystery of Clear Sky, a local group that vanished without a trace.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_wild_island_desc: In the center of the region stands a former toxic waste storage facility that is now claimed by Noontide. Lone stalkers avoid routes that go through the island – not because of its toxic fumes or radioactive water, but because of unsettling rumors surrounding its inhabitants.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_yanov_desc: Yaniv Railroad Station is a refuge for Degtyarev’s Corps, the protectors of the Boundary, a barricade of railcars blocking the way to Prypiat. The Corps tirelessly patrols the area, hunting and apprehending any stalkers who attempt to reach the Center of the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_yantar_desc: Standing on the shore of the lake, the Yantar Factory may appear scenic and tranquil. However, stalkers prefer to keep their distance, considering the place highly hazardous, with practically nothing of value left. Even the few scientists who were still keen on investigating the mysterious radiation at the factory eventually left the site, leaving only an empty bunker behind.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_region_zaton_desc: In its prime, Zaton was a bustling shipping center. After the disaster, the water receded, leaving ships and boats stranded on sandy shores to rust. Today, new businesses and arrangements have taken root, with the Sultan’s bandits and Beard’s stalkers vying for control of the area.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_skadovsk_desc: The Skadovsk, an old cargo ship grounded since 1986, is the unofficial hub of Zaton. Beard, her captain of sorts, makes sure there’s a spot for everyone aboard. The Skadovsk is the perfect place to take a breather, enjoy a drink, and gear up for the next adventure.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_supack_Kazkovy_Hub2_desc: The newest camp in the Zone. No one thought there would be madmen crazy enough to settle Kazkovyi, but so far, they're doing well.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_supack_Kazkovy_Hub_desc: Someone decided to seek shelter in a camp where several scientific teams have already disappeared. Not the best idea.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_locations_zone_desc: Since 2006, the Chornobyl Anomalous Zone has been a magnet for mystery lovers. Some see it as a fragile fairytale to preserve and safeguard, others — a living nightmare meant to be tamed or destroyed.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_01_desc: Following the treaty, Rostok fell into Freedom’s hands, becoming their stronghold and the Zone’s largest market. Whether you’re looking for relaxation, thrills, or trade, Rostok is the place to be.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_02_desc: If you’re going to be sneaking around, do it on a rainy day – it reduces visibility and muffles your footsteps. And another piece of advice: remember to turn that flashlight off, unlike some smartasses from my past...
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_03_desc: You can’t spot an artifact without a detector, no matter what other people might say. Invest in a top-notch detector for better loot. Don’t be stingy if you’re going on a serious run.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_04_desc: Every artifact comes with its own set of pros and cons. A seasoned stalker picks their artifacts wisely, ensuring that the positives outweigh the negatives. Be careful when experimenting, though. Or, at the very least, stay close to a medic.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_05_desc: Discovering an anomaly doesn’t guarantee that you’re going to find an artifact. The Zone is a capricious mistress – if you come up empty-handed in one anomaly, try your luck in the next one.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_06_desc: “Specific anomalies tend to cough up specific artifacts,” some know-it-all once said. He might have a point about the ordinary stuff, but what about the truly rare finds? You’ll only stumble across those if the Zone really loves you. No amount of scientific insight can help you there.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_07_desc: The better your armor, the more artifact slots you’ll have. Once you’re accustomed to the Zone, the first thing on your shopping list should be armor. It’ll shield you from bullets, and your artifacts won’t just gather dust in your backpack.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_08_desc: Putting random artifacts on your armor might make your life thrilling, but it’ll also make it ruefully short. Study each artifact, understand how their properties mesh, then incorporate them into your loadout.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_09_desc: You can’t pinpoint an artifact without a detector, but even with one, you might end up chasing your tail. Artifacts are crafty little swines – they won’t just drop into your lap. If it were that easy, everyone would be a stalker.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_10_desc: Artifacts come in all kinds of flavors. Some shield you from bullets, others from psi effects. Some might boost your strength, or even help you heal faster. But tread lightly around them, or no amount of anti-rads will save your ass.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_11_desc: Don’t offload all your artifacts – keep a few for yourself. Coupons won’t protect you from radiation or bullets, but artifacts just might.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_12_desc: You can actually hear artifacts if you listen closely enough. But take it from an old man – it’s more important to listen for a branch snapping under a bandit’s boot... or a mutant's foot.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_13_desc: There’s one rule everyone follows in the Zone: toss a bolt in there first, then make your move. Anomalies don’t discriminate – discharging into a piece of iron or ripping you apart, it’s all the same to them.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_14_desc: More and more stalkers are staying in Zalissya, and fewer at the Cordon. Can't say who's to blame – the new Perimeter, IPSF instead of the regular military, or that shameless Sidorovich. So if you're a greenhorn, head straight to Zalissya. Stay alive.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_15_desc: Lost your way in the Lesser Zone? Head to the balloon. It used to float over the CNPP Sarcophagus, but now it serves as a beacon for newbies. No one knows how it got dragged all the way to Zalissya, and if anyone does know, they aren't talking.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_16_desc: Korshunov came to the Zone and told everyone they either sign the D4 non-aggresion pact, or there'll be no one left to sign it. But don't think it's all rainbows and roses here. There may not be any big fights, but if you're with Freedom and wander off into Duty territory, you might go missing. Same the other way around.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_17_desc: We've been getting fewer mercenaries ever since the Ward came. Some even say Wardens forced them out of the Zone. But the ones left aren't getting any weaker or kinder: you get in their way - you get shot. If you see their colors, better stay away.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_18_desc: Clear Sky used to be a faction. Decent guys, I met some of them way back. But there aren't any left, word is, they all went to the Center of the Zone. So if anyone tries to talk crap about meeting them, don't fall for it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_19_desc: Noontiders are former Monolithians, building their new life on an island. Their boss, Strider, is a good guy. I still wouldn't get too close if I were you. What if they glitch again?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_20_desc: Hell knows who Monolithians were before. They used to pray to the Wish Granter and protect the Center of the Zone. Now they're not crazy anymore, they're living in the Zone like normal stalkers. So be extra careful around the weird ones – you never know which of them used to be a walking nightmare.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_21_desc: Spark are stalkers who used to only work for scientists. Their dream was to unveil the Zone's mysteries, until the Ward attacked them. Now they've got the biggest grudge against Wardens I've ever seen. Keep that in mind if you decide to work with Korshunov, and watch your back.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_22_desc: The Perimeter used to be guarded by the military. They've now sent the International Perimeter Security Force, or IPSF for short. Stay away from them, as they don't care which patch you wear. Loner, bandit, or Monolithian are all the same to them – intruders. You're just another target.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_23_desc: Freedom believes the Zone will make people better. Their version of 'better' is pretty unconventional, but they always have plenty of goods and coupons. If you need to buy or sell something in bulk, they're your guys.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_24_desc: Duty is trying to rid humanity of the Zone. Noble, of course, but the Zone is still here, and Duty… has seen better days. But don't push it. If you get too chummy with Freedom, they can still make your life difficult, even now.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_25_desc: The Zone has rules of its own. No wonder it attracts those in trouble with the law on the Mainland. There are about as many bandits here as mutants, so when you see them, shoot without thinking twice. 'Cos that's what they'll do.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_26_desc: Loners are the largest group here in the Zone – stalkers who haven't joined any of the factions, and only reporting to their conscience. Except not everybody has one, so think twice before making any deals. This is the Zone, and there's no such thing as friendship here.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_27_desc: If you need some kinda special gizmo, go to the scientists. We've got SIRCAA, STC Malachite, and even occasional loners, all hustling to neatly organize our miracles into their filing cabinets. But something tells me those cabinets ain't gonna hold up forever.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_28_desc: Help a guy out, and he'll probably tell his buddies about it. Same goes for hurting a guy. If you wanna stay under the radar, just keep on walking. And keep your finger off the trigger.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_29_desc: Life in the Zone is simple and straightforward. If you’ve botched your reputation or unintentionally taken someone out, keep some coupons handy… or be prepared to face off against the entire faction.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_30_desc: When an Emission hits, the worst thing you can do is get into a fight. All that matters is finding shelter and riding it out; everything else can wait. But don’t expect any help either – in these situations, it’s every man for himself.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_31_desc: The enemy of your enemy might not be your friend, but they might be a buddy of sorts. Kill someone, and their rivals might treat you better. Their friends, though… not so much.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_32_desc: If you’ve wrecked your reputation with a faction and have no intention of greasing the leader’s palms, gear up for war. Just don’t plan on surviving too long.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_33_desc: Pointing a gun at someone’s face is a bad call. At best, they might not get it. At worst, you’ll lose both your face and your gun.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_34_desc: PDAs are handy, but don’t forget to keep an eye on your surroundings. The world around you doesn’t stand still while you’re staring at a map.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_35_desc: Watch your step, and not just because of anomalies. Folks set traps near their stashes… or worse.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_36_desc: When the sky turns blood-red, bolt for the nearest shelter like your life’s on the line – ’cuz it is. An Emission spares no one, and there’s no escape out in the open.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_37_desc: Plenty of stalkers carry info about their stashes around just in case. So if you come across someone who won’t be needing his stuff anymore, give his body a once-over – if you ain’t too squeamish, of course.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_38_desc: You can’t cram everything you find in the Zone into a single suit. Just like with artifacts, pick your upgrades wisely. Otherwise you’ll be lugging around a ton of dead weight, and before long, you’ll wind up dead.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_39_desc: The Gilka may not be the most accurate detector, but it can sniff out an artifact on the other side of the Zone. Some say it makes artifact hunting even more exciting.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_40_desc: Capable technicians, the ones with the right set of skills, can both install and remove upgrades. However, some modifications are irreversible, no matter how hard you try. So think twice before taking a hacksaw to a gun barrel.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_41_desc: The Veles is the best detector out there. It’s not just about artifacts, though – it also sniffs out anomalies. So if you don’t want to end up in the wrong place after dark, get ready to fork over some serious cash.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_42_desc: A good technician is like a doctor – they’ve all got their specializations. If you want to add something unique, you’ll have to run around looking for a specialist.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_43_desc: You can track any location tag on your PDA, or even add your own markers. Don’t overdo it, though, or you might end up with a busted PDA… or a busted noggin.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_44_desc: Your compass doesn’t just display targets, it can also steer you toward folks who have already met their end. What you do with this information is your call, but the bandits are right about one thing: a dead stalker is as lucrative as a top-tier anomaly. So why let an opportunity go to waste?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_45_desc: You can always check your compass to see how much farther you have to go, but it doesn’t factor in obstacles. There’s no telling if you’ll need to take a detour around a hill, river, or the whole goddamn Slag Heap.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_46_desc: Some of the markers on your PDA point above or below you. When that happens, the compass will have an arrow next to the marker. If it points up, look up, and if it points down, look under your feet. And if it doesn’t point anywhere, just go straight ahead.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_47_desc: Radiation is more insidious than mutants and anomalies – mutants, you can spot, but radiation is invisible. So pay attention to your Geiger counter, have same anti-rad or vodka on hand, and keep an eye out, as lots of old radiation zones are marked with signs.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_48_desc: Bleeding isn’t “just a flesh wound” – it’s a serious, life-threatening condition. Remember to pack bandages and quality medkits.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_49_desc: Wild dashes, erratic jumps, and haphazard knife-waving might impress frightened rookies, but seasoned fighters know the importance of precision and restraint. They understand that conserving your energy is vital for survival.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_50_desc: To avoid becoming a mutant’s breakfast, make sure to grab a bite when you’re hungry. A starved stalker won’t last if he has to run, and the sound of your stomach growling can give away your position.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_51_desc: You know what kills folks more surely than any anomaly, mutant, or bandit? A backpack so crammed with loot that walking around with it becomes a struggle. Don’t get too greedy – stashes are there for a reason.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_52_desc: More than anything, mutants love sleepy stalkers – they’re so easy to catch! Make sure you always get enough sleep.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_53_desc: You gotta know your gun inside and out. The ammo it uses, its firing modes, compatible attachments – the whole megillah. You might forget your birthday, but always remember your gun’s caliber.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_54_desc: A real stalker has a steady hand, a cool head, and a spare mag. Once you’ve got that covered, the rest will follow.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_56_desc: Rumor has it that Strelok – THE Strelok – was spotted in the Zone again. The most desperate ones tried looking for him, and paid for it. Some lacked gear, others didn't have the skills, or simply ran out of luck. So unless you want to join them, prepare like never before.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_57_desc: I heard a story about that smartass who thought it was a good idea to toss a grenade at stashes tucked away in tricky spots. The loot stayed intact, but I’m willing to bet the mutants in the area appreciated the dinner bell.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_58_desc: Humans rely on sight, but mutants typically depend on smell. So don’t assume you’re the sharpest tool in the shed and the first guy to come up with the idea of sneaking past a pack of boars. Boars eat smartasses like that for breakfast.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_59_desc: In the old days, large packs of mutant rats were limited to the northern part of the Zone. However, their numbers have surged in recent years, and you can now run into them even in the areas that were previously considered “safe.”
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_60_desc: Normally, if you fall into a stupor in the middle of a fight, you’re toast. But when all sorts of debris starts flying around, the best move is to freeze. Stop, duck, and crawl away nice and slow. If luck’s on your side, you might just make it out in one piece.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_Loading_screen_61_desc: If you’re going on a hunt, make sure you’re packing the right piece. For dogs or Fleshes, a regular AK will do. If you’re after a boar or a deer, bring along a shotgun. And if you spot a chimera or a pseudogiant, ditch everything and run for it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_advicespack_Loading_screen_6: Cracked ribs can heal on their own, the same can't be said for your gear. So don't get greedy, and pay a visit to your local technicians for repairs. Make sure you're not left with nothing at the worst possible moment.

If you don't know the way or don't want to spend the whole day wandering around, go to the nearest big camp and find a guide. They know the safe routes, and will take you there in an instant. For a price, of course.

Keep different types of ammo on you. A smart stalker knows that expanding ammo is good for mutants, armor-piercing ammo against enemies in serious gear, and you can probably guess what the sniper ammo is for. Little things can be dealt with using regular ammo.

If your Geiger is crackling and you can't figure out why, check where you are first, then what you've got on you. Might be that you wandered into a contaminated area, or you messed something up with your artifacts.
Your gun always gets jammed at the worst moment. You can just reload and get on with if you like, but I'd run to the tech after the fight. If it got jammed once, it'll do it again.

Having all calibers of ammo on you at all times is not a bad idea, especially if you have a whole collection of guns. But don't forget that the more ammo you fit into your backpack, the less loot you can carry.
Came back an hour after the fight and all the loot from the bodies is gone already? You snooze, you lose applies in the Zone, too. Grab whatever you can right away, or forget about it.
Taking mutants apart is dirty work, but the money doesn't stink. So don't be squeamish cutting out the parts merchants are willing to pay for.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_advicespack_Loading_screen_7: An NVD can come in handy if you know how to use it. You'll be able to see like a Bayun when underground or during the night. Just make sure to stay away from flashlights or Electro. And don't use it in daylight, obviously.
Tip #70
If you bought yourself a brand new NVD, others can do the same. If you can see your enemies at night, they might be able to see you, too.
Tip #71

Mutants are still animals – changing lairs, and fighting for territory. So even if you're on a familiar route, best keep your head on a swivel. If a creek or a tree line was clear yesterday, today it might be filled with boars sniffing around or dogs howling.
Tip #72
It's a good thing the youngsters came up with those energy drinks to wake you up, just like that. Be careful, though, as if you double (or triple) down on them, they stop working.
Tip #73

If you see a zombie, shoot it immediately. Consider it a personal request since they used to be stalkers, like you and me. They used to want something, dream about something, and now the only thing they know is how to shoot whatever comes close.
Tip #74

An NVD might be useful, until you try to aim. Sure, you can try to do something about the laser or the collimator yourself, but it's better to ask a skilled technician to get your NVD and scope working together.
Tip #75

If you make it to the medic on your own, no worries, they'll patch you up. But after that, make sure to stock up on medkits and other stuff. You'll never know if you'll have long enough to get medical help next time… And one day, you might not.
Tip #76

Everyone's scared to carry artifacts at first because of the radiation. But I'll say this – the advantages are worth it. You'll be able to carry more loot, spend less on repairs, or recover from your injuries faster than a blind dog. Think it over, try it out, and maybe you'll find artifacts will become more than just goods to sell.
Tip #77
On one hand, helping the wounded seems like the right and noble thing to do. On the other hand, if you give someone a medkit today, they might shoot you in the back tomorrow. It's your call.
Tip #78
Sometimes, you'll have a lot of loot and not a lot of strength. To save having to decide what stuff to throw away, or just slowly dragging it all back, keep Hercules close.
Tip #79
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_advicespack_Loading_screen_8: Bleeding can be stopped with a bandage, and wounds are best treated with a Vinca. Without it, it'll take you a lot longer, and be a lot more painful.
Tip #80
Your knife is your best friend in the Zone. It can help you open a can of grub, cut a mutant, or take out a guard nice and quietly.
Tip #81
Anomalies don't care which patch you wear. If it goes off near you, it's not gonna be pretty – for you, your enemies, or your friends.
Tip #82
A grenade can solve a lot of your problems. Just don't forget you might be someone else's problem.
Tip #83

I've met my fair share of forest ambush pros who got killed on their first CQB mission. Seen it the other way around, too. A good stalker always knows that the same enemy can act differently in different settings.
Tip #84
Mainland gear only suffers from bullets. In the Zone, whenever you're hurt, your armor is also damaged.
Tip #85
Someone probably already told you that mutants can hear you. But you can hear them, too! So step slowly, listen closely, and you'll be able to get past them. Or catch them off guard.
Tip #86
Don't spend too much time around corpses. Mutants don't take too long to run to the smell of blood, so they might just save the corpse for dessert and have you for dinner instead.
Tip #87

Seen SIRCAA yet? I've no idea how the scientists managed to build that palace in the middle of the Zone. Word is, it's even better inside, just don't try to go in there uninvited. The Wardens are guarding it like really is a palace.
Tip #88
Malachite looks a lot more low-key than SIRCAA, but the scientists are a lot friendlier. If you're in the area, stop by. They can buy your goods, and maybe even give you a job or two.
Tip #89
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_lscreen_advicespack_Loading_screen_9: The Slag Heap has its own rules. Diggers comb through dumps, paying thugs for "protection", and the whole thing kinda just keeps spinning. Might look nasty, but let the Zone folks do as they do. Even if you're really itching to teach them a better way.

Even if you're totally exhausted, you can't sleep through an Emission. Scientists say it's your brain protecting itself from the damage. You won't be getting any sleep in the shelter, so stock up on energy drinks and tough it out.

Heard of the weird laboratories they keep finding in the Zone? Normally, I tell rookies not to fall for scary stories, but with this one, the reality's even worse than you think. Those are probably the scariest places of all.
Never step into deep water. If you need to get through shallow waters, stock up on vodka and antirads. You're more likely to find an Oasis than a puddle in the Zone that's not contaminated.
Guns are produced the same, people are made to be different. So if you feel uncomfortable aiming, get to a technician, and have the weapon tailored to your needs.
Need a specific attachment for a specific job, but can't install it on your own? Don't torture the weapon, and go to a technician. Maybe you'll be able to figure it out together.

Never trust an anomaly. Even the most familiar one can pull something so catastrophic they'll be scrubbing you off something on the other side of the Zone. Don't get me started on unfamiliar anomalies.
Binoculars are no "tourist accessory". A scope is good, but it's way more convenient to survey the grounds and watch your enemies with binoculars.
There's no shame in falling back. Your enemies know that, and so should you. Wounded pride is better than an unmarked grave.

ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_misc_custGame_diff_whatsNewPopUp_pat: Stalkers, welcome back to the Zone and to the newest changes in Update 1.7. Before we dive in – thank you so much for staying with us! A year ago, we began a new chapter in the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. series, which we continue to update and improve based on your comments, suggestions, and feedback. And there’s more to come, starting with Update 1.7!
Time to celebrate!

We’ve implemented numerous fixes and improvements to the A-Life system, so now factions can expand control over new territories. This means they may also lose control over their lands if they fail to defend them.
Even more A-Life Zone!

Various points of interest, checkpoints, locations (but not hubs) are in contest between different NPCs and… mutants! They also want to defend their lairs and territories from their very unfriendly stalker-neighbors. You can either jump into the fights or stay away.

We’ve introduced new difficulty level Master Difficulty to the game – a true challenge for the most experienced stalkers. Mutants and NPCs are much more deadly. A wrong step into an anomaly may kill. Radiation, hunger, sleepiness, and other effects can be extremely painful. Resources are low. Items are not as durable, and traders are not as economically friendly.
Master Difficulty & Expedition Mode

There are plenty of other adjustments for the hardcore enjoyers, but there is one more to mention – saves! Your progress will only be saved when exiting a Hub and within some Main Quest story moments. That's it. This is the peak stalker experience, of course, if you are strong enough!

As for Expedition Mode – this one is for those who don’t want to endure the struggles of Master Difficulty, but want to feel each trip is an Expedition. It has the same progress save system as in Master, but with the option to choose other difficulty levels.
Note: Both Master Difficulty and Expedition Mode require starting a new campaign. You can’t activate/deactivate those from the settings menu in the campaign.

With Update 1.7, enemies have real problems detecting you in tall grass or reeds, and are much less accurate when shooting through the bushes. Swamp shootouts will feel fair at last! You can now use the greenery to your full advantage, but be cautious – the closer you are to an enemy, the more likely you are to be spotted.
NPC Vision & Combat Update

Mutants and NPCs have also learned to retreat from the fight if they realize that chances for survival are low. They will also try to flank more actively, and choose a distance to fight from that best suits their weapon.
It’s also worth noting that NPC combat animation timings were slightly tweaked to make their movement more realistic. Oh, and mutants have also received new death animations!

We’ve completely redesigned the Equipment section in the Inventory. Firstly, we added protection stats. You’ll now be able to see exact info on how much protection you have from different Zone dangers. It calculates all the values from your armor, helmet, and artifacts, and also takes into consideration the equipment's wear and tear.
Inventory & Equipment Stats Update
Secondly – stats for artifacts and consumables. From now on, those have 5 levels of stats, with a more user-friendly interface for better understanding the pros and cons of using them.

And last but not least – the artifact radiation bar. This thing will help you understand whether you’ve balanced your artifacts well in terms of the radiation they produce. Keeping this bar level low will definitely help you to stay healthier.

With Update 1.7, we’ve reworked the stamina mechanic and added a new, ‘second sprint’ state to the movement system! We also reworked how energy drinks affect you. From now on, frequent consumption is not recommended, as it may result in tremors and shortness of breath, which leads to aim difficulties. Drink responsibly!
Run Skif, RUN!
The first one is pretty harmless, but looks very weird. It’s literally drops of water rising up to the sky from puddles on the ground.
New anomalies

The second anomaly can actually warm you in cold days and nights, but we don’t recommend using it in such a way because it’s too hot. Boiling hot, in fact! Test the new “Steam” anomaly with the bolt first.

From now on, you can lock to different enemies without re-targeting. Furthermore, you can now slightly correct your aim point on the locked enemy. As a nice bonus, you can set the time in seconds for how long you lock on to an enemy for.
Controller aim improvements

Introducing Immersive Mode, which allows you to quickly disable the entire HUD and change the FOV to a preset value so you can take beautiful screenshots or simply explore the Zone without distractions. It’s especially effective with the new Light Rainy weather scenario!
Even more updates in short format!

Another new thing – SD Cards with coupons on them in stashes. Think about those like digital wallets. Don’t want the headshot sound? Okay, then disable it. The navigation on the map in the PDA is also improved. Now, there’s an assist to select markers easily.
As a final touch, we’re also introducing DualSense support (via wire) for those who want to feel the Zone even more!
The extended version of the patch notes is available on our Steam page, while the complete version can be found on our website. Feel free to check them out to see all the changes!
And those are not all updates

Thank you very much for your ongoing support and feedback. With your help, the Zone is becoming a better place with each update. Please continue sharing your ideas and thoughts on our forums and socials, including those you have about Update 1.7. It helps us improve the game and deliver a better experience for all stalkers!
Update 1.7
Expedition

ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_misc_d1paritypack_saveLoad_popUp_sav:
You can show or hide advanced status info for your save files.

The point of no return status will display as either "Reached" or "Not reached".

The following statuses also show your access to The Cost of Hope DLC content:

- Locked – Content is locked because you have not yet reached the DLC starting point or have passed the point of no return.
- Story-gated – Content is partially accessible; progress further through the main story for full access.
- Unlocked – All DLC content is accessible.
- In progress – The Cost of Hope storyline has been started.
- Completed – The Cost of Hope storyline has been completed.

Save files that have reached the point of no return can still be used to revert to an earlier point in your playthrough. Selecting these files in the load menu will provide more details.

ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_misc_d1paritypack_whatsNewPopUp_patc: Places of horrific experiments on humanity and nature are spread across the Zone, sealed behind massive doors, or buried by the ashes of their own 'research' results. This time, there's a rumor across the Zone that Diode, a technician from Slag Heap, got access to the lower levels of the X18 lab!

Diode doesn’t care about loot, only about the one thing he really needs. It just so happens that Skif is now the man who can provide him with a pass to the lab, and a way to get richer. And what else do stalkers need besides a high risk, high reward gig with an air of mystery and the scent of secrets?

Besides, no one knows what's happening on the lower levels of X18. That’s on you to find out. Diode is paying well, and who knows, maybe by the end of it, you'll have your own reward – uncovered mysteries, things to use or sell, or even something for the Mainland.

This won’t be a walk in the park. We're talking about an X-lab, so make sure to prepare your gear and be ready to face the unknown. We obviously won't spoil what's awaiting you in there, but we can tell you this – your decisions will affect the outcome.

As always, enjoy this free new content update, and thanks for staying with the Zone! Your comments and suggestions help us make the game better. Please continue sharing your feedback, and see you in the Zone!

ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_misc_deadzone_stick_left_inner_desc:
Distance required to move the left stick of the controller for an action to occur in-game (e.g., character movement).
The lower the inner dead zone percentage, the more sensitive the stick becomes (i.e., less movement is needed to trigger an action).
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_misc_deadzone_stick_left_outer_desc:
Force required to move the left stick for the input to be considered at maximum.
The lower the value, the less you need to move the stick to reach the outer zone.
For example, a value of 0.9 means that once the stick is moved 90% of its full range, the input will be treated as maximum and won’t increase further.

ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_misc_deadzone_trigger_left_inner_des:

The higher the inner dead zone percentage, the harder you need to press the trigger to activate the action.

ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_misc_stationpack_deadzone_stick_left:
Distance required to move the left stick of the controller for an action to occur in-game (e.g., character movement).
The lower the inner deadzone percentage, the more sensitive the stick becomes (i.e., less movement is needed to trigger an action).

Force required to move the left stick for the input to be considered at maximum.
The lower the value, the less you need to move the stick to reach the outer zone.
For example, a value of 0.9 means that once the stick is moved 90% of its full range, the input will be treated as maximum and won’t increase further.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_misc_stationpack_deadzone_stick_righ:
Distance required to move the right stick of the controller for an action to occur in-game (e.g., camera movement).
The lower the inner deadzone percentage, the more sensitive the stick becomes (i.e., less movement is needed to trigger an action).

The force required to move the right stick for the input to be considered at maximum.
The lower the value, the less you need to move the stick to reach the outer zone.
For example, a value of 0.9 means that once the stick is moved 90% of its full range, the input will be treated as maximum and won’t increase further.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_misc_stationpack_deadzone_trigger_le:
Force required to press L2 for an action to occur in-game (i.e., for the button to respond to minimal input).
The higher the inner dead zone percentage, the harder you need to press the button to activate the action.

The force required to press the L2 for the input to be considered at maximum.
The lower the value, the less pressure is needed on the button to reach the outer zone.
For example, a value of 0.9 means that once the button is pressed 90% of its full range, the input will be treated as maximum and won’t increase further.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_misc_stationpack_deadzone_trigger_ri:
Force required to press the R2 for an action to occur in-game (i.e., for the button to respond to minimal input).
The higher the inner dead zone percentage, the harder you need to press the button to activate the action.

The force required to press the R2 for the input to be considered at maximum.
The lower the value, the less pressure is needed on the button to reach the outer zone.
For example, a value of 0.9 means that once the button is pressed 90% of its full range, the input will be treated as maximum and won’t increase further.

ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_misc_stationpack_motionAccCurve_DES:
Adjusts aim acceleration when moving the stick.
The response behavior depends on the selected mode:
- Off – Fixed speed with no acceleration.
- Linear – Direct response. Aim speed is proportional to stick deflection.
- Smooth – Ignores slight movements; requires more active input.
- Sharp – High input sensitivity. Any movement feels sharper and faster.

ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_misc_supack_whatsNewPopUp_patch18_pa: The Zone is constantly changing. Stalkers are always moving here and there, and as a result, some places can become populated enough to set up a campfire – or a whole new hub!
New place to take a breath!
With this free content update, the Zone greets new characters with their own personal stories, new locations, and items, and it’s all blended into a new journey for you to take part in.
Over five hours of gameplay have been added, depending on your pace. Discover the mysterious transmission that gives stalkers headaches, nose bleeds, and even hallucinations.
As the story unfolds, you can choose to help the stalkers and scientists figure out what’s going on. Make decisions, fight for what you believe in, search for answers, and more.

This is a story for you to uncover for yourself. It will be accessible after the early stages of the game. You can catch a PDA message anywhere on the map, with the biggest chance on your way to the Burnt Forest. Then, you’ll have to go to the Red Forest, and afterwards, well... spoilers, so that’s all we’re saying. As always, the Zone still wants to keep some things secret.
Why are you still reading this?
And, of course – thanks for staying with the Zone! Your comments and suggestions help us make the game better. Please continue sharing your feedback, and see you in the Zone!

ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_misc_whatsNewPopUp_CostOfHopeDLC_par: Our first major expansion — a new, non-linear journey into corners of the Zone that have stayed locked away for years. Dozens of hours of story, new ground to cover, new dangers to weather, and the first step of a bigger tale we're only starting to tell.

The fragile peace was never going to hold. With the D4 Treaty in tatters, the old feud between Duty and Freedom is burning again — Duty, who'd see the Zone contained before it costs us all; Freedom, who believe it's a gift too rare to lock away. 

You'll pick a side in a tangle of intrigue and half-truths, where no choice is clean or truly right. And you'll meet new and familiar faces along the way — Zulu, a veteran of Duty, and Mavka of Freedom — though whose word you trust is, as ever, up to you.

Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant, forbidden for decades, now calls to stalkers. Walk its reactor halls, cross the ground beneath it, explore its surrounding infrastructure, recreated in the tiniest details, and stand at the place the whole Zone was born from.

To reach it you'll have to cut your way through the Iron Forest — a dense, maze-like sprawl of steel and rust that doesn't give up its paths easily.
2 new regions — Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant and Iron Forest

The CNPP and the Iron Forest are only the headline. Revisit the magnificent SIRCAA, jump into the iconic X16 lab and other locations that are holding the unsolved mysteries and terrifying secrets. Lots of other locations for you to visit, but we obviously will not spoiler them. 

The Zone has opened up more than it has in a long time — plenty of never-before-seen places, together with the changed existing ones waiting for you to go looking.
And more of the Zone to find

New gear has found its way past the Perimeter, and you'll want them for what's waiting out there. Rare variations of proven weapons await those willing to explore every corner and listen to all the stories. A new detector will lead you to fresh artifacts, pulled from anomalies that won't give them up easily.

The deeper corners of the Zone keep their own kind of company. New mutated nightmares, freshly lethal anomalies with new artifacts as a reward for the brave ones, and human threats who'd sooner see you gone than share the road. The path through Cost of Hope is brutal and unforgiving — pack accordingly.

The S.T.A.L.K.E.R. saga gets a new chapter — and you're the one writing it. Your decisions shape not just how it ends, but the shape of the journey itself. One play through won't show you the whole truth. And where it goes from here is no small part up to you.

Cost of Hope is out now. If you own the Ultimate Edition or the Season Pass, it's already yours — just load in. To buy it separately, just click the button below! 

We also added an ability to jump straight to the DLC action for those who own it, if you want purely the Cost of Hope action. In addition to that, if you wish to continue with current campaign, and you've passed through the Point of No Return with no saves to jump back — we got you covered as well with an option to return just before the point of no return.

The Iron Forest and CNPP are open at last, and we couldn't be more glad you're here to walk through them. Thank you for staying with the Zone all this time — now go and discover the Cost of Hope for yourself.
If you are still reading this — thank you!
