ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ12_NoteFromDobrovolsky_hin: Found in one of the facilities at the Perimeter decontamination station
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ15_NoteRat_body:
$J0L0Vadya Profit: You rat.
Mytko Pear: Were you even there? No? Then shut your mouth!
Danya Izbach: You rat..
Mytko Pear: And you, stay the fuck outta it! We’ll handle this without you.
Timokha Bleach: You rat.
Vasyan Sniffy: You rat.
Borya Feint: You rat.
Mytko Pear: Guys, what the fuck? Guys?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ15_NoteRat_hint: Taken from a bandit killed near the Railway Bridge
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ16_AboutRoosevelt_body:
$J0L0Vadya Flyer: Nah, I’m sick of your crap.
Danylo Kepa: Oh yeah? And what’s that supposed to mean?
Vadya Flyer: You’re all actin’ like a pack of trained mutts, dancin’ to Roosevelt’s tune. He’s a fuckin’ cop, I’m tellin’ ya.
Danylo Kepa: Okay, I heard you.
Danylo Kepa: And when I come around to break your legs for flapping your gums, everyone else will hear you too.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ16_AboutRoosevelt_hint: Taken from a bandit killed near the Hydroelectric Station
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ17_AboutVaran_body:
$J0L0Vitya Bun: Hey there! How’s it going, Mr. Creepy-Crawly?
Roma Sipuha: Not great, man. Stay outta this place. Varan’s one mean son of a gun. Not as nuts as the Shah, but I’d rather not share a bunk with him. Went on a job with my buddy once and ran into an ambush. They were really laying it on, and my buddy started blabbering about Varan. They let us off, but sent Varan the tab.
Vitya Bun: Oh, fuck.
Roma Sipuha: Yeah. We made it back to the Plant, but Varan’s not one to let a debt slide. He hands me a piece and says, “Debts are meant to be paid.” Then he points at my buddy.
Vitya Bun: What’d you do?
Roma Sipuha: Shot him dead. What else could I do? If I hadn’t, that bastard would’ve had us both whacked, damn it! That’s how it goes, bro.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ17_AboutVaran_hint: From a PDA found in Varan’s camp
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ20_LostStalkerNote_body:
$J0L0Seryoha Siegmund: So? Did you get out?
Vovka Cottager: No. I didn’t.
Seryoha Siegmund: Why? What happened?
Vovka Cottager: It wouldn’t let me out.
Seryoha Siegmund: I see. Yeah, bro, there’s an entrance to the Zone, but there’s no exit. We just don’t belong anywhere anymore… not after what we’ve been through here.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ20_LostStalkerNote_hint: From a PDA found in a fishing cabin
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ20_LostStalkerNote_name: The Zone Never Lets Anyone Out
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ21_WaterNote_body:
$J0L0 The water here used to smell like diesel. There were so many ships. God, I hated that smell, and I know why.
It was my first day on the towboat when the XO found out I couldn’t swim after all. Well, what was I supposed to do? I’d never have gotten the job otherwise, so I had to lie. Anyway, he tossed me overboard, just like that. I kicked and thrashed and sputtered desperately, begging him for a lifeline, but he just stood there watching me. “You can lie your way onto a boat,” he told me. “But now it’s just you and the water. Let’s see how you lie your way out of this one.”
Now I look down and all I see is a dry riverbed. No water. Just me.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ21_WaterNote_hint: Diary from the destroyed Preobrazhensky Bridge
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ22_ClearSkyDiary_body:
$J0L0 We’re closing in on the objective of our expedition. The professor insists on proceeding slowly and cautiously… which is funny, considering that we’ve entrusted our lives to the first scumbag we met – some stalker who goes by “Scar.”
But I have to admit, I find him a lot more reliable than our professor, who’s been getting more and more erratic every day. He keeps repeating how absolutely sure he is that there won’t be any Emissions. Like we need any reassurance from him! I just hope he doesn’t drop his gun if we get attacked.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ23_AtasNote_body:
$J0L0Kolya Atas: If he changes the spot one more time, I’ll blow his fucking head off.
Seva Squirm: Hold on, guys.
Seva Squirm: Huh?
Seva Squirm: New coordinates. That Ward asshole just sent them.
Kolya Atas: Fuck!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ23_AtasNote_hint: Taken from a bandit killed at the Hydroelectric Station near Icarus
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ24_VenyaNotesText_body:
$J0L0 It’s done! You finished the job, and I’m grateful for that. I don’t think you’re ever going to read this, but I’m just writing it to get some closure. Although… we both knew you’d come find me one day. Am I right?
I’ve made my decision. I see no point in staying here. I mean, I did see a point – this whole business was the only point, the only incentive for me to go on. I have to write this down because I’m scared. It’s a terrifying thing, facing the end of your life. I always thought I could never muster up the nerve to… you know, pull the trigger.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ24_VenyaNotesText_hint: A letter found in a Prypiat apartment
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ_19_BanditDiary_body:
$J0L011th. My second week among the Brood. The Shah’s not as nuts as folks make him out to be. Sure, he flies off the handle sometimes, but that’s par for the course for a big shot.$J0L019th. There was a rumor this morning that Goon stashed some loot from the gang. That same night, the Shah had rounded us up at the Poisonous Hole. He grabbed Goon and dragged him to the vent. “Live like a rat, die like a rat,” he said, and shoved him in.
The anomaly turned Goon inside out, and the boss forced us all to look at the mess. Holy shit.

20th. I’m fucked. Found a gun in my stuff this morning. Looks like some scared shithead dumped it there after last night’s execution. I don’t know what to do. If I bail, they’ll think I snitched and find me. Gotta figure out how to get rid of it. Toss it in the swamp? Slip it into the group stash and play dumb? Fuck, fuck, fuck.$J0L023th Three nights straight, I get nightmares about the Shah. He takes the gun from my stash and shoots me in the chest. I fall to the ground, then I end up in the anomaly. It tears me apart while the Shah cackles. The rest of the guys are fed up with my screams waking ’em up at night. They’re eyeing me, I can feel it. Are they onto me?$J0L0Can’t sleep anymore. Yesterday, I buried the gun near the camp. And now they’re saying the Shah wants a word with me. Do they know? No, no, they ain’t gonna get me. I’m not going down like Goon. I’d rather do it myself.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANCQ_19_BanditDiary_hint: A bandit’s diary found in the Brood barracks
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_ANC_18_IOUNote_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault> I, Myshko Seagull, for the losses caused by my careless actions, hereby agree to compensate the group with: </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L1<NoteBody><ListItem><NoteDefault>One Rat King artifact</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>One flashlight</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>One Veles detector</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>One work jacket and its contents</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>Coupons for the pain and suffering endured by the group that had to rescue my ass.</NoteDefault></ListItem></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault> I pledge to refrain from any thoughtless behavior that not only prevents the group from finding new artifacts, but also results in the loss of previously acquired ones. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_BorodulinPDANote_body:
$J0L03/20 [20:55]
Roosevelt: I’ve got just the job for you, Colonel. I need to whip my new recruits into shape. Smart kids, but shitty shooters.
Borodulin: Training your rabble up to Duty standards? Not my cup of tea.
Roosevelt: Tea? More like vodka, huh?
Borodulin: Fuck off. I’m laying off the booze.
Roosevelt: We’ll see about that… $J0L03/26 [15:47]
Roosevelt: It’s a date, then? I’ve got an interesting piece to show you, by the way. Zulu brought it over from our old stash. Swing by the shooting range with my guys and check it out.
Borodulin: So Zulu’s riding high, huh? Don’t forget to remind him about that Rostok delivery. He’s only getting cozy at the Cement Factory because I chose not to spill the beans to the Ward or Voronin about what went down with his Freedom guards. You can shove your “interesting piece” where Zulu won’t enjoy it. Along with your goons. $J0L04/02 [17:20]
Borodulin: Sorry, got carried away for a moment there. All right, I’ll show your boys a couple of Duty moves.
Roosevelt: Deal. You’ve got the shooting range tomorrow. Just don’t leave a bunch of empty bottles there. We’ve got plenty of targets already.
Borodulin: I told you, I’m laying off the booze. $J0L04/04 [09:32]
Roosevelt: Borodulin, you bald sack of shit! What the hell did you do at the shooting range yesterday?! My medic had to yank bullets and glass out of my boys till his pliers snapped!
Borodulin: I told you, those clowns can’t hit the broad side of a barn.
Roosevelt: Clowns? You were sloshed! That’s it – no more allowance for you. You’ll spend it all on booze anyway.
Borodulin: Fuck you! Think you’re the next Voronin, huh? Still pretending to be a big shot in Duty? You’re nobody to him!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_BorodulinPDANote_hint: Chat with Roosevelt, the Commissary kingpin
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_Cemzavod_Note_Eger_Alensky_bod: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Jager: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>What's up with the newbies? The whole base is gossiping.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Alensky:</NoteBold><NoteDefault> I couldn't save them.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Jager: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>Shit! They went to take that bastard down, like real Duty. Back in the day, they would've gotten medals, postmortem, but still, and now they had to do it all hush-hush. Nowadays, Duty only awards cowardly dipshits who sit around with their traps shut.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Alensky: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>It is a real shame it was just the two of them. If there were more, they could've stood a chance.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Jager:</NoteBold><NoteDefault> And where do you think you can find a whole team of brave folks in this dump? I wish I'd known those guys were about to go there...</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_Cemzavod_Note_VoroninDecree_bo: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Having evaluated the situation with the special-class bloodsucker in the Cement Factory underground, I hereby order: isolate the location of the mutant, cut its food supply routes. Permission to eliminate is not granted. Utilizing the resource of experienced soldiers to take out a bloodsucker is irrational, if there is a possibility to eliminate it without risk. Failure to comply with this order, as well as vigilantism, will be reprimanded accordingly.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_Cemzavod_Note_Zulus_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>If you're going stir crazy sitting on your ass at the barracks and embarrassing Duty, we have something in common. I'm putting together a team of real fighters, who are ready to go to war against the Zone, because that's why we joined Duty.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_Cemzavod_Note_Zulus_hint: Found at the bar at the Duty base
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC00_KorshunovVartaNote_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteItalic>Korshunov:</NoteItalic><NoteDefault> Stay where you are, journalist. Don't do anything foolish, again. You have no idea what you are about to unleash.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteItalic>Korshunov:</NoteItalic><NoteDefault> If the information about the other Generators gets out, it will be a catastrophe. Worldwide riots and wars for Noosphere access would be just the beginning.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteItalic>Korshunov:</NoteItalic><NoteDefault> We cannot let that happen. So I strongly advise you to change your mind, I'll ask nicely this time.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteItalic>Korshunov: </NoteItalic><NoteDefault>I promise you, we will forget about all the damage you have done to the Institute. But this is your last chance to make it right, Veniamin. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC00_KorshunovVartaNote_hint: The last inbox messages on the Journalist's PDA
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC00_ScarSparkNote_body:
$J0L0Scar: Venia, Venia. Why do you have to run so fast?$J0L0Scar: I only had your best interest at heart... Have you forgotten who helped you get away from SIRCAA? $J0L0Scar: Tell me, journalist, why do you want to tell people this "truth" of yours so badly? $J0L0Scar: Why does it matter how many other Generators are hidden on the Mainland? Why do you care what the Regulatory Board will do with them?$J0L0Scar: We will be the first ones, Venia. The Shining Zone will begin here, and that is the only thing that matters.$J0L0Scar: Or is the truth more important to you than the happiness of all humanity?$J0L0
$J0L0
$J0L0
$J0L0
$J0L0
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC00_ScarSparkNote_hint: The last inbox messages on the Journalist's PDA
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC00_StrelokNote_body:
$J0L0Strelok: I've always liked you, Veniamin. I don't think you can comprehend what you are about to set in motion.$J0L0Strelok: If the public finds out about the other Generators, about what they are capable of, it will lead to a world war. $J0L0Strelok: Governments, international corporations - all of them will try to grab the Noosphere for themselves, with their dirty hands. There will be even more of those who want to take advantage of the Zone.

Strelok: I will not let that happen. She must be free. $J0L0Strelok: So, if you don't change your mind... You are pretty good at hiding, journalist, but this is my territory.$J0L0Strelok: I already know how to find you.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC00_StrelokNote_hint: The last inbox messages on the Journalist's PDA
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_CNPP_01_KhmelevNote: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Squads "Thunder", "North-2", and "Panther" – seize and secure the nuclear waste loading station. Fire support – sniper teams "Shadow-1" and "Shadow-2". </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Enemy headcount: around 90. Use of heavy weapons possible. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Upon securing positions, squad commanders shall immediately ensure ammunition delivery and report on losses. Enemy counter-attack: high probability. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>
From a PDA dating back to the Monolith operation
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_CNPP_02_StabbedNote: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Found an artifact on the crane. If it is what I think it is, I can chill at the base with a beer for a whole month!</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>My knee isn't too happy about it, though – doesn't wanna bend, even for this dope loot.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>So, no way I could've climbed the fucker myself, and had to ask Chop for help. He's a shady-ass dude, of course, but the rest are way worse. Offered him a third of whatever I make from it. He was happy to accept.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Writing this just so you know who's to blame if anything happens to me.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
PDA from a body near the CNPP crane
Notes of a stalker with a knife in his chest
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_CNPP_03_Bloodsucker:
$J0L0Skinny: We're here, with the loot. Open the gate.
Greek: I heard a roar. Did bloodsuckers follow you all the way here?
Skinny: Fuck, open up. We'll talk later.
Greek: Nah, not gonna fly. I'll open up when you deal with the bloodsuckers.
Found where a group of stalkers were killed
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_CNPP_04_LostRaiderN:
$J0L0Dimon Hide: Heard the news? The CNPP is open. Stalkers are all rushing in there.
District: So what?
Dimon Hide: They're all going in their fucking Sunday best. Top suits, guns, pockets full of artifacts.
District: No Zalissya chumps will go poking around the CNPP, and seasoned ones won't just pay up. They ain't easy to scare off, either.
Dimon Hide: If we can't scare them, we'll have the whole crowd to bring them down. Never seen a dead man refuse to pay up.
District: Good point… Boss know about this?
Dimon Hide: What does he care? We'll give him his cut. Come on, give the signal and gather the boys.
PDA from a body on the bridge near the CNPP
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_CNPP_05_Arik_Tuman_: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>There's this place southeast of the CNPP, like a car park, with all sorts of cars and buses abandoned there, rusting away. So I thought that it's not a bad place for a stash! If you don't know where it is, you'd have to turn every car upside down to find the goodies. If my ruck gets too heavy, I'll try to drop some stuff off there. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>
From the PDA of Yaryk Fog, zombified by the Flare
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_01_BuildersNote_: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>During the construction of concrete structures around the unsafe area, we have repelled three consecutive attacks. None of the attackers were human, all of them were eliminated. Casualties amount to 31 workers and 17 service members.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Requesting backup for the completion of the scheduled work and evacuation of the wounded.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
$J1L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Report on measures taken to control damage from the catastrophe</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
Document from the workers' room near the wall
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_02_CampfireNote_: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Stalker, some worldly wisdom for you: you can sometimes find more by sitting near a campfire than by running around.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_03_GeraNote_body:
$J0L0Hera Finch: Listen, wanna make some money? I remember that I owe you. The tip is good, cross my heart.
Tar: You know I'll make that heart stop beating if this is bullshit.
Hera Finch: So, there's this nutjob here, Chief, and he'll pay you to wander around with a recorder, climbing towers and stuff to record whatever. He'll give you a recorder, there's no risk, and he pays on time. I'm just telling you to pay off my debt, so don't tell anyone about this job.
Tar: If this job is so safe, you do it, then pay me back in coupons.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_03_GeraNote_hint: Found on Hera Finch's PDA in the Iron Forest
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_03_GeraNote_name: Chat about a job from Chief
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_04_BoryaNote_bod: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Thought I'd seen it all in the Zone, but never an anomaly like this one. I think I hear voices. I can barely make out words, but they're definitely words.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Yesterday, a voice said to me, "Over there, behind the rock!" I was surprised I was able to understand it! Nothing to lose, so thought I'd take a look. And there it was, a stash! The stuff inside wasn't trash, either – all IPSF issue. One hell of an anomaly!</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>It's quiet today. Strange. But the blasts keep coming.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>It's happening again today. They are all talking. It's so loud in my head… Why can I hear them? Sometimes they're kind, tipping me off about stashes, and sometimes they curse me. Who are they?</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Seems like it's the Zone, speaking in a myriad of voices. Hearing them is such a gift. I have to be grateful it chose me.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>It wards off the blasts. I could have died today… I think the Zone wants me to listen to it. I will, I promise.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>It said we should retreat! All of us! Deep into the forest!</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>We're here… It says we're here. There's something in the ground, under the roots. A gift from the Zone? It rewarded me! I will guard it with my life. IPSF never appreciated the Zone. It's angry at them.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Today, I will try even harder. For Her. Speak! Speak to me!</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_04_BoryaNote_hin: Found near the West part of the Iron Forest Wall
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_04_BoryaNote_nam: Abrupt notes with no dates or signatures
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_05_EastGateNote_:
$J0L0Captain Chaplyn: Unit No. 73 arrived at the east gate. No unauthorized visitors detected.
Major Zhvyr: Continue surveillance. And remember, captain: the east gate is under my specific supervision. Your predecessor turned that post into an open house for Myklukha's people when he abandoned it for some made-up reason. If I so much as catch wind of you making money off tourists, you'll be immediately court-martialed.
PDA from a mobile break room in the Iron Forest
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_06_WestGateNote_:
$J0L0[10:55] Pvt. Hross: Where are you?! We got no backup, and no ammo!
[11:29] Pvt. Hross: Fucking defector!$J0L0[09:21] Pvt. Hross: Don't know what to say.
[09:22] Pvt. Hross: Don't want this to be my last message to you.
[11:32] Pvt. Hross: Rest in peace. We put up a cross. Like you wanted.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_07_BlotNote_body:
$J0L0Valyk Bullet: Smudge, brother, here's the thing.
Valyk Bullet: The artifact your ass stole for the Iron Forest, it's, like, not meant for iron, get it?
Valyk Bullet: Not for radiation.
Valyk Bullet: It's like, for electro-anomalies.
Valyk Bullet: Capiche?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_08_LevcikNote_bo:
$J0L0Levchyk Boomstick: Listen up, Professor
Levchyk Boomstick: So…
Levchyk Boomstick: How do I say this…
Shcherba: Just go ahead and say it. You should also try formulating your thoughts before sending the message!
Levchyk Boomstick: Dear Assistant Professor Shcherba, I hereby inform you, though rather late, that the dog with the collar has disappeared in the spatial anomaly.
Shcherba: Then go after it, and bring it back!
Shcherba: Now!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_08_LevcikNote_hi: Found on a body near the Iron Forest warehouses
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_09_MercNote_body:
$J0L0Cherokee: Sprut, yesterday's blast breached an artificial lake. The way to our positions is flooded.
Cherokee: We need to change the patrol routes and possibly set up new positions.
Cherokee: Sprut?
Cherokee: Signal is unstable. I'll start mapping out the flood after eight, when it gets dark. Too crowded there now. Expect the map with the locations highlighted before midnight.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_09_MercNote_hint: From a body in the Iron Forest
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_10_OldNote_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Hello, Halya!</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Thank you for your letter. I've been so busy with work that I didn't even notice how April flew by – and that's the best time of year. The migrating birds are coming back from spending winter in warmer places, and will soon start nesting. Do you remember how pleasant it was last spring when we went hiking? You said that next time we go, you'll recognize more birds than I, just by their songs.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I'm afraid your triumph will be achieved too easily, as I can't deny that I've lost my touch! Can't say for sure when the last time I went outside to listen to the sounds of nature was. We spend all our time working inside. But will you allow me to take you up on that offer and invite you on a hike when I get back? Only a week left until we see each other again, and I can't wait. I've been waiting for quite a long time to tell you something.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Best wishes, Serhii.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ANCQ_IF_10_OldNote_hint: Letter found in the substation workshop
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_CNPP_Hub_Duty_Note1_body:
$J0L0Sgt. Hurza: Lt. Vira. Report on the order.$J0L0Lt. Vira: Hi. Well, listen…uh, something came up.$J0L0Sgt. Hurza: Where's my hardware?

Lt. Vira: Where it should be. Well, almost. Everything's at the CNPP. In different stashes.$J0L0Sgt. Hurza: What stashes? You were supposed to bring it to me!

Lt. Vira: Sorry, I'm not going back there. That Flare almost got our brains fried last time.$J0L0Sgt. Hurza: What did I pay my coupons for, then? Are you suggesting I run to the Flare to get my own damned order? What happened?

Lt. Vira: An Emission happened. Got us on the way back. We wouldn't have made it to cover carrying it all, so we had to drop it somewhere. Barely crawled outta there, and didn't even get the chance to geotag it.$J0L0Sgt. Hurza: Not my damn problem. You took the order, and didn't see it through.

Lt. Vira: Let's agree on half. I'll send you the approximate coordinates. Go there, look in the bushes, and you'll find it.$J0L0Sgt. Hurza: Approximate coordinates of some bushes for half the price? No thanks. You can keep it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_CNPP_Hub_Duty_Note1_hint: PDA found at the Duty base at the CNPP
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_CNPP_Hub_Duty_Note1_name: Lt. Vira's chat with Sgt. Hurza
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_CNPP_Hub_Duty_Note2_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>No one wants to go back for Sgt. Hurza's hardware, and we barely made it out alive. Here's the list of stashes:</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L2<NoteBody><ListItem><NoteDefault>Boiler House pipe.</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>Wagon by the crane.</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>Behind the big tree near the generators.</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>Storage tank covered in grape vines.</NoteDefault></ListItem></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_CNPP_Hub_Duty_Note2_hint: PDA found at the Duty base at the CNPP
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_CNPP_Hub_Duty_Note2_name: Message to Lt. Vira from Pvt. Zinchenko
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_CNPP_Hub_Duty_PaperNote_: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>It happened in Kopachi – a village near the CNPP. I was born and raised there. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I was 13, a noise outside woke me up. I could see the neighbors' house burning. I rushed outside and, just like that, jumped right into the burning building to get the people out. I was running around, shouting, but there was no one inside! And I couldn't find the way out – everything was covered in smoke. I started suffocating, coughing. Then, someone's hand grabbed me by the wrist and dragged me somewhere. I woke up lying in the snow. Yana, my neighbor, was standing next to me. So pretty! She said, "Where did you think you were going, you silly boy?" </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I don't even know why I'm writing this. But I got into some trouble in the swamps: I was drowning in the bog. Everything went dark, sludge in my mouth. And at the last moment, someone's hand grabbed me by the wrist and dragged me somewhere. I opened my eyes, and saw Horchak – the guy I showed the route to! And he said to me, "Where did you think you were going, you silly boy?" </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>This is how the Zone destroys everything. Even the happiest memories.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_CNPP_Hub_Freedom_Note1_b: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Thanks for the spares you brought me. As promised – paying in stashes! To be extra careful, I'll describe the places in riddles so no one gets to them other than you!</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L2<NoteBody><ListItem><NoteDefault>This thing used to be smoking hot, like a Freedom squad on a smoking break. The stash is right on top of it.</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>This used to carry heavy stuff with a guy in a steel booth up top. The stash is in the little wagon near it.</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>Way back, this could give you quite a shock! An electric one. The stash is behind the wooden giant.</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>A huge rusty thing, covered with something you could make real wine from (probably). The stash is right next to it.</NoteDefault></ListItem></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_CNPP_Hub_Freedom_Note1_h: PDA found at the Freedom base in the CNPP
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_CNPP_Hub_Freedom_Note2_b: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Bonespike: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>We did our part, and now we'd like to celebrate. A small party would do everyone at the CNPP some good. Doctor's orders! But we need additional supplies for that. Can you help?</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Arnie: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>Why can't Zen ask me himself? I'm not mad at him anymore for recommending that Mavka put me in charge of Rostok. Well, not much.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Bonespike: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>Come on over, and ask him in person. I bet he'd be happy to see you. Plus, you'll get to see how he's running things.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Arnie: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>First, he should come over to Rostok and see how I've been running things. I'll send whatever you need. Say hi to Zen for me.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_CNPP_Hub_Freedom_Note3_b: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Mavka: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>I left you in charge and took off. Sorry it had to be this way. I hope you understand. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Zen: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>I made my choice. A wise person once told me to "Chill out!"</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_CNPP_Hub_Freedom_Note3_h: Freedom leader's PDA found at the CNPP
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_CNPP_Hub_Freedom_Note4_b: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Take 1: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>What do a bandit and a blind dog have in common? Both attack whatever's moving.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteItalic>Note: No. Boring. Not funny at all.</NoteItalic></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Take 2: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>They say, no one likes bandits. But not everybody knows boars love them! Just in a different way!</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteItalic>Note: Not clear enough. What different way? Stupid. Joke needs reworking.</NoteItalic></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Take 3: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>Everybody knows that a bandit in the bushes is an omen – it means blood loss. But not everybody knows that a bloodsucker in the bushes means bandit loss!</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteItalic>Note: What a clever pun. Did I really come up with that all by myself? I'll test this joke on my next client.</NoteItalic></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ContractPDANote_body:
$J0L0Contract: What happens when we destroy the Perimeter?
Nord: It'll all be over. We'll leave the Zone, and no more missions.
Contract: Can't believe you'll really do this, Commander.
Nord: Not just me. All of us.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_DLC01_CNPP_Map_Note_hint: A worn hand-drawn map of the CNPP, schematic but precise. It marks several Monolith depots, one of them has a brief note next to it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_DLC01_CNPP_Map_Note_name: Map of CNPP with Monolith stashes
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_Doctors_PDANote_body:
$J0L0Doctor Slavenko: Khutynych, I need fresh specimens. Urgently. The procedure requires us to continue.
Assistant Khutynych: The deliveries are late.
Doctor Slavenko: Then bring me the ones from the floor below. They're waste anyway.
Assistant Khutynych: I don't know if they'll make it.
Doctor Slavenko: Can't see any other options, then. Get the test subjects.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_Doctors_PDANote_name: Doctor Slavenko's chat with assistant Khutynych
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_EQ02_LajkoPDANote_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Nitro, I can't reach the junkyard – the fucking chimera is holed up there. Looks like the same one that beat up Zulu. It tore Belyakov to pieces, now I'm all alone here. Can't get the crunching sound out of my head, when it… That fucker's following me all the time! It's like it wants me to know it's right behind me, and not finishing me off just yet. I'll get a grip, move further away from Kurin, then try to lose the damn thing. Can't let it find our camp. Remember me, and… don't try to take revenge, all right? Don't let my sacrifice be for nothing.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_EQ03_TohaLastNote_body:
$J0L0Tokha Mole: I eavesdropped on our employers. I know where they left some goodies for the diggers.
Vetal Sot: So what? They got codes everywhere.
Tokha Mole:I'm not stupid, they talked about the code, too. You just need to listen and keep your eyes peeled when you're there.
Vetal Sot: Better stay away. They got eyes on the whole Iron Forest. Those goodies aren't meant for us.
Tokha Mole: And what's meant for us? A handful of coupons and stale bread? Plus, those diggers are dead anyway. Whoever claims their work first will get paid.

Tokha Mole: Vetal, the fucking IPSF shot me. Shit! I won't make it. Take the loot, so I don't fucking die for nothing.
Tokha Mole: Alpha. Tango. Delta. Victor.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_EQ03_TohaLastNote_hint: Found on a dead body in a Kurin basement
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_EQ05_LotosPDA_Note_body:
$J0L0Lyova Root: Dude, I heard you were looking for a way to make coupons. Wanna join me on a job?
Kostya Lotus: What kind of job?
Lyova Root: There's this base where we can nick some documents from Duty armories. We'll get in when the uniforms are changing shifts. I'll distract the guards, you'll get the papers.
Kostya Lotus: Sounds easy. I'm in, amigo!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ElhantNote_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Looking for the container missing from the SIRCAA lab? Don’t waste your time, it’s already been found. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>But don’t you despair! You’ve found this old tree, and that’s way more valuable. It’s seen many an annihilated empire in it’s long life, and nothing could stop it from growing. But radiation. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>You know that elves hide treasures in trees, don’t you? I hid one too. And you found it. Maybe, you’ve got elven blood in you? </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Anyway, take it all, you’ve earned it. And I’m going back to my peninsula, with more trees and fewer curious stalkers. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_ElhantNote_hint: What kind of elf wrote this note?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_FujiPDANote_body:
$J0L0[10:47] Angel: I think Fire's losing it. Always on and on about his future on the Mainland. Rambling about his dream country house.
[10:53] Fuji: Is there a better time to make plans? So far, we've been working here with hardly any sleep or rest. But it's almost over now.
[10:54] Angel: Like you don't know what's gonna come next.
[10:56] Fuji: All the more reason to dream on.

[11:30] Angel: You know what? A country house sounds nice. I'll get myself one twice as big as Fire's. Just to mess with him.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_IronForest_Hub_Note_Kefi: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Wassup, gents! I clearly remember having a bag of candy here not long ago. So where's it at? No pointing the finger at Duty, neither – they didn't know it was here. I know it was one you as I can feel the knife in my back! So, do me a solid and come forward, yo? Or I'll make you regret it.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_IronForest_Hub_Note_Voro: Boilerplate Duty document with a note
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ02_MavkaNote_body:
$J0L0Forest Elf
My child, I hold you not.
The Water Goblin, in his bogs so thick, is used to sucking up all living things.
While I respect your freedom.
Play with the wind, joke with the Will-o'-the-Wisp, and, if you desire, draw the force of the forest – that of the water and the rocks – all to yourself.
But step not on human trails, my child. No freedom can be found there, only woes to burden you.
Away from them you stay, my daughter! Take this one step – and there your freedom goes!
Mavka (laughing)
But that can't be, for freedom to be gone.
The wind cannot disappear!
Think about it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ02_MavkaNote_hint: Page from a book of poems with a message
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ02_STOAntenna_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>As I mentioned earlier in my explanatory note attached to the proposal to cancel the field mission, the fact that the signal of our antennas cannot ensure stable psi emission outside the actual CNPP territory is obvious, and does not require additional confirmation. My colleagues and I are currently gathering data from the antennas. Not to prove their inability to function in the Iron Forest, but to prove the incompetence of the persons responsible for making decisions on the necessity of field missions in cases where they are not necessary at all.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteStrike>As if my laboratory research was not enough, we just had to be dragged all the way here… fucking Scorcher… We will zombify ourselves if we keep going like this…</NoteStrike></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ02_STOAntenna_hint: Page from a field log found at the Vehicle Workshop
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ03_TestingWorkshop_Not:
$J0L0Date: 11.16
Shift: А (Doctor Klopotenko in charge)
Subject: 62-М modification testing. Installation of the EM-amplification module.
Testing process: Conducted a series of tests on power augmentation of Model 62. Standard energy modules have been replaced with experimental modules, connected through an upgraded power distribution chip. Test shots were fired with the modified version of Model 62-M.
Conclusion: The device is severely unstable. Firing the third round led to a powerful EM-emission, which caused a failure in all electronic devices within the testing area.$J0L0
Achieving the requested objectives within the expected timeframe is not possible. We strongly advise listening to reason and focusing the team's efforts on upgrading the fuses for the new model. We are already working beyond our limits, and the next test may turn into a real tragedy.
What's left from Project X times

$J0L0Hardware: Assembly is complete, no abnormalities detected$J0L0Power system: Indicators normal$J0L0Biological element: ABSENT$J0L0
Comment: All hardware nodes are functioning properly, the power supply is stable, the software system is activated, but the key biological element is absent, which excludes the possibility of utilizing the technology.$J0L0
Solution: Operations on hold. Project suspended until the biological component is received.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ04_ArchiveNote_Note_bo:
$J0L0We are paying extra attention to the Bubble anomaly in the experiments that involve teleportation.$J0L0So far, we have not been able to conduct a controlled transportation of living or non-living specimens into the anomaly. However, Major Degtyarev's experience of interacting with the Bubble proves that entering and exiting the anomaly is possible.$J0L0Access stability remains an important factor. According to the natural hypothesis, this can be achieved by ensuring a specific, as of yet undefined combination of artifacts.

The technogenic approach to opening the Bubble is considered operational by using the Svarog detector. It was used by Major Degtyarev, and allowed him to discover the bodies of Tachenko's squad and the body of Duty's founder himself, who had been considered missing.

We are currently looking for ways to strengthen the detector's mechanism, and allow longer access to the Bubble within the framework of field research.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ04_ArchiveNote_Note_hi: Document found in the SIRCAA archive.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ04_ArchiveNotepad_Note: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Due to the finalization of valuation activities and inventory in archive room No. 2, I hereby order:</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L2<NoteBody><ListItem><NoteDefault>Assembly of a working group, led by Y. I. Zelenyi, to digitalize the documentation, prioritizing section 3A.</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>Preparation of digitalized documentation for long-term storage.</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>Storage of the digitalized data on encrypted information storage devices, type Kyiv</NoteDefault></ListItem></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Upon completion of all listed tasks, report directly to me.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>To: Information Storage Office Director, O.S. Kolomoyets</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ04_ArtFarmNote_Note_bo:
$J0L0So, dear dudes, spelling it out for ya – this manual is based on sweat and blood. I pretty much wanted to jump off this centrifuge myself a couple of times:

1. To start the damn blades, turn on all levers near their base. Look for the little steel shitsticks with the red handles. You can do it, I believe in you.

2. The damned anomalies are getting in the way of the electric current. Fuck knows how it all works. To make them disappear for a short while, you need to discharge more than one of them. I'd draw a diagram, but I'm not an artist.

3. When the levers are on, the anomalies are discharged, and it's all peachy. Then you can go down. Activate the control panel, and off you go.

Break a leg!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ04_ArtFarmNote_Note_he: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Why isn't this piece of shit working?</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ04_ArtFarmNote_Note_hi: Found on a wall in the centrifuge room
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_BrockenMercPDANote_:
$J0L0[10:43] Bosch: We got a situation. Basalt and Mirage are gone.
[10:43] Nord: How?
[10:44] Bosch: The fog. They stepped into it and went off comms. No screaming, no interference, nothing. We can't find them.
[10:47] Nord: Is your group all right?
[10:47] Bosch: Waiting for orders.
[10:48] Nord: Avoid the fog, and keep searching for the target. I'll let the others know.
[10:49] Bosch: Roger. My PDA's dead, so we'll communicate through Celt.
Found next to one of Nord's dead mercenaries
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_BunchukDeathNote_bo: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteItalic>I can't take it anymore. I see him every night – Kosmach standing on the verge of light, just… staring. Without a word. Just a dead, blank stare. He's not a ghost, either, he's too real. The headaches are getting stronger as the anomaly plays with my sense of guilt, with my fears. I betrayed him. I sent him to his death. I thought I was doing the right thing, following orders and my sense of duty, but… I was wrong.</NoteItalic></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_BunchukDeathNote_hi: Found on the body of Bunchuk, who hanged himself.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_BunchukPDANote_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Day 7.</NoteBold><NoteDefault> The incident with Colonel Kosmach. He came to me with a sabotage proposal. As per regulation, I reported to the commander. The general made a decision to eliminate, and executed it personally. Major Chepurny defected that the same night. It seems the general is losing his mind.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Day 9?</NoteBold><NoteDefault> Kosmach, you were right. About everything. You came to me as a friend and shared your plan… but I was scared. Not scared of the general, scared of disobeying orders – those same damn orders that make up every fiber of my being. I thought I was doing the right thing, as a soldier should. Instead, I signed your death sentence. Now you're dead. Chepurny ran on the same night because he was smart enough to figure it all out. And I stayed here with him, with the general. I can't take it anymore. Please, if you can, forgive me.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_BunchukPDANote_hint: Found on a PDA abandoned in anomalous Lymansk.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_Controller_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Deggy, I know you won't see this message, but if I ever fall out of here like Duty's general did – dead or alive – you'll know that I tracked down the controller who caught Gadbee's group. They aren’t necessarily in a better world, but surely not in this one. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I don't know how the mutant ended up in this shithole with me, but I think the fucker is even more scared than I am. Which means there's a chance to get rid of him, not just his entourage, before he wakes up.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Wish me luck.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_Controller_hint: PDA of a stalker in Corps uniform
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_DeadManApartsPDANot: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I was on my way to Lymansk. I wasn't thinking straight anyway, and then there was this house. Wish I never went inside. Dude, if you find this, get outta here, or you're toast!</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>This house messes with you. It started bullshitting me as soon as I got hungry. I thought about some bread, and there it was, a painted piece of fucking wood! Almost broke my teeth! It plays tricks on you like you're a sucker.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>It knows I'm hungry. And freezing. I'm starting to smell kebab… but I get it now. It's all just one cursed trick.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Don't fall for it.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
Found by a dead body in anomalous Lymansk
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_DutyCampMapNote_bod: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>The general thinks the target is in the Radiowave Institute. The problem is, we aren't able to find a way straight to it. It's as if the town is reshaping itself. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Our third attempt today resulted in us back at the start, even though we strictly followed the compass. This yard remains the only stable place – no fog, no anomalies. We've set up camp here.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>The tension in the squad is getting stronger. Kosmach says nothing, but I can see how nervous he is. And the general is shutting everyone out – sometimes he spends hours staring into the fire. It's hard to stay optimistic in this setting.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_DutyCampMapNote_hin: Found in the Duty squad camp.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_FamilyPhotoNote_bod: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>The photograph shows a happy boy with his parents. There's something wrong about the way they look, but it's hard to put a finger on what it is.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_FamilyPhotoNote_hin: Found among the things of a stalker nicknamed Barabash
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_KosmacPDANote_body:
$J0L0I don't want to do this. My whole service, I've been taught that a commander's orders are above all. Now, I'm getting ready to disobey the general.
But I can't watch this anomaly eat my people alive! Zakharchuk is gone. Chepurny is on the edge. Bunchuk is only hanging on because of orders. And Tachenko… Tachenko is no longer the person I would follow to hell.
Chepurny agreed to help. Bunchuk promised not to interfere, and that's the best he can do.
The general keeps going on about an imminent disaster if we turn off that ugly piece of shit. Maybe, he's right, but if there's the slightest chance of getting our people out… I have to try.
As their commander, I'm responsible for every soldier. Dead or alive. If I die, at least my conscience is clear.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_KosmacPDANote_hint: From the PDA that belonged to Kosmach from Tachenko's group.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_LimanskMapNote_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>The sheet of paper is clumsily folded, ripped, and looks like part of the map is missing. There are several marks, but one has been heavily circled with a red marker – the owners were looking for a way into the Radiowave Institute.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_LimanskMapNote_hint: Found in the Duty squad camp
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_LonelyStalkerNote_b: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Should've never gotten into this anomaly looking for the fucking Klondike of artifacts! I think I'm going crazy. Or the anomaly can read my mind.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I opened the door yesterday and ended up outside the house I grew up in. But that house is in Lymansk! And I've never lived here.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I went up to my floor. Everything was almost the same as my childhood memories: the floor creaked where it always did, the TV hissing quietly in the living room. But, the thing is, through that interference, I could clearly hear my mom calling me to lunch. I was thirsty, but there’s only jelly-like slush in the tap.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Sometimes, I can hear boys playing soccer outside. I remember thinking that was the best day of my life.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I can see the other victims – Duty soldiers wandering the hallways. But they can't see me. They're looking for something in a hurry, and I think I finally understand – they're inside their own trap, while I'm inside mine. My trap is what no longer is, and will never be.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Every time I fall asleep, I wake up in this apartment. I go outside, then I end up back here – 27 Gagarin Street, apartment 42.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>The best day of my life.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_LonelyStalkerNote_h: Found by a dead body in anomalous Lymansk.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_LonelyStalkerNote_n: Diary of a stalker nicknamed Barabash
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_MercSniperNote_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>You can only get into an anomaly with the detector set up. Procedure:</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L2<NoteBody><ListItem><NoteDefault>Enter in small groups, as larger groups risk causing instability.</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>The person with the detector enters the anomaly first. The rest have to follow the first person's every step.</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>Upon entry, radio communications will only work over short distances – the anomaly blocks the signal from the outside.</NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault>If any traces of Tachenko's group are discovered, report to Nord personally.</NoteDefault></ListItem></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_MercSniperNote_hint: Found on a dead sniper's PDA.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_OnTable_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I sent the instructions in the previous message.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>You're not a scientist, but I tried to make them as detailed and clear as possible, so… good luck.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>If you manage to make it, you know where to go on the Mainland. If you don't… we all do what we believe in. And we can consider ourselves lucky if we're the only ones paying the price for our beliefs.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_OnTable_hint: From a PDA found in anomalous Lymansk
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_SniperKeltNote_body:
$J0L0[14:55] Celt: Nord, I got visual. Sector 6. Four of them. Looks like Duty.
[14:55] Nord: You sure?
[14:56] Celt: Old-style uniforms, armed, moving in formation. They don't react to our presence, so we couldn't communicate with them. They mentioned Tachenko.
[14:57] Nord: It's them. Keep them close until they make it to Radiowave.
[14:57] Celt: Roger.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_TachenkoPDANote_bod: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Day 5. Or 6? </NoteBold><NoteDefault>We're trapped. Zakharchuk disappeared while scouting apartments. We only heard him scream, calling for help from somewhere behind the walls. Kosmach demanded we continue the search, but I had to refuse. I can't risk losing the others trying to find one. The mission prevails, but I can see the first cracks in the squad. Only Bunchuk remains true to his duty.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Day 8. </NoteBold><NoteDefault>I suspected this was a one-way ticket, but I didn't know what we were up against. The boys trusted me, and I… used their loyalty to see this mission through. An unspeakable, but necessary decision. I keep telling myself that. But sometimes, I can't get the thought out of my head that maybe I shouldn't have rushed? Maybe, if we'd taken the time to get ready instead of jumping in headfirst, it could have turned out differently. What if there was a way to settle this in a less… unpleasant way?</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>I don't know what day it is.</NoteBold><NoteDefault>The spatial distortions are getting stronger. Keeping track of time is impossible, and visual reference points are unstable. But the information has been confirmed – the target has been located and is now under my control. It's a shame Chekhov got away. Kosmach suggested we turn off the equipment. I tried to explain that it was safe here. And if we destroy it… what if the whole Zone turns into this? The whole world? If we keep it, what if it ends up in the wrong hands? Back on the Mainland, they believe the laboratory has been destroyed, and this specimen is the last. I can't risk it. I have no right to.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Day 10? </NoteBold><NoteDefault>Kosmach and Chepurny have been colluding, but Bunchuk told me about their plan. I had to… take action. Better to have one death than millions. Chepurny and Bunchuk are looking at me differently. They don't see me as their commander. Just as an obstacle.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Day whatever.</NoteBold><NoteDefault>Chepurny ran off, and I have no idea where he is now. I need to send a report to HQ: spatial anomaly, all personnel dead or driven crazy, I took my own life. Better if they think there's no one here to send a search party for. I'm sure Duty will live longer than its general.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_TachenkoPDANote_hin: From a PDA found in anomalous Lymansk
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ06_WaterCoridor_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>They're there, deep down. I am writing this on scraps of wallpaper and throwing them into the water. They're not answering. Just looking. But I know what they want.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Every time I wake up, I'm off to the endless apartments for more paper. And every time, I'm begging them not to make me do it. I don't know how many times I've done this already. But I know it's not enough. I don't want to be silent, I don't want to freeze in this darkness, like a fly in a piece of amber. Like you froze forever. Please, don't make me do this. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Don't make me follow you.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I don't want to.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I don't want to.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I don't want to.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>

ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ07_MercFile1_body:
$J0L0When the Ward lured the Zone mercenaries into a trap, pretending to want to negotiate, then shooting them all, Nord was one of the few who managed to break out of the cordon and get his people to safety. In order to survive, he had to lay low.
And he managed to, for a long, long time. All due to the fact that there wasn't a single failure, a single unhappy employer, or a single contract broken.
His impeccable reputation allowed him to work with a few chosen, trusted customers, including some Freedom members.
Someone from that group might have recommended Lukash to contact Nord.
But now it's clear that Nord never planned to hide from the Ward forever. He was simply waiting for the right moment to strike, knowing he would only have one chance to get his revenge.
And it seems that the special technology Lukash had been experimenting with looked like a good enough chance for Nord to go all in.

ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ08_Experiment1_Note_bo:
$J1L0Test subject N17 voluntarily agrees to go through a full research course led by Dr. Slavenko.
Test subject N17 is aware of all possible negative health consequences (physical and mental), and assumes full responsibility for the results of the following experiments:
– medicaments, incl. (information redacted),
– testing under the impact of psi devices,
– mixed (medicament and instrumental).

The experiment may only be terminated upon agreement from both the test subject and the doctor.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ08_Experiment1_Note_he:
$J1L0Test subject name: (information redacted), hereinafter – Test subject N17
Sex: M
Age: 34
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ08_Experiment2_Note_bo:
$J0L0Within the final part of the course "(information redacted)" using (information redacted), the vitals of the test subject N17 are severely abnormal. Subject displayed signs of hyperactivity (rapid heartbeat, increased sweating) and auto-aggression (chest lacerations, attempts to push out eyeballs), as well as aggression towards personnel (Lab Assistant Pukhko – open TBI and broken orbital cavity).

At the moment of inspection, the status of Test subject N17 is satisfactory, vitals normal.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ08_Experiment3_Note_bo:
$J0L0Conclusion: During the repeat testing of "(information redacted)", test subject N17 displayed repeated hyperactivity and aggression, as well as seizures accompanied by hallucinations.
The application of electrical stimulation and medicaments led to heart failure.
The autopsy showed large malignant brain tumors that would have led to the death of test subject N17 withing 7-10 days.

ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ08_FirePDA_Note_body:

ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B01_VoroninOrder_No: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>More and more mutants under the base. Breaking to the surface through underground tunnels.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Mission: clear the room under the checkpoint and collapse all tunnels.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Get the charges and go down. Set explosives next to every hole. Be careful: we need to collapse the existing passages, not create new ones. Don't tell anyone about the operation until I give permission.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
Found on a broken PDA under the Cement Factory
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_DzebaNote_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I think you get the idea of how much we could make off those boxes that can barely hold all the artifacts. There is just one catch: all this crap needs to be delivered to the buyers on the Mainland. Long story short, my offer is that you help me with the artifact delivery, and you get three per cent. Three, because you're not the center of the universe. If you don't want it, others will.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>If you're in, let me know within one hour.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_DzebaNote_hint: PDA with a business offer from Hundo
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_MikluhaNotes_bo: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>It was inevitable anyway. Lukash took off to look for the source of what I brought from the Scorcher. Mavka then took off to look for Lukash. It will catch up with you in the end…</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I should have thrown that mutant into a creek, instead of giving it to Chekhov. Although, it would've been naive to think no one would find out where the Bubble came from. About as foolish as thinking no one would follow me, and the laboratory would never be found.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Come to think of it, I've done a lot of foolish things. But still not as many as Lukash or Chekhov. Or Mavka.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>She thinks I don't know what she's doing. Gathering people around her, preaching to them about true Freedom… What an idiot.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>There's no such thing as true freedom. Your freedom is only measured by how full your pockets are, and how good you are with a gun. Everything else is a lie.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>A lie we had to die for. And I refuse to die for a future I won't even be around to see.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I am at least free enough to make this choice.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_MikluhaNotes_hi: Myklukha's notes on the true price of Freedom
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_Note_ContractGo: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Order for А. Sm. (get ready before Saturday): </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteStrike>Skipjack – 2 pcs, Harp – 1 pc, Liquid Rock – 1 pc, Night Star – 1 pc, Flytrap – 4 pcs, Petal – 1 pc.</NoteStrike></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Taken from batch 598 – write off 10 artifacts ("lost in transit") </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Think of new reasons for write-off – Mercury?</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
Copper's notes about an order for an unknown customer
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_Note_Kil_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Barque: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>The Myklukha thing is confirmed.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Keel: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>Fuck me. Nothing left here for me, then. I'm a free man, don't owe anyone a thing, so I'm packing my shit, and going.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Barque: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>Really? My information says different. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Keel: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>What are you getting at?</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Barque: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>Someone would like to see you. Mykha Concrete. Remember him? Couldn't help but notice you're sitting here at the plant all the time, staying in.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Keel: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>One run from here to the Cordon – no one's going to find me. After that, I don't give a shit. You can shake down some other chump.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Barque: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>Sure, they won't find you without some help. But maybe I'm in a very helpful mood today, and looking to put my good intentions to good use?</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Keel: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>You're a piece of shit. What do you want from me?</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Barque: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>Whatever I ask for. For starters, get Copper then drag your asses back to me. I've got a job for you.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_Note_Kil_hint: Chat with an ultimatum, found on Keel's PDA.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_Note_SafetyRule: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Last week, we made a bet that Jaybird was too chickenshit to touch that crap in the warehouse. He's a daredevil all right, but I never thought he'd do that for ten grand… And no way we could've known that shit swallowed people whole! </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Hundo fired the shift leader afterwards. The warehouse was shut down, got some new rules and whatnot. Didn't even need to, though – everyone was already shitting their pants. Some might quit out of fear, but Myklukha's the only one who can fire people from the station. Fucking rules... They're the only reason I'm not back on the Mainland. I don't think I told anyone, but if Jaybird breathed a word about our bet to anyone, the guys'll shove me straight into that Mercury shit next. Who knows, maybe it would serve me right…</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
Note about an accident because of a bet with Jaybird
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_PDA_Godo_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>I never thought I'd get to see trains here in the Zone! But they are so different here. We had a depot near the laboratory back on the Mainland – you could see all the locomotives and train cars from the window. It was so cool to watch them while on breaks, especially in the summer.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Here, I can also watch the monorail trains come and go sometimes. Not often enough, though. It's a shame because every train from the Mainland means new stuff! Last month, we had this tea with a lion label, and coffee. I know someone is nicking stuff from the deliveries… but I'd also love to have some of that tea. This month, we had candy delivered twice. I'm still looking for someone who'd help me get some candy for myself. Myklukha won't cry.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Back in my college years, I learned that if I wanted to have something more than a slice of bread with a big fat slice of nothing on, I needed to stick with the right people. If I can do that here, I'll get my candy – and maybe even some caviar.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_PDA_Godo_hint: Godot's reflections on deliveries, found on his PDA
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_PDA_Kobza_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Latnyi: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>How come they closed the warehouse where Mercury gobbled up Jaybird? Someone else died in there, or what?</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Ursin: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>Nah, Hundo closed it down. Said no more patrols in that area.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Latnyi: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>Took his sweet freaking time. Barque sent me there last shift, said that was enough slacking off.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteBold>Ursin: </NoteBold><NoteDefault>I'm not surprised. Should've gone there himself, the piece of shit.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_PDA_Kobza_hint: Note with some opinions about Hundo, found on Ursin's PDA
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_SojkaArtefactNo: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Godot, did you set me up?! Why didn't you tell me that cargo 612 is flying around like a fucking bird? The damn thing's stuck under the ceiling. I tried shooting at it, and I think it moved. I'll get some more ammo. Be right back.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_SojkaDebt_body: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>February: </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteStrike>Bets – 10,000</NoteStrike></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteStrike>Bar – 3,000 (paid)</NoteStrike></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>June: </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteStrike>Bets – 20,000 + 10,000 from last month (3 months work for Myklukha)</NoteStrike></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>July: </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Bets – 23,000 + 20,000 from last month (5 months work for Myklukha)</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Fuck, there's no way I'm getting out of this damn slave labor. I'll have to agree to Barque's terms.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ10_B02_SojkaDebt_hint: Paper with amounts and work to make it up
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ11_B01_PDA_DeadFreedom: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Amigos, your group stays in the Control Depot. I suspect that Duty could try and follow us to the CNPP, so hold them off for as long as you can. We need to win some time for Mavka.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Don't scout the depot – take up your positions and stay there. I don't want anyone else dying in a zombie encounter. Those crazy Wardens could be anywhere in the depot.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
Found on a Freedomer's body in the Monorail Control Depot
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ11_B01_ReactorNote_bod: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Reporting on the reactor No. 4 control system failures: </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L1<NoteBody><ListItem><NoteDefault>Repeated failures of sensor readings in the control and protection systems </NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault> Safety system activation delay (up to 18 sec.) </NoteDefault></ListItem><ListItem><NoteDefault> Unstable low-power operation </NoteDefault></ListItem></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault> I have raised these issues repeatedly in our meetings, but they have not been recorded in the minutes, while the need for emergency shutdown has been repeatedly deemed unjustified. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>$J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>Thus, I am asking you to consider the provision of funding for hardware updates. In order to avoid the risk of failing to fulfill the "plan from higher up", the update process can be included in the repair work plan for Q3, 1986. </NoteDefault></NoteBody>
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ11_B01_ReactorNote_hea:

ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_notes_DLC01_MQ12_LostScientistNoteBo: $J0L0<NoteBody><NoteDefault>… these experiments will be the end of me. They made me believe I would study test subjects, but I'm the one being studied. I won't let them! No one can find me here. Plus, I change the code every day. Now I just need to remember it.</NoteDefault></NoteBody>
Found on a dead body in X19
