What's your problem with D4?
It's not much of a treaty, it's a mockery of Duty. Pfft. In case you didn't know, before that, Rostok used to be our base.
We tried to take it back, but then Korshunov came with his "peace", and we got pawned off to the Concrete Plant.
Who knows which would've been the richest faction if not for D4. Now we're stuck here, sweet-talking Freedom for a can of grub…
Why do you keep hanging around here, if things aren't that good with Freedom?
In Duty, all we do has a purpose. We're fighting the Zone, and that's not just empty words – ulike the vague principles Freedom lives by.
Our squad is here on General Voronin's orders to find out the reason these blasts started. We are not leaving until we complete the mission.
No matter how many mutants stalkers kill, they just keep getting stronger.
Since I came here, we've had new sub-types appearing, and now – boom! A whole new type of mutant. How's that not proof enough that the Zone should've been destroyed a long time ago?
It stinks like hell already with Freedom always smoking in here, and now we got ourselves a stalker, too. Damn that D4…
Ah, all right, sorry. I'm just nervous because of the 'neighbors'.
Let's pick up where we left off.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_IronForest_Hub_DLC01_ma: Better get out of my way now.
Don't get too close to Duty.
And you too, stalker. Don't overstay your welcome.
When the fuck is Duty finally gonna leave this camp?
At long fucking last. They're finally getting out of here.
Fucking back already. He'd be better off bolting home.
Strained relations with Duty?
Duty turns a human being into a set of rules – do this, don't do that. They want everyone to live in automatic mode, like them, only listening to 'big brother's voice'.
Life is tough as it is. I gotta have my right and freedom to relax. It so happens that the place I feel most relaxed in is the Zone.
And I'm pissed when someone's trying to take that away.
What do you know about D4?
It makes pretty good toilet paper.
I have no clue how Myklukha could sign that. We were one step away from winning, and we would've had all those mutts at our command.
Now we have to treat them as equals. No attacking, no refusing to trade, no refusing medical help, and all sorts of other shit.
What's Freedom doing in the Iron Forest?
Why are you so interested?
Friendly advice: even though Myklukha's a capitalist, he has little patience for competitors.
I support freedom of all kinds, but maybe the Zone would've been a better place if they didn't let just anyone in.
Damn Duty. They botched such a great specimen. I could've still saved it!
Why couldn't they hit it a bit lower? No danger to others, and less work for me.
The only option now is to cut it up and give it to some scientists. And that's no easy job, I'm telling you.
What was it…
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_IronForest_Hub_DLC01_se: Watch out!
Good luck to you in the Iron Forest, stalker.
Ciao!
Service duties aren't going anywhere, so we can chat before another blast hits.
Service is one thing, but I'm a bit sad to leave. A couple more games, and I'd finally win some money… But I won't risk it like Zulu.
And what do you think of your commander?
Commander Zulu is a seasoned fighter, a fierce one.
They say the general himself insisted on bringing him back to Duty. That has to mean something.
I don't know what happened before that, and I try to stay out of it.
How do you like it here with Freedom?
My motto is to treat others like how you would like to be treated yourself, instead of just following regulation.
So it's simple with Freedom – I try not to cross paths with them.
How's it going with Freedom now?
Turns out Freedom are pretty decent. Not when they play cards, though…
Objection, your honor.
My hands are clean.
Now I get the whole point of D4. It makes no sense for us to fight.
You look too relaxed to be a Duty member.
Service is one thing, I just don't like fuss. If we're ordered to wait, we wait, and if we're ordered to go, we go.
If you're in Duty, you have to learn to wait. Otherwise, your actions might put everyone in danger.
Can you remind me what D4 is?
Treaty of the four – Duty, Freedom, the Corps, and the Ward, of course. Withdrawing from attacks against each other.
I can't remember the details exactly – too much of a long-read. And I'm no expert, but if you want my opinion, Colonel Korshunov's initiative was good.
This Iron Forest is weird, even by Zone standards. I didn't think mutants could even get more aggressive. Looks like these blasts got them all worked up.
Service duties aren't going anywhere. We need to finish our chat.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_IronForest_Hub_DLC01_ve: Not now. I need some rest too, every once in a while, at least.
Take care, you'll be on your own out there.
You should get out of the Iron Forest too, stalker. For your own good.
Let's see what the Zone's done to you.
Good to know you're helping Zulu with the mission, stalker. He needs some rest.
Voronin was right – we shouldn't be here. Keep an eye on Zulu, make sure he changes his bandages, at least.
That’s all I wanted to know.
Do you treat Freedom too?
According to D4, both Duty medics and Freedom medics have to provide aid to the opposing faction.
But I was doing it even before D4. Any body armor is red when covered in blood.
Do you have time to talk?
Ask away. I'm used to curious Freedom members around here, so might as well get used to a curious stalker.
Do all Duty medics have to go out on missions?
We all go through basic military training, and have to be able to provide tactical first aid. There are no 'stay-at-home' medics here.
Every doctor has their shift schedule. Voronin always makes sure all of us take care of ourselves while saving others.

It is mandatory, yes. But if you ask me, no matter how hard it is to treat a wound on the battlefield, you're more likely to save someone there, rather than bringing them to the Concrete Plant half-dead.
What's it like to work with Zulu?
He's harder to deal with than any other squad captain. Most of our boys are way more careful than Zulu.
That young man always wanders into the deepest, darkest corners of the Zone and enters the most dangerous underground places without even a second thought.
Many Duty members think it's a hero's spirit. While I think this path leads to a nameless grave in the Zone, not to a world with no Zone or the Silver Shield.
Zulu's going on a mission without a medic?
He and Nitro went without me to deal with the repeater. They don't always follow the rules, you see. Especially veteran Duty members.
Veteran or not, anyone's luck can run out. Sooner or later, Zulu will have to start thinking about the consequences.
Nothing new in Duty. But I don't think that's a bad thing at all. The human body needs a stable routine, not constant stress.
Yeah, stalker, all these young boys should be thanking General Voronin for introducing the mandatory medic on a mission rule.
If I wasn't right next to them, half the squad would've been dead. Including Zulu. Though, if he keeps chopping up mutants with that injury of his, even I won't be able to help him.
Listen to an experienced medic, boy. No praise, no lifelong achievement – even one as big as destroying the Zone – is worth a single human life.
So we were talking about…
I'll share what I can.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_IronForest_Hub_DLC01_ze: We can share some wisdom, stalker.
Top notch wisdom! Good as the flour in Myklukha's bread.
Shame about them boys, lurking around in the dark at that Plant. They just let 'em off the leash…
Lots of folks criticize Myklukha 'cause he thinks too much about the coupons and not enough about Freedom. But I'm one of those guys who likes to have sausage, not a belly full of ideas.
Heya, stalker-boy! Grab a seat, and don't be shy. Shuffle up and deal.
Nah, leave the boyscout alone. You heard same as me that he's here to help Mavka. Sooner they're done, sooner she's back.
Nah, my man. When you're dumb, you're dumb, but when you're right, you're fuckin' right.
Be a good boy now, stalker. Mavka's our friend, and we'd move mountains for her!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_IronForest_Hub_QC_Emiss: ... Stalkers, attention... The emission... Is over...
... Listen up, diggers... An emission is about... To be headed our way... Seek shelter...
... Alright, folks... Attention everyone... There is an emission outside... Do not leave the shelters...
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_IronForest_Hub_QC_Kefir: I'm worried about Mavka.
You need to chillax.
Boys, I don't have that much on me right now. I'll pay you back once the check comes in – Duty's honor.
Whatever, man.
We'll let this one slide. Peace.
Just like that?
See, that's some top story shiz right there – relieve a Duty member of his duty. A good joke's worth more than a good bling!
We can get mo' money. Sucks we got no one to play with, though. Our guys don't wanna play with us no more – they thinkin' they'll be flat broke in no time.
Enough with the candy already, you're piggin' out, man! You'll get so fat that someone's gonna shoot you at night 'cuz you look like a stray flesh.
Look who's talkin'! You're growin' like a fuckin' mushroom with all that sausage. They can see you all the way from the Slag Heap, ya know.
Nah, man, sausage is protein! Gives muscle, like six-packs and shiz.

You ain't messin' with my brain that easily – I see whatcha doin'. You wanna hustle my candy to them stalkers for bling. Not gonna fly, man! You want candy – you come in handy. Myklukha don't give it away for nothin'.
I'm bored.
No one to play cards with.
Wonder what Mavka's up to.
Think I had too much candy.
Solid vibe here when Harpoon ain't mumbling.
Maybe one more, eh, Bulba?
What's Voronin makin a fuss about now?
Why didn't Myklukha call us?
Who ate my candy?!
Someone best take Harpoon home with them.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_IronForest_Hub_QC_Nitro: It's good that we're leaving. Very good.
Good job, Nitro! Passed with flying colors, as always! Finally, we won't have to hang about with this damn Freedom lot in this god-forsaken Iron Forest.
It wasn't me. It was Mavka and the loner who helped me. The one from "damn Freedom". So I guess it's them you should be thanking.
You're a sharp one, Nitro. You can take on any type of tech, but you can't take a win. We all know that little miss wouldn't have done it without you.
So, where should we put a repeater of our own?
Need to make sure I got everything.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_IronForest_Hub_QC_PeltB: Trapped us here with these hippies.
Maybe we should play some cards?
What are you waiting for! Go to Vezha and get that wound dressed!
Why are you all nervous? The wound isn't serious. Some Freedom boys got it way worse. I'll wait.
Damn D4! I can't wrap my head around it. That's our medic! He's supposed to treat Duty, not the whole damned Zone!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_IronForest_Hub_QC_Vezha: Everyone needs to be extra careful. Everyone! No exceptions.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_IronForest_Hub_QD_Kefir: Are you going to be fine here without Duty?
We saw this spot first, no shiz.
Of course, we'll be good.
But bummed out a bit, ya know, 'cause no one to play cards with.
Being bummed out's a part of Zone life, man.
How are things with Duty as your neighbors?
Peachy.
They don't go gettin' in our way, and we're card pals.
But they're, ya know, losers and no fun.
Sure's no fun for them when they lose all their bling to us! But whatcha gonna do, right, man? It is what it is.
How did you end up in the Iron Forest?
Harpoon dragged us along with him. We're his top notch mutie-catching crew.
"Top notch" meaning we're doin' everythin, and he ain't doin' shiz.
Do some nosin' about, put a mutie in a cage, deliver a mutie – all us. Harpoon just bums around and criticizes.
Got a minute to chat?
We're, like, normally super busy.
But right now, you hit the jackpot.
I have some more questions about Mavka.
Shoot. We can go on and on about her for hours!
Weeks!
Does Mavka have any kind of special role in Freedom?
She's our commentator in the Arena. Can't really remember how she ended up there…
But she's always been the loudest one. And she's the showwoman type. Something she's got in common with Myklukha.
I heard they had a casting, for real, and they picked her.

I heard that too, but I'm sure that's BS. Between us mind – and I'll deny all of it, man – I reckon Myklukha put her there so she didn't get in his way. But it ain't that easy to make our gal stay in one place, heh.
How did she end up in Freedom?
Like the rest of us – walked right on in.
That ain’t what the fella means, dude. We don't know the lowdown, but my gut's tellin' me she didn't come to the Zone 'cause the Mainland was all rainbows and roses.
Mavka loves Freedom, for real. Well, not like, it's people and stuff, but in general. Said she "couldn't breathe" on the Mainland, but the Zone is where it's at.
And who loves the Zone best? That's right – Freedom, man. So she started hangin' out with us. 'Cause her biggest dream is to give the gift of Zone miracles to everyone on the Mainland.
What does your leader think about her?
Oh, that's a can of worms.
Not easy to say, either, man.
Myklukha's got a whole lotta beef with Mavka.
'Cause Mavka's got a lotta beef with Myklukha.
What can you tell me about your lady friend?
Mavka's the best fo' sho'. We met on a mission, and she saved our asses from mutants down there, ya know.
Which, by the way, made her lose some big-shot package, Myklukha gave her a shizload of trouble after. Dunno if I'd have done the same.
That was long back, but we's still friends. We can tell you a whole lot about her, but you gotta ask whatcha wanna know.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_DLC01_azot_0_InfoT: Sometimes I regret leaving Yaniv – it was all peace and quiet, after all. Then I start thinking about how Zulu will get into trouble without me, and the regret is gone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_DLC01_bolshak_0_He: Why are you bothering me, stalker?
Beethoven is with me now. He doesn't talk, and doesn't get in my way. And he won't get in yours. He'll just take you where you need to go.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_DLC01_bolshak_0_In: Every action of yours is a note in the story that I will hear soon.
Everyone has finally left the forest. I can just listen, at last.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_DLC01_bolshak_0_Re: So what was our story about? Ah…
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_DLC01_bolshak_0_Tr: I'll take it. Pass it on. Repeat.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_DLC01_bolshak_0_Up: No detail will be left unnoticed.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_HarpoonCalls_Af: I told Marabou that we could use an extra pair of hands. First, we got Duty, now we have a loner too!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_HarpoonCalls_In: Come over for a meet 'n' greet, monsieur stalker!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_HarpoonHoping_I: Cher Dieu, help the stalker get this done!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_LukashTrace_Mes: Now I understand what you meant. I saw it with my own eyes. It… it's worth it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_MavkaBolshakCal: Watch out for the mutants! While the machine is on, there'll be more of them than we usually get.
We can do it. Turn it on.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_MavkaBolshakCat: There he is. You getting it?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_MavkaBolshakLoc: Got the location. The source of the signal is nearby, somewhere in the Testing Workshop. Sending it over.
I need to know where the second signal's coming from.
But the repeaters can hardly handle it. Plus, the mutants.
Do what you're told. You don't want me as your enemy.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_MavkaGoToCamp_N: And… I'll stay here. I need to… need to think.
Stalker… sorry you had to deal with the mutants. I thought… I thought I'd be out here on my own.
Now you need to get to Zulu. Knowing him, he wouldn't want you to go to the Workshop alone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_MavkaRetranslat: There's gonna be a lot of them because of the Blasts.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_MountOrder_Comm: A witness. Get rid of him.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_NitroAfterDialo: Phew, what a day. I wish Duty would deal with this Zone already. I need to pull myself together and get to the camp.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_NitroCallAfterF: Whoa! Look at that, it's working! Comms are back on. That means the repeater's up and running.
I don't know what you did, but it fixed the problem. I'll meet you back on the ground.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_NitroEncourage2: That's it, stalker! You could replace me as Duty's technician!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_NitroEncourage_: Sorry for my negative vibes. I'm stressed out, so I'm grumpy. I'm sure you'll have no problem dealing with whatever broke down.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_NitroPlayerRuns: Hey, where are you off to?
Stalker, where are you off to? We're not done!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_NitroReminder_R: Not too eager to climb the tower, stalker? No judgement. But there's no other way we can fix our repeater problem.
You need to climb the tower and see what broke down in the repeater.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_NitroSad_Whinin: On the other hand, how would Zulu manage without me? He couldn't.
Maybe I should've stayed in Yaniv, kept my head down…
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_ZuluInvite_Invi: If you have any questions, ask away.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_ZuluMavkaChange: There's still time to change your mind. It's dangerous.
But I get it, Zulu. I wouldn't come if it wasn't important.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_ZuluPostBriefIn: If you need to clear anything up, ask away.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_ZuluVezhaWound_: Don't touch your shoulder. Leave it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_ZuluVoroninCall: General, we found the source of the Blasts and we're ready to start phase two of the operation. Requesting confirmation.
General Voronin, can you hear me? Over.
Operation canceled. Gather your unit and leave the Iron Forest.
Unacceptable risk of losing the unit. The danger level is too high.
Say again… I can't hear you, General.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_ZuluVoroninGo_B: Lieutenant Kozhukh, get everyone and return to base.
I'll take a walk before I'm court-martialed.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QC_ZuluVoroninGo_U: Zulu, this is an order – get your squad out of the Iron Forest. The operation is finished. Over and out.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_BolshakFirstMee: And you… are you okay?
Are you? And the Zone? And what about the world? I can think of an answer, but will it be true? Sorry, I'm averse to lying.
Those bandits outside won't be back.
Our business with them is over. I'm no longer interested in their story.
Here are the coordinates. She's looking for something, like you are. And just like you, she can't find it. But there will be a story, I can hear it.
Here are the coordinates. She's looking for something. A story of her own. One day, I'll hear it.
What was the story Mavka told you?
She only gave me a piece of the puzzle. A list of incoming and outgoing communications from the IPSF checkpoint.
I'm yet to learn the story. And there definitely is one, I can hear it.
And how much will it cost to use your equipment?
Money won't fly with me. Money is good, but it has no value. Stories – now that's where I live.
I need help with calculations. Should be right up your alley.
I didn't know Mavka had another assistant. She talked me through everything already. Consider my services paid for.
If you want to know more, go after her. I don't like repeating myself. Already too much chatter on the channel.
I don't.
Shame. You're here, but not really. We'll have a hard time getting along. But I'm used to dealing with your kind. Tell me what you need.
Do you recognize the tune?
Do you happen to know where Mavka went?
I do. I know a lot of things.
Of course I do.
So you understand it, too. You dissolve in it. That's good, stalker.
You and I, we speak the same language.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_MavkaFirstTimeM: We'll chat later, I promise, but right now we're running out of time. I have to install the last repeater so Chief can get his equipment running.
It only works during Blasts, and we can't afford to miss the next one. So let's get going. You'll be helping me fight off mutants.
No worries. Water under the bridge.
Zulu sent me to help you. His wound got worse, so I'm filling in for him.
Got it, sorry, stalker. I really am. We don't have much time, so I'm all wired. Hope you get it. No hard feelings, deal?
Hold. I'm not looking for trouble. Are you?
Freedom knows how to welcome their guests.
It’s even more welcoming at Rostok. You can see it for yourself, wise head.
No more pointing your gun at me.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_MavkaPostBriefi: I saw a Chimera figurine in your camp here.
I left it there? Dammit! Just don't tell Zulu: he carved it for me after he defeated a Chimera at the Arena.
Too many things on my mind, so I forgot. I'll  go back for it, I will. But first, the Workshop.
Is Freedom having some kind of problems?
Freedom's not what it used to be, stalker. Most newcomers don't even know we're actually supposed to liberate the Mainland.
Coupons aren't bad. What's bad is that they stopped serving Freedom's cause, and now serve something else instead.
Who are you trying to find in the Iron Forest?
Someone who was supposed to bring Freedom back to its roots, but vanished all of a sudden.
That's all I can tell you for now.
Sorry again for the mutant set-up, stalker. I couldn't risk refusing help at a crucial moment.
How long have you and Zulu known each other?
Since I started as the host for Arena fights. Can't even remember the exact year, I'm bad with numbers. Myklukha would know.
But it feels like a long time. It's hard for me to imagine an evening fight without having a cup of tea with Zulu after.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_MavkaZuluWorksh: Can a Duty member disobey orders?
No. There will be consequences, but only if I survive our mission.
So there's no point thinking about it. Mission first, life plans later.
What's the plan?
God, finally back to the point. This Duty drama… Oh, it's like a lullaby.
Mavka! You're here! I didn't even notice you.
I got bitten by a bloodsucker, so now I have an invisible mode, you know.
Don't say that. Not funny.
Okay, fine. By the way, I've been to the Workshop already. We've got two problems back there.
We?
Aha, I'm coming with you.
I'm not sure I should trust her.
Why not? She's a person, not a mutant. You can trust people, despite the risks, even if the Zone teaches you not to.
I know what stalker means. Okay, no mutant set-ups this time. I promise.
You mentioned we have problems at the Workshop. What problems?
The entrance is blocked. With all due respect, even Zulu won't be able to open those heavy doors, no matter how hard he tries.
I think we can still open them somehow, but we need to turn the power on first. There's a power station nearby. That should be enough.
So the plan is that Skif powers up the power station while we will take care of the Zone fauna around the workshop. I'm guessing that's problem number two.
Exactly! Nice to go out on a run with someone experienced!
Why not. Fine by me.
Off on a mission with a stalker and a Freedomer. Heh, not everyone in Duty would approve.
But the mission is what matters. And people aren't mutants. You can trust people, despite the risks, even if the Zone teaches you not to.
Sorry for… for all this. I thought the call would go differently.
But that doesn't matter. What matters is now we know where the source is. Which means Nitro's theory was right, and we might be able to get rid of the Blasts.
We don't have many people – none, in fact – but you and I, stalker… we can do it. I hope you won't say no. I'm offering more than just gratitude, that goes without saying.
Why did Voronin order the squad back so suddenly?
You heard him. "Unacceptable risk of losing the unit".
And I understand… I know why the General doesn't want us poking around there. Voronin is being cautious. He cares about every single soldier.
But every Duty member knows what they signed up for. We have to destroy the Zone, no matter the cost. And I'm willing to pay with my life.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_NitroRetranslat: How do you know Chief? Should I trust him?
I know every technician in the Zone. All of them used to go to Prypiat for some curious spares, and the only way there was through Yaniv.
Chief and I are hardly best friends, but I trust him with my life. Apart from Zulu, he's the only person in the Zone who never lies.
For Zulu, telling the truth is a matter of principle, and Chief… he just… he can't lie.
And Chief will help us free of charge?
You'll have to find out. We discussed this plan with Mavka, but it never went further than that discussion. You'll have to play it by ear.
Thanks for your help, stalker. Duty won't forget it! And neither will I!
What kind of equipment does Chief have?
The triangulation kind. It measures the angles between the positions of the repeaters and the signal's direction.
I thought a PDA could do this, but I overestimated it. Too much data to process simultaneously.
You're taking your sweet time, I see. Don't get me wrong, I'm the same! Whatever needs sorting out will sort itself out, and if it doesn't, well… it wasn't that important.
Back to the point: what was the problem? The repeater turned into a sentient being and you had to have a good old gunfight?
What was the problem? The repeater turned into a sentient being and you had to have a good old gunfight?
SIRCAA was working together with Duty?
At least one good thing came out of working with the Ward. There was a ton of paperwork I had to file, of course, but I was used to that 'cause we do the same in Duty.
Not exactly. There was a poltergeist lurking nearby.
Aaaah! Electric! How come I didn't think of that! They love messing with all kinds of equipment. Damn! If Zulu was here, he would've suspected a mutant right away.
Maybe SIRCAA has some research on how to repel them from equipment, but there's no way I can get my hands on that now. Damn Zone!
I'll need to stop by SIRCAA. Maybe they have some research on how to repel them from equipment. Damn Zone. You never know what's waiting around the corner!
SIRCAA is working together with Duty?
At least one good thing came out of working with the Ward. There's a ton of paperwork I have to file, of course, but I'm used to that 'cause we do the same in Duty.
What's next?
I'll go to the camp, to Vezha: that's enough Zone adventures for one day. And, honestly, I just want to see Zulu sitting around doing absolutely nothing with my own eyes.
And you, stalker, will have to meet Chief – the merchant and technician who's going to help us decipher the data from the repeaters.
I thought my PDA would be enough to run the calculations, but no. Chief has equipment with a much higher processing capacity. It should be able to give us the location of the source of the Blasts.
Won't I fall down from there?
I hope not. But you look like you're in good shape, unlike me.
I've been a technician for quite a while and got used to the comfort. A bit too much, I guess.
I can help you find her. Zulu sent me to give you a hand.
Oh, oh, oh! Now we're talking! So there's hope my plan with the damn repeaters might still work out!
So, Zulu sent someone instead of coming himself? And sat this one out? Wow! I'm proud of him! That's progress.
Any idea what might have broken down?
In the Zone? In a device that I put together in a couple of days from borrowed SIRCAA spare parts? With Zulu hovering over me?! Any number things might have broken down.
Anything from physical damage caused by a sneaky rodent to mapping software bugs.
We won't look for Mavka?
Nah, I just wanted to find her so I could ask her to climb up there and take a look at the repeater. Heights are her thing. In every way.
But you'll do just fine, stalker. Mavka's got another repeater to take care of, so I'm sure she's got her hands full.
You mean Mavka?
Exactly! How do you… Never mind. You probably know her from the Arena. I keep forgetting half the Zone knows who she is.
I could never understand it. The Arena, I mean. It's hard enough as it is in the Zone, so why go and make your life even harder?
Whatever. It's a good thing you know her. If I'm lucky enough, maybe you'll agree to come look for her?
Oh, stalker! Have you seen a girl around here... you know, a spirited one? From Freedom.
How can I figure out what the problem is? I'm no technician.
I am, and there's no guarantee I can pinpoint the problem, either.

It's more complicated than it seems with this Zone equipment as there's always some kind of trouble. That's why I work with Duty. They'll get rid of the Zone and make the world a lot, lot more simple.
Let's hope it's just a loose screw. If not, grab it and get down - we'll figure it out together. The radio doesn't work without a repeater, unfortunately.
So what do you need me to do?
You need to deal with the repeater, the one Mavka already managed to install.
She installed it all right, but for some reason it stopped working. You need to climb up there and find out what went wrong.
See? I tried to play the hero, just like Zulu, and tried to climb up there myself. It didn't work out. I fell, and... and I don't want to try climbing it again.
What do you mean, "progress"?
Everyone in Duty wants to be a hero. But Zulu is the only one of them who's willing to go to great lengths for it.
Loads of people at the Concrete Plant admire him, but I know the real reason for that eagerness and what the consequences might be.
These "heroic feats" of his are only making things worse for himself, and don't really serve Duty's cause at all.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_ZuluHarpoonBrie: And how can we deal with those Blasts?
Nitro, our technician, thinks their nature is technological and has a source. So, if we find it and destroy it, there'll be no more Blasts.

You might think this is a reliable plan, stalker, but the problem is, they don't know where to find the source. They brought their… what was it… repeaters to locate it, but they bit off more than they could chew.
Duty's resources are… limited. The area turned out to be more dangerous than we thought, and we don't have enough hands to install the devices. That's why we need your help, stalker.
You said you had a job for me.
We do. Unfortunately, Duty, us, and everyone else in the Iron Forest are in the same sinking boat. And it's because of those Blasts.
That mutant attack you helped us fight off wasn't the first, won't be the last, and it happened because of those Blasts.
Amok was provoked by Blasts, too. They make all the mutants around more aggressive.
Duty has been surveilling this new anomalous activity for a long time. As soon as we came up with a theory on how to deal with it, we arrived in the Iron Forest immediately.
I didn't know Duty was so active.
That's a fair point. Not a pleasant one, of course. Duty's not at its finest as a faction these days, but I assure you, stalker, that not everyone in Duty has given up.
We still have soldiers who can't just sit around when yet another manifestation of the Zone opens up its rotten maw.
Freedom members let Duty into their camp?
How could we refuse these darlings, willing to destroy everything we hold dear? We couldn’t, obviously!
And we are very grateful for that. Thank you, truly.
You're welcome. I'm not too eager to admit it, but with Duty here I do feel… safer. These Blasts are damn scary, and it would be nice if someone finally put an end to them.
So is it a Freedom camp or Duty?
Freedom, of course! We're ahead of the curve! We were the first ones who heard the goss about a new type of mutant lurking here. The Arena needs fresh goods!
And as soon as the area became more accessible, we grabbed our cages and rushed over to catch some of those pretty boys for folks' entertainment.
Who could've known this five-minute adventure would turn out to be full of these damn Blasts – and to top it off, those buzzkills next door.
Your first fight with an amok?
Yeah.
Die-hard bastards. Fighting to the death. Don't fall for it, aim for their spinal block and they're done for.
They're done for. You're done for... That's Duty for you. Their plans are always the same – destroy, clean up, wipe out. But then what, huh?
Has Freedom been helping you?
We sent our Mavka to assist. Honestly, I didn't want to as I didn't think she was tough enough for it, but Zulu insisted. And was she of any help? Is the mission successful?
It wasn't her fault I got wounded.
We are helping. But Freedom doesn't have people to spare.
We can help!
When are you gonna do that? You haven't even finished what I asked you to do an hour ago.
How do Duty and Freedom get along in the same camp?
We're okay, negotiating. Like we used to in Yaniv, many years ago. We get occasional personal disagreements, of course, sometimes Harpoon loses his temper, but… I get it. I'm not mad at him.
You better! Ah… whatever. We got ourselves a bigger problem, and oddly enough, Duty is helping us deal with it.
So, what do I need to do?
We needed at least three people for the mission, now it's just Mavka – sent by Freedom to assist – and our Nitro, and I'm sure they could use some help.
Zulu's reassurance is all we have because Blasts don't just get mutants worked up, you see. They also disrupt the comms all along the Iron Forest.
We don't know for sure where they are, what their status is, or if they are even alive. You need to find Mavka or Nitro and give them a hand.
Chances are slim, but they might be somewhere around these coordinates. This was one of the spots where I was supposed to install a repeater.
Good luck, stalker. Everyone's life would be easier without these Blasts. You won't regret signing up for this.
What does this repeater do?
Our technician, Nitro, invented it. I'd love to tell you more, but I can't. These things aren't exactly my strong suit.
They somehow read the signal from the epicenter and through tri… quad… annihilation, frustra… Ah, I'm bad at this.
They'll give us the location of the Blast source if we install them all around the Iron Forest.
Nitro tried to explain it to me, too, but I didn't understand a thing he was saying then forgot it all.
Why is this area so dangerous?
Mostly, aggressive mutants. They did this to me. Mavka, Nitro, and I were on our way to install a repeater when they attacked us full force. We managed to fight them off, but I'd lost too much blood.
Mavka went further ahead, and Nitro insisted on taking me to the camp to recover. As you can imagine, the fight against that amok wasn't much help in the recovery process.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_ZuluPostBrief_D: I joined Duty as soon as I stepped inside the Perimeter. The Zone used to be my enemy back on the Mainland – all my friends came here to get rich, but only found death.
I couldn't just sit and watch the Zone consume people. Back then, I didn't know the time would come when it would get to me too.

I didn't know what it'd turn me into. A monster. A drunk. A thoughtless animal. If it wasn't for General Voronin's personal involvement, I would've been dead in that tower. Another one would have been lost to the Zone.
But he got me out. He took the bottle from me and reminded me of my purpose. Since then, I don't drink, and I always remember who my real enemy is, and what it's capable of.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_ZuluPostBrief_F: How does Duty get along with Freedom next door?
Same as we did in Yaniv. One human being can always reason with another.
But there's no reasoning with mutants.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_ZuluPostBrief_M: A Freedomer. It's her voice you probably heard in the Arena. She came here as part of Harpoon's squad, and now she's helping us deal with the Blasts.
I knew her even before the Iron Forest – you can count on her. She'd rather die trying than let someone down.
Nitro says we have that in common, but… I don't know. I've let people down more than once.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_ZuluPostBrief_N: Our technician. Even though he's not officially in Duty, he's one of ours in spirit. He has the magic touch! He's the one who crafted my shovel.
Along with many other things for Duty, including those repeaters. We're not a hundred per cent sure the plan will work, but Nitro can always come up with something else.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_ZuluPostBrief_P: I have a couple of personal questions.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_ZuluPostBrief_S: You mentioned you've let someone down, more than once. What was that about?
This isn't an easy topic for me, stalker. But I hate lying or dancing around the truth just as much as I hate my past. So listen up if you want to know the answer.
After yet another pointless Duty run, I lost it. I attacked my captain at the time, Shulha, and… and I almost beat him to death.

After that, I left Duty. Sat around in the tower, drinking, and turning into what I came here to fight. I let my captain down, and my general, and I let Duty down. There isn't a day I don't regret what I've done.
And I would rather avoid this topic in the future.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_ZuluPostBrief_T: I still have some questions about the mission.
You need to find Nitro or Mavka at the coordinates I sent you and help them install the repeaters.
These devices will help us find the source of the Blasts, and then we'll have a chance to figure out how to get rid of them.
What do I need to do?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_ZuluPostBrief_V: What do you know about Voronin?
What everyone else knows – he's got no secrets. A Duty general, Tachenko's successor, and used to serve on the Mainland. He's from a military family.
He's a good man, and a good strategist. Even though it sometimes seems he's thinking too much and doing too little.
But that's my personal opinion, and it doesn't matter. I owe him a lot. Including the fact that I'm still in Duty.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_QD_ZuluPostBriefin: Are you sure I can trust Mavka?
I'm not stupid. She needs something from the Workshop. So she volunteered to "help".
But I'm also sure she's not going to stab anyone in the back. Mavka isn't like other stalkers in the Zone. She values people. Even when she doesn't get any profit from it.
I've known her since the Arena. I sometimes fight there, I… I need to blow off steam. And Mavka is one of the few people who doesn't judge me for it.
We're off on an expedition to the Workshop – the supposed source of the Blasts.
Mavka and I will clear the fauna outside, and you have to find a way to power up the door to the Workshop.
The founder of Duty. Came here on an army mission, saw what was happening, and decided to devote his life to destroying the Zone.
He died tragically, along with his squad, on a mission in a spatial anomaly.
An incredible man. No fear, whatsoever. Fighting to the very end. He understood the Zone couldn't be defeated without sacrifices.
We can do it, stalker. We'll deal with those Blasts. I'm sure we will.
Why did you decide to deal with the Blasts?
Voronin asked me the same thing. He thinks they're like Emissions – evil. But the kind that can't be dealt with.
I studied general Tachenko's notes. I can't share everything, but they made me understand that the Blasts might be man-made.
Which means we can deal with them. Which means we have to.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_mavka_0_InfoTopic_: I miss the times when stalkers went to the Zone for the ideas, not the coupons. I hope that one day Myklukha comes to his senses and brings Freedom back to its roots.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ02_zulus_0_InfoTopic_: The Zone has to be destroyed. I believe that, one day, every stalker will understand that.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_AL_MavkaZulu_Elect: Good work, Skif. Head to us.
But be quick, or you'll miss out on all the fun! Zulu's lighting it up like it's his Arena debut.
Wow! Look at that shovel hit! One more — missed the zombie dude!
It's not the Arena, so stop commenting like that. You'll jinx us!
I thought you were used to it by now. Fine, Mavka out.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_AL_MavkaZulu_Priva: Damn vents. Only sewers are worse. Feels like a ton of rats are gonna crawl out from behind.
I thought Freedom members saw good in all Zone manifestations.
Only in those useful to humankind! Rats in vents definitely aren't.
Cool it, I'll keep watch. No mutants can get past me. Unless, of course, they're lurking in some side passage…
Damn it, Zulu! Next time, you're going in.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_AL_NordFenrir_Plan: Nord, come in! Code 3008. I've never seen shit like this!
Dead. I think… He felt something was coming in his last moments... It didn't turn out nice and quiet for any of us.
I can't. Whatever Lukash was building there, it didn't survive combat. If you wanted to use it, you'll have to find yourself a new one…
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_DLC01_troj_0_InfoT: Way back, I thought D4 would last forever. I was even happy they came up with it. But after what happened… No more dirty deals with those Freedom scumbags.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_MavkaZulu_CallS: Skif, Mavka and I are heading to the Testing Workshop. Once you deal with the power, come and join us there.
Keep your radio on, and don't get lost!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_MavkaZulu_Corri: I can reach it through the vent, but the bar will give me some trouble.
This will only solve part of the problem. Something's definitely blocking the power, even after Skif started the generator.
Weird… The next room has power. Skif, go check it out. I'll help Mavka with the vent while you try to restore power in the control room. We'll be on comms, main channel.
This looks like the control room. The door can be unlocked.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_MavkaZulu_D4Cha: So, will Duty expel you again this time, or merely issue a reprimand for insubordination?
Mavka. I lost control back then. Nearly beat Shulga to death. But anyway, they never expelled me even for this.
I left on my own. I felt I was unworthy of my comrades' trust.
I made it to Prypiat. Saw the Zone for what it really is and remembered what we're fighting against. Duty needs every last soldier.
I don't see eye to eye with General Voronin on every matter. But he gave me another shot, and I'm thankful for that.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_MavkaZulu_DoorC: Damn it, we didn't get far. It's closed. Let me…
Fuck! Nah, that wound is serious. Let's find a way around.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_MavkaZulu_DoorJ: Zulu, there's fresh blood on your bandage. Let Skif open it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_MavkaZulu_DoorP: Open the door already! I'll help him!
That damn polter messed up the electric lock!
Fuck... Skif! It's just you against him. Hang on!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_MavkaZulu_Doors: I wonder what kind of gizmos they tested here.
Looks like some kind of Project X equipment.
Nothing. Forget it. Let's figure out which way we should go.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_MavkaZulu_NearV: It's all good. We'll figure it out.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_MavkaZulu_Safet: By the way, how's the Arena doing while you're away?
Oh, that's a funny one. Myklukha temporarily dragged in some host from the Mainland.
Was someone really up for it?
Of course. The boss can be generous.
I'm not worried he'll take my place. I'll go back when I want to. Maybe you'll join me one day?
Maybe, but we gotta finish here first.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_MavkaZulu_Shove: By the way, you never told me where you got that jacked-up shovel of yours.
Curiosity killed the cat. Looking to get one for Eugene?
Not everyone in Freedom is looking for money.
Nitro made it, in honor of my return to Duty. I'm sure you can ask him to make you one. He won't say no to you.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_MavkaZulu_Split: Okay, so why didn't this hermetic door open from the control room? Any ideas?
Not yet. Let's split up and look for ways we can move forward. Boys to the left, girls to the right. Make sure to keep your radios on.
I heard a campfire story that started just like this.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_MavkaZulu_Walki: Finally, a decent run! You and I, like old times, watching each other's backs, and a good fighter by our side…
Last time you said it was a "decent run", we stumbled upon a chimera.
First, it was the chimera who stumbled upon us, and second, since when were you so superstitious?
The Zone can make anyone feel superstitious. If it's not the Blasts, it's the Emissions — and don't get me started on mutants and anomalies.
But the bone marrow of that chimera may become part of a cure for some rare disease.
I wanna believe that beast will save more people than it managed to kill.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Mavka_AfterComb: Give it up for Skif, master of the A-a-a-arena! That was le-gen-da-ry! The crowd is in awe.
Not bad, you fought better in the Arena, though.
You two can chat later. Still got that key card in a safe place?
Good job. We need folks like you in the Arena.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Mavka_CallToBac: Whoa, Skif, it's this way! We're waiting on you.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Mavka_Climb_How: Anything but rats… Freaking hate rats.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Mavka_InteractQ: Thanks again, Skif. Zulu and I will keep looking for whoever is really behind this.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Mavka_LetZuluIn: Zulu's here… Hold on, I'll let you in.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Mavka_OpensDoor: Hey, relax! I'm fine, don't worry. Just a little trouble on the road.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Mikluha_Interac: Freedom won't forget what happened here.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Zulu_CallMavka_: Excellent work, Skif. Where did Mavka go?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Zulu_DoAsYouDid: Skif, the first electric drive is connected. I don't know what it is you did, but keep up the good work.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Zulu_Fork_GoThe: I'll look around. Maybe I can get the door's electric drive motors connected. You should go further down the hallway and check it out.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Zulu_GoAhead_1_: You go ahead, Skif. Mavka and I will take it from here.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Zulu_GoCamp_Mee: Mavka and I are done here. Lukash… We gave him a proper goodbye.
Heading to camp now. We'll meet you there. Hope you have some news for us.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Zulu_HelpRoomPo: I can handle this alone, Skif. You'd better go and get the power on in the room.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Zulu_KillThisAn: If you see this, shoot it or go around it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Zulu_MoveOn_GoF: You go on. I'll stay and see if there's anything we can do here.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QC_Zulu_UseCard_Us: Skif, it looks like there's a slot for a key card here. We should try it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QD_MavkaZulu_LetsG: Ready to go to the workshop?
Easy. Had to deal with a couple of zombies, other than that, it was a piece of cake.
Everything's a piece of cake according to you. Doesn't sound like the Zone at all.
Any trouble on your way here?
Not everything. I'm just not used to whining.
Nitro got it from some seasoned tech. Looks like Degtyarev himself had it with him in the Iron Forest. So treat it like a true relic.
We need to go through the underground tunnels of the Testing Workshop. We'll find the source of the Blasts and deal with it.
Here's the key card. It should come in handy. Mavka and I will clear the hallway.
Great, let's roll! Open the door, Skif.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QD_Mavka_AfterTalk: Zulu has the PDA. But here's something else.
You don't believe Duty's behind this?
Of course I don't! It's bullshit. Why would they? Zulu's guys would never…
Myklukha can believe whatever he wants — or pretend to believe. I'll find the real culprit.
Zulu and I will keep digging. We'll contact you once we find something. I hope you'll still want to help.
The merc's PDA has an unusual emblem on it. Zulu has it.
This is something. Thanks, Skif, really. For everything. Here, for all your trouble.
What do you think happened here?
A well-planned massacre. Someone waited for Zulu's people to leave and slaughtered every single person at the camp.
I… I can't believe it. Why? Someone definitely knew everything about my squad. I don't know, Skif…
But I'll make sure to find out.
I don't even know what to say, Skif. All of this just… sucks. First Lukash, and now the guys.

And this whole farce with D4 gone. "Choice is a privilege…" Bullshit. No one had a choice! Myklukha was forced to react to the deaths of his people, just like Voronin had to react when Zulu was being threatened.
I didn't have a choice, either. I couldn't save them. But I'll make sure to find whoever's responsible for this.
Nothing good. This has given people a reason to be at each other's throats. Whatever shit's actually happened here, it's triggered a whole damn avalanche.
I'm done with the Arena for sure. To hell with it now! I'll find the murderers, and I'll make them pay. I promise. Fine, enough… Did you find anything at the Testing Workshop?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QD_Myklukha_AfterT: How did you find out what happened here so fast?
Harpoon reached out to me as soon as comms went back on and told me what happened. I figured I should be here in person.
Once I came to see for myself, well… I guess my gut was right again.
Stop by Rostok. Even after what happened here, we'll welcome anyone with open arms, as long as they're not Duty.
And remember: Freedom gives everyone what they deserve.
Is D4 no longer in force?
You heard Voronin. The general said D4 is done for. Mind you: his words, not mine.
No one expected the written obligations to last forever. But they still kept the factions from slaughtering each other for territory or power. It almost worked.
That looks like it's going to change.
We won't forget what happened here. No discounts for Duty – they'll pay in full for what they've done.
Now's the time to get ready. I'm sure Voronin is thinking the same. While the Ward is calling the shots here, they won't allow a straight-up war.
But war doesn't always have to be fought in plain sight. Soldiers might be the ones to charge forward, but we look for workarounds.
War. So far, the Wardens have their hands full, meaning they won't meddle in our business. We'll figure it out on our own.
Skif, right? I heard you're one to end up in the wrong place at the wrong time quite a lot.
That's convenient, being in the center of the action. You get to hear all the news firsthand.
So, what did you want to ask, Skif?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QD_Troy_AfterTalk_: Let's chat another time, loner. I'm grieving my fallen friends right now.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ03_QD_Zulu_SearchArea: I'll stay here to help Mavka with Lukash. We do everything in our power to bury our own in Duty. Mavka isn't Duty, but she's one of us — and that means her friend is, too.
So far, so good. As if nothing was ever wrong with it.
It didn't help Lukash much, though. And there's no way of knowing what it'll do to me. I'd prefer my wound to heal naturally.
You've not heard of him? Lukash is the former leader of Freedom. He was in charge until Myklukha got back from the Scorcher.
It was Lukash who brought Mavka to the faction.
They were pals, as far as I know. But Mavka will get through it. She's strong. In this place… that's how it is.
Try to find out who did it, but stay out of trouble. We've had enough deaths for one day. I'll meet you at the camp.
Here, take it. In case something goes south.
Check out the rest of the facilities, Skif. Lukash sure didn't stab himself.
I wish I knew for sure, Skif. Seems like the Blasts and the Oasis were connected to this device.
We got rid of the source. Some might feel sorry the Oasis is gone, but not me. These miracles of the Zone always come with a catch.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_AL_KarmaPDA2_Archi: It's gotten crowded here in the Iron Forest, Commander! Blasts attract attention. If it keeps going on like this, our old friends might come to visit.
I have an idea. We could give them a new thing to try and track down.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_AL_KarmaPDA_Archiv: Yeah, as discussed. Unloaded at the Warehouse, security has been put on it. It's a freaking scientist's dream down there.
You can run your experiments in peace and quiet now. No need to stash your spares away.
I hope you handled it with care on the way here. I warned you, this special technology is fragile equipment.
Come on, Lukash! We're professionals. Speaking of…
I'll transfer the coupons as soon as I make sure everything's in order.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_AL_NordBanditOne_A: Just wanted to ask. Are we gonna go, like, deep into SIRCAA? It's just that rumor has it the eggheads experimented on folks down there.
Nah, I don't! But hell knows what those eggheads were really up to. And those spooky experiments are probably still wandering around the laboratories… I just don't wanna risk it for nothing!
We only need the archive. I don't care about the laboratories.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_DLC01_dzen_0_Defea: Dude, I'm hit! Help me out!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_DLC01_dzen_0_InfoT: The Zone remembers everything it has seen. And when the time comes, it will tell it all to somebody.
That's why investigating here is easier than on the Mainland. Starting wars is easier, too.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_DLC01_karma_0_ByeT: Run, I'll give you a head start!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_DLC01_karma_0_Defe: Damn, he got me! Need a medkit!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_DLC01_karma_0_Info: Listen carefully – here's how you make a hostage do whatever you need without having to promise anything in return.
Just tell him all about what you'll do to him if he doesn't cooperate, but don't tell him what you'll do if he does.

His little mind will come up with all sorts of things to fill in the blank, like that we'll give him a ton of money if he helps us, then send him home to mommy. But it's not on you because you didn't promise him anything!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_DLC01_karma_0_Resu: One more time, like you mean it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_DLC01_suslov_0_Bus: I won't be much help at the moment.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_DLC01_suslov_0_Hel: I'll tell you everything you ask.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_DLC01_suslov_0_Inf: There is no danger in the Zone that science hasn't made even worse.
Just learn your lesson, know when to stop! But no, they insist on stirring up this massive, anomalous hornet's nest, thinking, "What can go wrong?"
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_DLC01_suslov_0_Res: So, where were we... Ah, right.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_DLC01_urka_snyr_0_: Not in the mood for this.
All the best. But not at my expense.
These days, I have less and less desire to go beyond Sultansk.
The train of bright thoughts went off the rails.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_DLC01_vova_lepila_: I'm not in the mood for... anything.
What's the deal with you stalkers? You must be batshit insane to just decide to leap into an anomaly. Ain't no payday in the world worth that!
So... where the hell were we?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_BanditOne_OnInt: Fucking mercs. No way I'm signing up for their jobs ever again!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_BanditTwo_OnInt: Yeah, not something I can brag about back at the Sultansk.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_Bandits_Archive: Ian, what's up, buddy? You still kicking?
If you can hear me, get your ass down to the archive. Karma's mad and needs a hand. Should be one floor below you.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_Bandits_Centrif: Sup? Ian said anything? He was supposed to give me a heads-up about that second elevator, but I've heard nothing.
Tokha, pretty please – shut the fuck up. Are you in the archive yet?
Then call him yourself! If his ass didn't fall from the centrifuge pulling those levers, he should pick up.
How are you doing over there? Are we getting that power up soon?
We are, Tokha, we are. Just not right this second.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_Dzen_OnInteract: You stick to your business, and I'll stick to mine.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_MavkaAfterTalk_: I can feel that negotiations with the mercs will either start with a firefight, or end with one.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_MavkaSuslov_Tal: Got a question for you, Doctor...
Suslov. Go ahead. And drop the 'doctor.' I haven't even finished my Master's.
Same here. Though I'm not a scientist.
Who would’ve thought that being a scientist was such a dangerous job?
You'd be surprised. All my misfortunes in the Zone came when I was a man of science. Being a man of trade is an entirely different story.
Well, I'm not so sure. Back at Rostok, selling stuff is more dangerous than running off to Prypiat.
Am I familiar with any of the things you invented? You Zone scientists are always making stuff for stalkers. Take Hercules, for instance!
I don't think you are. That one and only time I tried to create something significant, enhancing the anti-psi pill, it turned into an absolute disaster.
That means your great discovery is still waiting for you!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_Mavka_OnInterac: Don't worry about the scientist, I'll get him out. Head outside. Maybe Zulu will try to reach you!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_Mercenaries_Tal: Deal with it. We can't leave any witnesses.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_RadioCallToSkad: Skif, Zulu here. Sorry I was off the comms for so long. Mavka and I were trying to find who set Duty up in the Iron Forest.
We're finally on to some real suspects here. Come to the Sultansk, we could use your help!
Unfortunately, time's not on our side. Over and out.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_RadioCall_Skado: Skif, Zulu here. Got some news. Looks like we found the ones who set Duty up in the Iron Forest.
Come over to the Sultansk ASAP, we need your help here. Zulu and Mavka out!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_SircaaBandits_C: Stalker, stalker, don't shoot! We've had enough already!
Better help us out with some medkits!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_Suslov_ArchiveC: Stalker, are you good? I'm here. Come on over, and let's chat.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_Suslov_OnIntera: I thought it would be my last day in the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_Suslov_ToHimsel: Well, the archive suggests SIRCAA's funding was quite sufficient.
When I was younger, I would've given anything to have access to this.
And now, after getting pushed around by Karma, I can't even look at classified files.
I need a moment to pull myself together. Got to figure out if there's anywhere in the Zone where Nord's people won't reach me.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_TalkOnSkadovsk_: Have you been there after the incident?
You know I've had no time. Otherwise, I'd have been the first one to sneak in. All sorts of people have already tried, even bandits.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QC_ZulusSkif_CallC: Come in! I chased down the merc who survived, but he's keeping his mouth shut. Have you found out anything?
The mercs are looking for the entrance into the Bubble spatial anomaly. It has the technology they're after, and it's all somehow connected to the details of Tachenko's death.
I know where Nord is headed. We need to get to Tachenko's memorial. We put it up where the general's body fell out of the Bubble. And the entrance to the anomaly might be where the exit is.
Whatever technology the mercenaries are after, we have to stop them. We'll meet up there. And Skif, while you have the chance, get ready. It's about to get serious.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_FastTravel_1_86: Zen can take you. It would certainly be faster. Ready to go?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_FastTravel_ByMy: Thanks, but I can get there myself.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_FastTravel_Wont: Good! I'll let Zen know - he hasn't signed up for this yet, ha-ha.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_MavkaArchive_IF: The mercenaries took a hostage, Suslov, to help them find information on how to enter the Bubble and get some kind of special technology from it. He's a former scientist.
Good thing you were there to help him. He'll be our witness when we take the proof to Myklukha and Voronin.
About the proof. Have you dug anything up?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_MavkaArchive_Ma: Phew, Skif! It’s good to see you’re alive.
The meet at the Sultansk went to shit, of course. The mercs started shooting off the bat, we barely made it. One of them slipped away, so Zulu had to follow him.

He said he'd call when he found out anything. But regular radio can't get through to SIRCAA, so I decided to come warn you myself. And give you a hand if you need one. But you seem to have already figured it out.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_MavkaArchive_Yo: Take a look at this. You'll find it interesting.
Stop. I don't understand. Lukash associated with mercenaries that killed our people in the Iron Forest? But why? What technology was he working with?
This must be why they killed Lukash. We must find out what it is and how it functions. The merc mentioned some stashes, and Lukash shared the locations of a couple of them. We need to check them out.

Let me take care of our new friend here, get him somewhere safe. He looks like he really needs it. Once I'm done, I'll need your help with checking the stashes out. I'll send you the coordinates later!
All I know is that the mercs don't have it yet because they're still on a hunt. They're even willing to risk exploring a spatial anomaly to get it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_MavkaSkadovsk_A: So, Skif? Are you going to take care of this? Will you check out if there are mercs at SIRCAA and what they're looking for?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_MavkaZulusSkado: Why didn't you contact me earlier? Have you been investigating this whole time?
We didn't wanna bother you until we knew something for sure.
Yes. For Mavka and I, there was no choice whether to investigate or not. While I'm sure you had your hands full. Especially when Monolith started showing up on every corner.
But what we're about to do now is important. We can't do it without you.
What do you have on these mercs?
Mavka and I showed the emblem and patch to different people who trade in information. But we didn't think to ask anyone at the Sultansk. We're not used to working with bandits.
Then, Zen told us to go and ask Owl. We found out this insignia is used by mercs who – bingo! – sometimes shop for new recruits at the Sultansk.
Last time they recruited bandits was for a run at SIRCAA. Before that, the Iron Forest.
Sounds like a plan. I'll get on it.
What we really need is to find out what's up. Be careful. It's best to go there at night, but you decide. And stay on comms.
We knew we could count on you!
Why do the mercs need SIRCAA? Whatever the Ward didn't have the time to take from the ruins, was probably looted by loners.
We don't know, Skif. The locals weren't able to tell us much, either. Bandits aren't at all curious when it comes to these matters, unless they were promised money.
I bet this is connected to whatever Lukash was up to.
Are the mercs your only suspects?
The IPSF had no reason to kill Freedom members or set Duty up. Bandits alone couldn't take our guys down. And we already crossed Duty off from the list of suspects.
Yeah, sure, there's always a chance that a Ward or Spark squad happened to be there and somehow decided to wipe out Kurin.
But first, it was only the mercs who had a camp out there, and second, they already killed a Freedom member before. Lukash.
Skif! I'll get right to the point, okay? Zulu and I were able to find out who killed the Freedom members and put an end to D4!
Mercs. I had my suspicions right away. But they are always split into small groups, it was almost impossible to tell which one we were dealing with.
The patch and the PDA you gave us in the Iron Forest came in really useful, but we can't prove anything without solid evidence. If anything, we'd just make it worse.
I need to think about it first.
I understand.
Just don't take too long. The clock's ticking!
Is it just the two of you? Or is anyone else helping you out?
Mostly, it's just us, though Zen butts in from time to time. There aren't that many people willing to investigate something they don't consider a mystery.
Almost everyone in Freedom, except for Zen, blames Duty. They blame me, a little, too – for being out scouting with a Duty soldier while Freedom members were getting killed.
While Duty is sure it was a setup. Proof won't do much there anyway as no one will believe it.
So are Duty and Freedom actually at war?
Hmm, how to say it… Yes, D4 has been terminated. There are clashes, but no large group-on-group ones. And none are expected in the near future, knock on wood.
Which is pretty good for us. If Voronin openly declared Freedom as an enemy, it would've been almost impossible to investigate anything.
Yeah. At least for now we won't get shot right away if they find out we're working together.
What exactly do you need my help with?
We need to find ironclad proof that it was the mercenaries who started the bloodbath at Kurin. And find out why.
Owl promised us a meeting with the owners of those patches. He did say the outcome would be our responsibility. So, before they get here, we can't leave the Sultansk.
We need you to go check out SIRCAA. We're not sure when they'll get there, but if they've arrived already, find out what they're looking for.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_MeetDzen_1_8014: Slow down, amigo. The way forward is special invite only.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_SircaaBandits_E: Take the medkits and get out of here.
No problem, we're outta here already!
And, uh, loner… if you wanna get into SIRCAA, stick to the high ground and wait for the water to drop. You could fucking drown, just like that.
I have no reason to trust bandits. Or waste any medkits on you.
If you don't wanna do this the easy way, we'll do it the hard way!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_SircaaBandits_H: Have you seen that group of mercs before? Worked with them?
Nah, we haven't, but it sure wasn't the first time they came to the Sultansk.
Yeah. Mercs usually recruit at the Slag Heap. They aren't really regulars at our place.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_SircaaBandits_N: I don't have any medkits on me.
Great. Thanks for jack shit. Damn it, loner! Get outta here, we got enough trouble.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_SircaaBandits_W: So did you find a way in?
Looks like the mercs did. I almost drowned halfway. We're lucky they just left us here and didn't finish us off. One of them even said they would, the fucking shitface!
His boss didn't let him. Said it's no use wasting ammo.
What do mercs want with SIRCAA? What are they after?
Their boss, Nord, said they needed the local archive. I didn't ask why, and he's not exactly the talkative type.
They brought this old guy with them, too, but didn't make him go into the anomaly. They just kept him close, at gunpoint. Like he was useful.
That's all we know. Gimme the medkits, loner, it freaking hurts!
What are you up to in the SIRCAA ruins?
We signed up for this job for the mercs! They said there was lots of equipment just sitting around at SIRCAA. That we could sell it for a decent amount! And we fell for it.
They just used us like lab rats! Sent us to go look for a way in. Yurko was hit by an anomaly right away. I headed back, only to be hit with a gun barrel. Had no choice but to look for that entrance.
So you decided to become stalkers? Since when did bandits start crawling through anomalies?
Gotta crawl through worse things to survive, loner.
Spare a medkit, will ya, loner? Please?
Yeah! We'll get patched up and beat it, for real.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_SuslovArchive_A: Do you have any idea why Nord picked you for this mission? The Zone seems to have a lot of scientists.

I asked him the same question, but to no avail. Why did it have to be me and not somebody else? I'm sure he could have found a scientist willing to cooperate with the mercenaries without being forced.
At first, I thought it might have somehow been connected to my work at Clear Sky. But I suspect it had to do with something different.

My research specialization was anomalous energy. Nord was extremely confident that I could deal with this special technology that he needed – and that means its function was somehow connected to my area of expertise.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_SuslovArchive_M: Thank you. I don't know who you are or why you're here, but you saved my life. And I don't even have coupons to repay you.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_SuslovArchive_N: No, thank you. They didn't hurt me. For my illness, a medkit's no help.
I'm highly sensitive to loud noises. Sometimes, a single gunshot is enough to cause a headache, and no medicine can bring me relief. Only time does. And silence.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_SuslovArchive_S: Nord actually wanted me to help him find out more about that special technology, and after we'd found it, to take care of setting it up.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_SuslovArchive_T: What were you doing here? What were the mercs after?
Nord was interested in both how Tachenko, the founder of Duty, died, and in spatial anomalies. One of them, the Bubble, contains a special technology that he's after.
He took me to the archive with him so I could help find the information. I tried to sabotage the search, but Karma's methods were… quite persuasive.
What do mercs want with the founder of Duty and his death?
Oh, Tachenko's death is directly connected to the spatial anomalies. He and his men disappeared without a trace on their last run.
And then, after a long time, they fell out of the Bubble. Dead. They had been still alive when they got in there, but how and under what circumstances, nobody knows.
What is the special technology that Nord is after?
I… I don't know for sure. I only know that General Tachenko had set out on a search for it before he fell off the radar.
How did you end up with the mercs?
Involuntarily. They held me hostage because they thought I was still a practicing scientist. That hasn't been the case for a very, very long time.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_SuslovArchive_W: Do you know where the mercenaries were headed next?

I'm afraid I do. They got all the data they needed from the archive, so they must be on their way to the Bubble and planning to enter it. Although, I have no idea where they might be looking for the entrance.

If you decide to follow their group, watch your back. From what I understand, Nord isn't doing all this for nothing. He's out for revenge against anyone who crossed the mercenaries. And he'll stop at nothing.
You don't want to be in this man's bad books. Although… I guess it's too late for either of us to worry about that.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ04_QD_ZulusAfterTalk_: What were you up to after you took off with Voronin?
I told Voronin about what we found at the Testing Workshop, about the Blast source. I tried to explain why I didn't leave with the others.
He said I'd have the opportunity to explain everything that's happened in a formal written report. And that he wasn't interested in listening to excuses.
I'd prefer Voronin just being mad at me. I expected additional duties, a reprimand, whatever, but nothing followed except for some changes to my work schedule.
I used to think I hated the whole Zone, all of it equally. But after the Kurin bloodbath, the Iron Forest is top of the list.
What's your take on Myklukha and his speech in the Iron Forest?
I never liked Myklukha. He talks a lot, but he's holding back even more.
But no matter what I think of him, he did have every right to demand to interrogate me. If my people were killed, I'd have done the same.
Does Voronin even know you're here?
No. And he doesn't seem worried about it. It's like I'm on my own now.
I was taken off all the patrols I used to be in charge of, and not put on any new ones. It's as if Voronin's totally given up on me.
I'm not complaining, though. This gives me enough time to investigate.
Why did you take up the investigation with Mavka if you know for sure it wasn't Duty's fault?
First, because people died. The fact that people die in the Zone every day doesn't make stuff like this normal.
Second, these were Mavka's people. Be as it may, they did let us into Kurin and gave us a roof over our heads. That alone is reason enough for me to help her.
Third, no one in the Zone knows this isn't Duty's fault. Voronin doesn't see fit to make excuses. For me, the faction's reputation is more important than my pride.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ06_AL_Cepurnyi_LastRe: Day… I don't know what day it is. Still wandering around this doomed town.
There's no escape. This Lymansk is constantly changing. Someone's watching me, roaring in the dark. Not a regular mutant. Smarter. It's playing with me.
But I won't return to Tachenko – the general has lost it completely. Bunchuk stayed with him, that suck-up…
That beast is getting closer again. I should try another route to the east side. Maybe, there…
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ06_AL_Cepurnyi_Radiow: Found it… Top floor, connected to that object. Tachenko won't let anyone near it, he's walking around in circles, thinking. I don't like the look on his face…
The general lost it completely. "The last line"? Damn it! What's that even supposed to mean?! That we're stuck here forever?!
Kosmach wanted to shut the damn thing down. The anomaly would get destroyed, he said, and we'd be outta here. But Bunchuk ratted us out. Fucker…
Tachenko shot Kosmach on the spot. Right in the face, in cold blood. I'm fucking outta here. Alone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ06_AL_Chekhov_Archive: I'm not much of a scientist. If it wasn't for the Doctor's additional instructions, I never would've built anything here. But… it seems to be working. Now I just have to launch it.
The institute, of course, wasn't built for this. We need something with a larger capacity if we want to use this on the Mainland. And we will.
Duty's general is following me, and he's not alone. I hope my plan works. I hope I can manage to launch this thing on time and not blow it.
The Zone, and then the whole world, will be liberated.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ06_AL_Duty_Dictaphone: Is it recording? I want to… leave something behind.
I should've stopped him back then. We were the only ones left from our squad. The two of us, a bunch of paperwork and that… device. I thought it was clear what we should've done.
I thought wrong. I saw death, horrors that needed to be destroyed. While he saw freedom. A tool.
You asked what we were doing here for real? Righting my wrong. My poor judgement and my blind confidence. I won't make the same mistake again. I no longer have the right to.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ06_AL_Tachenko_1_8604: ... whichever way we, go we always end up in the same exact spot. I still can't get used to this fog... It's weird... That Chepurny disappeared, without a trace. Strange. Maybe he found a way out?...
Day six, we have run out of water... The Colonel flipped his lid, shot two people at point blank range, and then himself... Now I'm on my own in this damn anomaly...

If I hadn't fixed for our communications with HQ to go down. They could have rescued us. Retirement, country house, fishing — and Duty wouldn't have existed. I wonder how things would have turned out.
Ah, screw it. That Captain Tachenko died a long time ago...
And this General Tachenko of Duty will follow him...
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ06_QC_Cepurnyi_Corrid: "This is my duty, Major". Duty?! To whom?! To what?! When I was leaving, he gave me this look, like I was a traitor. A traitor!
But I didn't betray anyone. I was the one who was betrayed! He decided to lock us all up here, fucking bastard!
I should look for a way around from the west…
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ06_QC_Duty_Apartments: Get back! Get back and take cover!
Quiet! It attacks when it hears us! Fall back. Quick!
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ06_QC_Duty_Balcony_1_: Bunchuk, what's the hold-up? We need to keep moving.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ06_QC_Duty_BehindTheW: All clear. Chepurny, where are we at?
I think I figured out which way we should go, but I lost the entry point – the area behind us has changed already.
So mark the way. Our priority is to find the object. Clear?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ06_QC_Duty_CampState1: Storm squad ready to secmove out. Search radius – residential block, east of the camp.
Okay. Stick to the plan. The priority is to find ammunition and medical supplies.
Roger that, General. What about provisions?
We have enough food supplies for now. We'll worry about that if we stay here longer than two weeks.
Comms check every 15 minutes. At the slightest indication of fog, turn back immediately.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_phrase_DLC01_MQ06_QC_Duty_CampState2: The apartment sweep is complete. We're moving forward to the west blocks.
