ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E06_MQ01_Card_de: This old green key card is a bit scratched, but the magnetic strip seems to be intact. It should probably still work.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E06_MQ01_CryptoK: The key to the back room in the Cryptobiology Lab, kept by a lab technician who hid in a cage to escape rampaging mutants.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E06_MQ01_SciMaga: A clipping from an article in a prominent scientific journal. Found in Dr. Dalin’s penthouse.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E06_MQ01_ZombieN: A tattered tag, taken off a zombie at the Cryptobiology Lab.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E06_MQ03_DalinDa: A high-tech flash drive that contains comprehensive data on recent SIRCAA research, including the experiment in Lab X11.
Flash Drive with the SIRCAA Archive
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_EQ01_Zelenyj: Damaged during the battle with Monolith, this PDA contains a recording that sheds light on the reasons behind the stalker’s desperate act.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_MQ01_Fuse_de: An essential component that protects devices from the impact of voltage fluctuations.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_MQ01_HorsPDA: A PDA belonging to the Noontide technician. It looks like it was just unboxed yesterday. Khors was meticulous about everything.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_MQ01_SinajAu: The device contains a single recording, seemingly made right before the Signal.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_MQ01_SkiperP: This old, but reliable PDA was owned by a mercenary who was working on Wild Island for an unknown client.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_MQ01_TihiyDo: A regular graph paper notebook filled with Quiet’s sprawling handwriting, detailing his business transactions.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_MQ02_PripoyK: A small metal key received from Solder.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_MQ02_SyhinOf: An official document bearing the signature of the IPSF commander.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_MQ02_SyhinPD: An ordinary military-grade PDA, although its owner turned out not to be the person he was pretending to be.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_MQ02_SyhinSt: Captain Sukhin’s medical records, found in his office at the Sphere.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_MQ03_Archive: A voice recorder with an illegible inventory number containing an archival recording by Dr. Orlov.
Voice Recorder Labeled with an Inventory Number
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_MQ03_Control: This device can be used to control and transmit data within the X-Network. When installed in a communication node, it grants limited control over network elements.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_MQ03_SciDict: A nondescript voice recorder containing a report from an unidentified agent.
Recording of an Unknown Agent from Promin CMD Factory, pt. 1
A nondescript voice recorder containing a report from an unidentified agent.
Recording of an Unknown Agent from Promin CMD Factory, pt. 2
A nondescript voice recorder containing a report from an unidentified agent.
Recording of an Unknown Agent from Promin CMD Factory, pt. 3
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_PsyEmitter_d: The device used to transmit the Signal. Despite its compact size, the radiation it releases is so intense that conventional psi-defenses are unable to counteract it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_SQ01_LinzaPD: This PDA found in Lens’s workshop has a large crack across the screen. Its owner must have dropped it during the uneven battle against the Monolithians.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_SQ01_MPDA_Da: The Monolithians under Uncle Lyonya’s command used this shabby M-PDA to receive their orders. The former guide and protector of rookies in Zalissya was apparently determined to destroy everyone who trusted him.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_SQ01_NoteFor: A note on a scrap of paper, left by a grateful rookie on Uncle Lyonya’s desk. Little did the rookie know that the former Zalissya guide would turn out to be a Monolithian…
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E07_SQ01_Surgery: Carefully wrapped in a soft cloth, these scalpels and clamps look pristine and razor sharp.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_DvupolovReco: The professor’s pocket voice recorder, containing Dvupalov’s sessions with his test subject. The device was left abandoned in the cell – more of a cage, really.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_EQ01_CollarB: Stained with dried blood on the inside and scratched on the outside, this massive electronic collar must have been uncomfortably tight for an adult specimen, so the mutant tried to peel it off.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_EQ02_CollarS: This collar appears brand new except for the partially destroyed tag. What little remains legible reads “Test sub…”
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_EQ02_DenyaBy: This PDA looks pretty battered, but it fared much better than its unfortunate owner.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_EQ03_CollarB: A metal device showing minor damage, as if it had been grazed by a bullet fired at the mutant.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_EQ03_KrikPDA: A PDA retrieved from the body of the hunter Yevhen Mamay’s body containing exchanges with Viktoria Dorozhnyuk, his client at Malachite. Looks like Mamay will never get to make his move after all.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ01_Activat: A small sheet with a memo on activating the Mirror VPC. Maybe its late owner wanted to see what would happen if he broke the rules.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ01_Desiato: A document containing Desyatov’s formal request for transfer. Evidently, it’s tough to work under someone you don’t get along with.
A voice recorder containing Desyatov’s notes. It appears that prior to his involvement, the staff at Mirror VPC was pretty lax about safety precautions.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ01_Phantom: The print on these instructions from the Mirror VPC has faded slightly over the years. Given its condition, it was probably a hit among the local scientists.
Protocol for Dealing with Induced Illusions
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ01_Razumov: A voice recorder containing the notes of Prof. Razumovsky, reflecting his genuine passion for his work.
A voice recorder containing Prof. Razumovsky’s later notes. It’s impossible to say for sure whether his visions were merely residual induced illusions, or something more profound.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ01_TruePha: Written in a shaky hand, this crumpled note is abruptly cut off at the end. Evidently, the person who wrote it was suffering from residual induced illusions originating from the Mirror VPC.
Real Protocol for Dealing with Induced Illusions
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ01_TuningI: A document outlining the protocols for communication within X-Network facilities. It looks like the scientists were exchanging a truly massive amount of data.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ03_Collars: This faded paper provides evidence of mutant experiments at Lab X5. The “Project Leash” label is barely legible.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ03_ConrolR: A key to the control room of Lab X5’s experimental area.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ03_Dvupalo: A worn-out leather-bound notebook. Someone frequently consulted these notes, even after the professor had left the lab.
One of the recordings is set on repeat. It's labeled “Prof. Dvupalov, 2006.”
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ03_Keycard: The key card for Lab X5, located beneath Ahroprom. Miraculously, it’s still functional after all these years.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ03_LetterF: Classified documents found in Lab X5. The laboratory apparently continued to operate under the direction of MOST after it was officially closed.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ03_ListWar: A note from Dvupalov’s desk at X5.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ03_Recepti: A note from Lab X5, stained with dried blood. It’s unclear whether the recipient managed to carry out the instructions.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ03_SciArti: It’s hard to fathom which scientific journal would have accepted this kind of research for publication.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ03_SherbaT: A draft of a message addressed to Prof. Dvupalov, composed by a graduate student named Shcherba. It looks like someone is completely unable to let go.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ03_Strelok: Strelok’s old PDA. He went to his stash before making the decision to leave the Zone. Judging from the recording, the stalker had dealt a substantial blow to the Ward and intended to come back and finish the job.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ03_Suppres: The schematics for the Suppressor, a device designed to hinder the psi abilities of mutants.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ04_Explosi: A container packed with high-powered military explosives.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_MQ04_Undergr: A small key card granting access to one of the engineering rooms in the underground section of the Duga.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_SQ01_KardanD: An old PDA displaying an incoming late-night call. The timing of the call suggests that something important was going on.
Coated in a layer of dust, this PDA contains negotiations involving some kind of device.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E08_SQ01_Kartezh: This worn-out PDA contains messages between a stalker and a scientist involved in something big.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E10_MQ01_ArhipPD: The lack of concern shown by this PDA’s owner implies that buying a replacement was likely not a problem for him.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E10_MQ01_LeaderP: Wolfhound left this PDA in an abandoned village. He clearly intended to come back for it, but it wasn't meant to be.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E10_MQ01_SiviyPD: A bloodstained PDA belonging to a stalker called Gray, found in a clearing in the Red Forest. Recovering it was easier than expected.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E10_MQ01_TundraP: Even as he was dying, he tried to warn others about the danger. He must’ve been a good man. Just goes to show you that good people don’t last long in the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E10_MQ01_Volkoda: This PDA contains nothing but a set of coordinates recently transmitted to an undisclosed recipient.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E10_MQ01_YarlPDA: A somewhat battered PDA. It must have endured some tough times during its owner’s last stand.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E10_MQ02_Monolit: A small sheet of paper providing a summary of the current state of affairs at the Monolith infirmary.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E10_MQ02_OldPDA_: A well-worn M-PDA, rarely used and frequently lost in various locations.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E10_MQ02_PDABrod: An M-PDA retrieved from the body of the former leader of Noontide. He wanted to build a new future on Wild Island, but his Monolithian past caught up with him.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E10_MQ02_Regener: A medical device used by Monolithians to treat injured soldiers.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ01_Cartrid: A small storage drive containing data from the signature station. It can only be read on a compatible device.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ01_Deciphe: This electronic lockpick seems capable of unlocking the door to the abandoned science lab in the Cordon.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ01_Stalker: This PDA’s deceased owner found the new Oasis after all. However, as is often the case in the Zone, it wasn’t what it seemed. Unfortunately, a malfunction has rendered the stalker’s name illegible.
PDA of a Stalker from X3
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ01_Tracker: A tiny gadget containing the coordinates to the entrance to Lab X3 at the Cordon.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ02_2ndKaym: Notes from Dr. Kaymanov found at Orbita Station.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ02_3rdKaym: Notes from Dr. Kaymanov found at Orbita Station.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ02_Audiolo: This worn, dusty recorder contains a copy of a conversation between Scar and Prof. Ozersky.
Recording of a Conversation Between Scar and Ozersky
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ02_CodeToB: A memo outlining guidelines for the station’s managerial staff.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ02_InstAnt: Handwritten instructions for restarting the antenna at Orbita Station.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ02_Kaymano: Notes from Dr. Kaymanov found at Orbita Station.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ02_KeyCard: A key card to the entrance of Lab X15.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ03_PTSthre: A yellowed and dusty report from the Troposphere Comm Station, filled out in neat handwriting. The author, whoever they were, took great care in their work.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ04_DoorKey: A key to the cell in the detention center, given by Dalin. Without the doctor’s aid, escaping the Chemical Plant seemed nearly impossible.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ04_PDA_Che: Chornozem’s PDA, found in a warehouse at the Chemical Plant. Apparently, there was more to the bandit than meets the eye.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ04_PDA_Nes: Nestor’s PDA, found in a warehouse at the Chemical Plant. The former Garbage kingpin apparently had the backing of someone even more important than the Ward.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E11_MQ04_Protoco: At first glance, this file of documents found in the infirmary of the Chemical Plant appears totally unremarkable. However, the papers inside are clearly not meant for prying eyes.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E12_MO01_DuhToRi: A short message on a crumpled piece of paper.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E12_MO01_GroupsN: A sheet containing an annotated list of names, found in Spirit’s bunker. There were probably many others like it, but only this sheet has survived.
List of People Crossing the Boundary
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E12_MO01_Instruc: A sheet of paper with instructions for the device. Looks like it was used as a coaster.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E12_MO01_PDAOzer: A surprisingly neat PDA in almost pristine condition that somehow found its way into Spirit’s belongings. It only contains a single exchange with a colleague.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E12_MO01_PhotoIs: This crumpled photo must be a precious memento for its owner.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E12_MQ01_DuhStas: The scuffed surface of this magnetic key card suggests it has seen frequent use.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E12_MQ01_PDADuh_: This unassuming PDA contains a message with some crucial information.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E12_MQ01_SkanerM: A modified scanner capable of temporarily disabling anomalies. It can be operated by anyone who has read the manual.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E14_MQ01_Coordin: A PDA containing a scanned map of the Foundation underground military facility. One of the rooms has been circled three times with a ballpoint pen.
PDA with a Map of Prypiat Military Facilities
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E14_MQ01_Helicop: An aged and partially damaged flash drive. Despite its appearance, it still works, preserving confidential data on Operation Fairway.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E14_MQ01_Laundro: A miraculously preserved fragment found in the Laundromat. The paper has faded over the years, but the names of the rescued Stingray group members are still legible.
Papers from Former HQ in Prypiat
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E14_MQ01_Promete: A PDA showing signs of damage after a pitched battle with mutants. It contains coordinates for the locations where Spark’s main force could be heading with the scanned archive in tow.
Dead Sparker’s PDA from the Prometheus
A PDA showing signs of damage from an encounter with mutants. It contains coordinates for the locations where the Ward’s main force could be heading with the recovered documents in tow.
Dead Warden’s PDA from the Prometheus
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E14_MQ01_SCAT7Fl: A flash drive recovered from the wreckage of Stingray-7. The group was apparently searching for an entrance to the Foundation underground facility, but the helicopter crashed before they could transmit their discoveries to HQ.
Flash Drive with Coordinates to Foundation Entrances
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E14_MQ02_MobileB: Grants entry to the Mobile Bunkers.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E14_MQ02_Tunnels: Unlocks the entrance to the underground tunnels that lead to the Foundation.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E15_MQ03_Cartrid: A small storage drive. It can only be read on a compatible device.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E15_MQ03_Project: These scribbled drafts are full of revisions and crossed-out sections. Whose work is this, and who was it intended for?
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E16_AgentsFile_A: The archive encompasses hundreds of files detailing every agent recruited by C-Consciousness. For years, these people operated in the Zone and beyond, unknowingly carrying out instructions they were programmed to execute. The list includes a number of familiar names.
Archive of Files on C-Consciousness Agents
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E16_MQ01_PDA_Sca: A PDA taken from Scar’s corpse in the Neurolaboratory. He went to the Generators looking for the Shining Zone, but all he found there was death.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E16_MQ02_Marshal: A PDA belonging to a long-dead member of the original Spark. C-Consciousness used its owner’s memories as the basis for a new identity.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E16_MQ03_4thKaym: Notes from Dr. Kaymanov found in his office at Lab X7.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E16_MQ03_5thKaym: Notes from Dr. Kaymanov found in his office at Lab X7.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E16_MQ03_6thKaym: Notes from Dr. Kaymanov found in his office at Lab X7.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E16_MQ03_Caribbe: Old scientific papers outlining the experiment that confirmed the Noosphere theory. These records paved the way to the Zone’s emergence.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E16_MQ03_Cartrid: A small storage drive. It can only be read on a compatible device.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E16_MQ03_Instruc: An old instruction sheet covered with handwritten notes in red pencil.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E16_MQ03_KeyKard: An old key card, once the property of Lt. Col. Korshunov. It grants the highest level of clearance, which is necessary to enter Lab X7.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_E16_MQ03_Strelok: By the look of this PDA, it faithfully served Strelok for many a year. The most important entry deals with the procedure for recording a psi-signature.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ08_FreshBread_: Soft and crispy, with the lingering smell of the oven. How on earth Myklukha gets fresh bread to the Zone is anyone’s guess, but it’s only available in Rostok.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ109_MarikTopot: A PDA from a stalker’s corpse, found in a crashed helicopter at the edge of the Burnt Forest. The harsh reality of the stalker life – the very thing Marik Stomper sought so eagerly proved to be much tougher than he anticipated.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ109_VitekLunaP: A PDA belonging to Vityok Moon, a bandit associated with the Sultan, who went on to start his own gang in the Burnt Forest. Just another wannabe king of the Zone who didn’t quite grasp that an imaginary crown won’t protect him from a bullet to the head.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ10_PastuhPDA_d: This veteran stalker’s PDA is full of messages and personal notes. One entry designates a stash location, along with a reminder to rig it with booby traps.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ110_DokaPDA_de: A PDA belonging to Dima Hotshot, a stalker who died near the school in the Burnt Forest. His search for the legendary Hermit’s stash was cut short by a mutant encounter. The Zone fiercely guards some of its most coveted secrets.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ110_HermitPDA_: A crumpled note written by veteran stalker Hermit. The warning left by the Zone seems to have scared him out of his wits. Found in the school at the edge of the Burnt Forest.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ111_KorkaPDA_d: This PDA belonged to a Freedom member who carelessly ignored the presence of mutants in his haste to recover some stolen goods. Found at the Krug Antenna Complex.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ118_DeadIskraP: A PDA belonging to a dead Sparker found near the checkpoint at the bridge in the Red Forest. It contains information about a mission given by Ozersky.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ11_NortonPDA_d: A PDA taken from Norton’s body. Based on his messages, it seems like he and his partner were arranging a mercenary hit on loners from the Cordon. Sidorovich might be interested in hearing about this.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ13_FilimonPDA_: This PDA belonged to a Freedom member who used it to conduct business. It holds some recent correspondence with a bandit who purchased the coordinates of a stash. For some, there are no friends or foes in the Zone – only a bottom line after accounting for income and expenses.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ13_MihaPDA_des: This PDA of a lone stalker stores a chat with a mercenary. The latter is ready to tell him who sold the weapon stash to the bandits and got Cowboy’s friends into trouble. Of course, in the Zone, any information has a price, but Mykha is ready to give up anything for a chance of revenge.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ140_IluhaVorob: This PDA belonged to a lone stalker who was seemingly plagued by perpetual misfortune. Unfortunately, his luck didn’t change this time. In a desperate attempt to regain the Zone’s favor, the stalker embarked on a dangerous adventure, only to learn that, unlike luck, death had no plans to pass him by.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ141_TurgaPDA_d: A PDA taken from the body of a stalker in the southern part of the Burnt Forest. It contains an audio recording that abruptly ends with gunshots and bloodcurdling screams.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ143_KolubPDA_d: Columbus’s PDA, found near the Vehicle Graveyard. Given the high radiation levels, his nearby stash should have been almost inaccessible. However, his ploy worked even better than intended: the Stalker himself succumbed to radiation poisoning. The Zone proves once again to be a dangerous and fickle ally.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ144_ArtemPodvo: A shattered PDA that belonged to Artyom Submariner. The screen is cracked, with notifications about unread messages still visible, but inaccessible. Someone with the right skills might be able to breathe life back into it or dismantle it for parts, but it’s of little use in its current state.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ144_GlazgoPDA_: A PDA taken from Glasgow’s corpse. After locking himself up, the stalker continued calling for help, only to realize that the dead man behind the door was his friend. Stumbling upon a fat stash, getting wasted, turning away a man seeking help during an Emission – this story could only have ended up badly. The Zone has punished people for far less.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ144_KucyjPDA_d: A PDA taken from Short's corpse. Locked in the basement by a stalker who died right on the other side of the door, he and his companions perished amid a mound of loot that proved worthless in their predicament. Short probably didn’t even have a chance to sober up.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ145KostaKonusN: A crumpled piece of paper found on the body of the scout Kostya Dry. It provides detailed observations on IPSF patrol routes. It looks like Spark is actively planning to infiltrate the Duga.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ146_MonolithPD: A Monolithian’s PDA containing a recording of Faust’s sermon. Even in death, the shepherd continues to lead his flock.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ148_KeyFromCon: Unlocks the old assembly hall located on the school’s second floor.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ148_KostasPDA_: A soldier’s PDA containing an audio recording. Seeking refuge in the school after Monolith seized the Duga, the group stumbled upon a deadly menace within. For Kostas, it was the last straw.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ150_NoteOtshel: Found in a small village at Yaniv, this note narrates a journey through the Red Forest. If these accounts are true, the path through the forest is fraught with danger, even for a stalker of Hermit’s ability.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ155_BromPDA_de: In his final exchange, Bromine boasts that he’s about to get his hands on the scientists’ stash as long as he can find the “corpse with the password.” It looks like the “corpse with the password” found him first.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ155_CollarCont: The metal collar has a tag on it with a barely visible inscription: “Test subject #48.” Someone wrote the number 24 next to it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ156_CaseBones_: A small suitcase found on the body of Zhenya Blizzard in the swamps of Ahroprom. It’s filled with human bones. The Sparker’s PDA could reveal the motive behind this gruesome collection.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ156_MorozPDA_d: A PDA belonging to a Sparker killed in the swamps near Ahroprom. In his final exchange, Zhenya Blizzard promises to deliver a suitcase full of bones to Viktoria Dorozhnyuk, a scientist from Malachite.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ161_kudravyjPD: A PDA belonging to a Sparker who set up an ambush at the X5 exit. The stalker wanted to seize Korshunov’s badge in order to sabotage the Ward, but the attempt ended in failure.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ163_PripoyFune: The writing on this sheet of notebook paper is unsteady, and the ink is partially smudged.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ165_TrachukPDA: The scientist's PDA contains exchanges with a Sparker named Trickster. He apparently trusted the guy and was intending to hand his research over to the Sparker. Sadly, his attempt to protect the discovery from the Ward ended in tragedy.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ165_USBTrachuk: A flash drive with the results of Trachuk’s research. The scientist went to great lengths to protect his data, even putting his own life at risk. This information must be very important indeed.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ166_ValerianPD: A PDA recovered from Father Valerian’s corpse near the Cooling Towers. If the messages are of any indication, Valerian’s group was already falling apart when he met his end at the hands of mutants.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ167_NoteOtshel: A note found on Hermit’s body in the Dead Valley. He was apparently ready for death, and embraced it without fear or regret.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ16_FaraPDA_des: The PDA of a stalker with the soul of a poet who cherished the Zone’s unique beauty. But even here, death is still horrible – Headlight can attest to that.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ26_EmptyFlashD: A flash drive found on Lefty’s body, marked “Property of STC Malachite. Please return to Viktoria Dorozhnyuk.” Lefty was apparently assigned to record the psi-radiation measurements on the drive.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ26_FlashDriveW: A flash drive found on Lefty’s body, marked “Property of STC Malachite. Please return to Viktoria Dorozhnyuk.” The drive contains psi-radiation measurements, so I can take it back to its owner.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ26_LevsaPDA_Al: A Sparker’s PDA containing data on psi-radiation measurements near Lake Yantar, along with messages from Viktoria Dorozhnyuk, a scientist from Malachite. I should take this PDA to her.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ26_LevsaPDA_de: A PDA belonging to Lefty a stalker exposed to psi-radiation near Lake Yantar. It contains correspondence with Viktoria Dorozhnyuk, a scientist from STC Malachite. Science demands sacrifices, and the Zone is always willing to oblige.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ29_TradeNote_P: The military’s terms for trading with the stalkers are blunt, but concise. These soldiers are posing as enforcers of the law, yet they constantly violate it themselves.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ30_DobryakPDA_: This PDA was retrieved by a stalker who found Jolly Azat’s corpse at the Ribs. It’s not much, but it’s better than disappearing into an anomaly forever.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ30_ReshkaPDA_d: A PDA belonging to a stalker who died at the Ribs, found by a nearby slab of concrete. Apparently Lyova had a bolt he kept as a lucky charm. He should have kept it on him when he went into that anomaly.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ30_TitunPDA_de: An old PDA found near the Ribs. It doesn't seem like anyone was especially broken up about the owner’s death.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ35_LegendAdvic: A note from Lex the Legend's "generous" stash. A first life lesson, of some sort: don't trust the loudmouths promising dope loot.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ35_LehaLegendP: A PDA belonging to Lex the Legend, AKA Snag. His correspondence reveals a well-prepared scam. Lex maneuvered into a position of influence while doing business directly with the kingpin. In the end, that didn’t help him very much.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ35_VolanNoteSh: A note found at the Flea Market, addressed to Lex the Legend. His ardent disciples swear to follow their idol through hell and high water. He seems to have them firmly in his grip.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ36_KucherPDA_d: A PDA belonging to a stalker who was paying his respects to his partner and mentor Tolik at the Cherevach village cemetery. Apparently this Tolik guy had some kind of history with the legendary Strelok. Unfortunately, anomalies don’t discriminate based on who you are or who you know.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ37_GromNote_de: Found by the Cage at the Cement Factory, this note lists the names of Hromovyi’s comrades-in-arms who fell during the First Raid – a time when Duty had yet to be established, and the captain held a rank far beneath his current stature.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ38_Instruction: Left in a backpack in the Poppy Field, this note asks the reader to leave spare energy drinks in the stash for anyone who might need them. An uncommon display of kindness in the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ38_ThanksNote_: A note found in the Poppy Field stash offering thanks to the anonymous benefactor who stocked it with energy drinks, ultimately saving the author’s life. Energy drinks might not be the healthiest beverage out there, of course, but they’ve got nothing on anomalies.
Note from the Energy Drink Stash
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ48_GiverPaper_: The author of the note bequeathed his stash to whoever finds it first. In the Zone, an occasional act of kindness like this can be more surprising than the most wondrous of miracles.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ51_TemaJetPDA_: A PDA retrieved from the body of a Duty member killed in Kopachi Village. The decision to split up to complete Zulu’s objectives cost the owner his life, and Duty lost yet another soldier, further depleting their already diminished ranks.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ52_PuzirPDA_de: This PDA was owned by Bubbs. He owed money to the Shah, so he went into an anomaly to secure an artifact and died there. By the standards of those indebted to the Shah, he got off easy.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ58_TimurMolcan: A PDA belonging to Goodwin, found in the Yantar underground. It contains records of a stalker’s unsuccessful bid to save a partner who turned into a zombie. As the saying goes, hope is the first step on the road to disappointment, but in this case, disappointment was just the beginning.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ60_PDAVovchik_: A PDA belonging to a rookie who refused to tell bandits where his stash is. Sadly, it didn’t save his life.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ64_MakisPDA_de: A PDA belonging to a stalker slain by mutants in the Lesser Zone. Like many rookies, he had big plans for the future. But, as the saying goes, “a stalker proposes, the Zone disposes.”
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ65AK74_descrip: A customized AKM-74U outfitted with a silencer and a collimator sight. Few of the loners haunting the Cordon can afford a gun like this.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ65LosPDA_descr: Found on a dead body by the Elevator, this PDA mentions a job from Sidorovich that the owner will never be able to complete. Guess I could take advantage of this and make some coupons.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ65PiavkaPDA_de: Several exchanges on this PDA suggest that dealing with Leech wasn’t a popular choice. Nevertheless, Stets always received prompt responses from his contacts within the IPSF.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ67UraKotPDA_de: A PDA belonging to a Freedom member whose unit was slaughtered by Monolith. The fear instilled by this terrifying group is so intense that even veteran Freedom soldiers hesitate to come to the aid of their comrades who fall prey to the fanatics.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ68_KubrakPDA_d: This PDA is pristine, without a single scratch on it. The device is either brand new, or its owner took exceptionally good care of it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ70_DeadBodyPda: A PDA belonging to a stalker who attempted to safeguard his stash using radiation signs. The ruse proved ineffective against the mutants, which mauled him to death.
PDA of a Stalker Killed by Mutants
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ73_EdikBaskaPD: A PDA belonging to a thug dressed as a Freedom member, probably affiliated with the Brood. He was in cahoots with Docent.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ74_Jitnichenko: A PDA belonging to a Malachite scientist. Zhytnychenko’s theories didn’t sit right with his supervisor, which resulted in the troublesome employee being sent out on a dangerous expedition. I guess when there’s a power struggle, scientists can be as ruthless as the bandits in Zaton.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ75AK74_descrip: An AKM-74S recovered from a trench near the Slag Heap.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ82_konserva_de: A swollen can of food, expired long before the Zone came into being. Without a decent gas mask, the stench is unbearable.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ84_LotPDA_desc: A PDA preserving the final words of Vasko Lot, who went missing on Wild Island. Guess he learned firsthand that the Zone’s gifts often come at a hefty price.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ85_MelPDA_desc: A PDA belonging to Stefko Tactician, found at the Pontoon Warehouse, where he met his end while looking for a stash with his associates. The audio log implies that their partnership did not pass the Emission test.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EQ92_TunnelPDA_d: A PDA belonging to a dead stalker containing a conversation with some unknown person. There’s a chance that this stranger might have had a role in the owner’s death.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_EchoE01_descript: With outdated electronic components and subpar usability, this basic artifact detector is only redeemed by its very modest price.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Electrocollar_de: A collar-shaped electronic device with inner metal electrodes designed to make direct contact with the wearer’s neck.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_FaustData_descri: Taken from the body of Faust, the Voice of the Monolith. This object is made from an unknown substance and has a mysterious hi-tech device embedded within it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_FaustPDA_descrip: Found on the Preacher’s dead body, this M-PDA exposes Faust’s years of scheming to bring the Monolith back. Through this device, the Monolithians received orders that ruined hundreds of lives.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_FreshBread_descr: Soft and crispy, with the lingering smell of the oven. How on earth Myklukha gets fresh bread to the Zone is anyone’s guess, but it’s only available in Rostok.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_GontaPDA_descrip: Honta's PDA – a hunter from Zaton who set up a school for rookies. Looks like he set up a job market for future hunters, too.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_GunTOZ_Gonta_des: A popular hunting shotgun. Very cheap and affordable, and much more effective against mutants than a pistol.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Himzavod_Hub_Not: A report on a sheet of 8x12 paper. Given the illegible handwriting, its author was likely a medic.
A sheet of handwritten text. Even the letters themselves seem to stand at attention.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_IKAR_PikmanPDA_d: A standard military-grade PDA. The device is somewhat hard to activate – the button requires a slightly longer and firmer press than usual.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Icon_description: An old family heirloom, likely left behind during the evacuation in 1986. This item has no place in the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Inductor_descrip: A device for decrypting messages on old Monolith PDAs. Requires a connection to Azimuth Station. This model has been phased out.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_KozimkovPDA_desc: A PDA belonging to the commander of the Ward’s Bravo Team, containing a distress signal from Echo Station along with its coordinates.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_KuziaPDA_descrip: A PDA belonging to Kuzya, a bandit with a knack for fleecing “rich suckers” from Rostok. In the messages, he flaunts his lavish lifestyle and urges his buddy to join his venture, contributing to a shared stash at specified coordinates. In the Zone, survival comes first, but once you’ve survived, it’s time to turn a profit.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_LeshiyPDA_descri: A PDA belonging to a bandit called Leshy, who was hiding at the Supply Depot. Looks like he overestimated himself and turned from hunter to prey. Well, should’ve prepared better to take on the kingpin.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_MaksSubbotaPDA_d: The PDA of a stalker from the Lesser Zone, a member of Mastiff’s group who made his living by robbing the stashes of dead stalkers.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_MalahitElevatorK: A key that opens the elevator to X17.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Malahit_Hub_Note: A crumpled printout found at Malachite. Its contents clearly caused great offense to the recipient.
Written Reply to a Request for Collaboration
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Malahit_KeyCard_: Presenting this access card guarantees easy entry to STC Malachite.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Malahit_PDADoroj: A PDA belonging to the Malachite trader. Its pristine condition is a testament to the owner’s perfectionism.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Malahit_PDAKupri: This brand-new PDA contains negotiations between an STC Malachite employee and a stalker. Obtaining coupons from scientists is clearly no easy feat for a loner.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_MuhaPDA_descript: A PDA belonging to a bandit who died during a ‘negotiation’ with a rival gang in the classic Garbage tradition.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_NegodaPDA_descri: This PDA didn’t get a single scratch during many years of heavy use, but now there’s a big crack across the device’s surface.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_NestorHenchmanPD: The PDA is perfectly clean, and the screen is covered with a protector. It seems that the owner kept it from getting scratched, even after he turned into a zombie.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_NestorUSB_descri: An ordinary device used for storing and transferring information, marked with the haphazardly carved word “Nest.”
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_NoonBase_Hub_Pan: This misplaced PDA contains the Noontider’s correspondence, but it would be inappropriate to intrude into his private messages.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_NoonBase_Hub_Ros: A battered PDA belonging to a Noontider that contains an exchange filled with contemplations about the Mainland.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_NoonBase_Hub_Vec: An ordinary PDA containing correspondence on topics that concern everyone on Wild Island to varying degrees.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_NoonBase_Hub_Zav: Covered in small scratches and scuffs, this PDA seems to be ever-ready and functional, even when not intentionally in use.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_PomorPDA_descrip: This stalker’s PDA contains a map of the Poppy Field. Taking advantage of those who succumbed to sleep within the anomaly, he now finds himself trapped in a dream from which he will never awaken.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_PripoyPDA_descri: Solder’s PDA reveals the owner’s involvement in clandestine dealings with Nestor, the kingpin of the Slag Heap.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_ProjectControlle: These faded papers contain gruesome details about experiments conducted in X5. It looks like these are the documents Shcherba was after.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Prypat_NoteItem1: An 8x12 sheet carrying a message from someone who knows Degtyarev well.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Prypat_NoteItem2: A short note penned in confident handwriting.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestArtifactCry: An artifact that came out of Professor Dvupalov’s moonshine still.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestArtifactHea: An incredibly rare, almost mythical artifact that functions as a psi-radiation amplifier. The degree of amplification depends on the characteristics and individual capabilities of the source. Its properties are still not fully understood, with the comprehensive range of parameters yet unknown. Presumed to encapsulate the original structure of the Zone’s matter.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestItem_Folder: A file containing important papers – a traditional office management essential.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestItem_Fuse_L: A common fuse protecting electronic circuits from voltage fluctuations.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestItem_Fuse_M: A device that protects electronic circuits from abrupt voltage fluctuations. This specific fuse is designed with medium characteristics in mind.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestItem_KeyCar: This old blue key card is a bit scratched, but the magnetic strip seems to be intact. It should probably still work.
This old green key card is a bit scratched, but the magnetic strip seems to be intact. It should probably still work.
This old red key card is a bit scratched, but the magnetic strip seems to be intact. It should probably still work.
This key card grants Level B access.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestItem_Key_Ch: A key to an old padlock. The kind used to secure barns and garages.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestItem_Key_Do: A fairly modern key, probably for a door or a decent padlock.
A little old key, clearly meant for a door.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestItem_Key_Pa: A massive old key, probably for some kind of old-timey lock.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestItem_Notepa: The robust cover of this notebook ensures the safety of the notes within.
An officer’s field bag, used to store documents and notes. A staple for many servicemen prior to the digital revolution.
An aged, well-worn diary – an excellent repository for one’s thoughts and observations.
A simple, everyday notepad, prone to staining and water damage. Best stored in a dry place.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestItem_Record: A commonplace voice recorder, often used in the Zone for note-taking and diary-keeping.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestItem_USB_Da: This old flash drive has been through a lot. The case is held together with black duct tape.
This old flash drive has been through a lot. The case is held together with classic blue duct tape.
Evidently, this flash drive has been exposed to high temperatures. It’s nothing short of a miracle that the device still works.
This old flash drive has been through a lot. The case is held together with white duct tape.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestItem_USB_Mo: A relatively up-to-date USB drive, capable of storing a large amount of data.
A relatively up-to-date USB drive capable of storing a large amount of data.
A relatively up-to-date USB drive capable of storing a large amount of data.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestItem_USB_St: A traditional portable USB drive, widely used to store information – even in the Zone.
A traditional portable USB drive, widely used to store information – even in the Zone.
A traditional portable USB drive, widely used to store information – even in the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_QuestItem_USB_Up: This USB drive contains data related to equipment upgrades.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ01_NewbiePDA2: A PDA belonging to an unknown stalker. He thought he could make it back, but the Zone had different plans for him.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ01_NewbiePDA3: A PDA belonging to an unknown stalker. He shouldn’t have strayed from the fire.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ01_NewbiePDA4: A PDA belonging to an unknown stalker. Sometimes friendship and the drive for revenge can kill as swiftly as any anomaly.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ01_NewbiePDA_: A PDA belonging to an unknown stalker. He ventured into the Zone and never found his way back.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ01_WarlockPac: A small, neatly wrapped package ordered by Warlock. Whoever packed it has clearly done this before… and will do it again.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ04_C05_FuelCa: A tightly sealed gas can with a pungent aroma of industrial alcohol.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ04_C10_Glavar: A run-down, outdated PDA containing the ill-gotten coupons of one of the gang leaders.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ05_C01_FlashD: A securely locked briefcase requested by the merchant Owl from the Sultansk.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ05_C10_IItemP: A PDA belonging to one of Owl’s agents. Some of his operatives do more than just gather information. This one clearly found more than he bargained for.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ05_C10_ItemNo: A note on a piece of paper smeared with dried blood. Looks like whoever took down Owl’s agent isn’t stopping anytime soon.
A torn piece of a document that Owl’s agent was willing to die for… and probably did.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ05_C10_ItemPD: A PDA belonging to an agent who bit off more than he could chew. In a way, he was lucky, since Owl doesn’t take kindly to those who try to peddle his information on the side.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ06_C04_Goods_: The stolen goods Sidorovich wanted back.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ07_C09_Contai: The gaps in the container are securely insulated, but it’s still giving off a little radiation. There must be an artifact in there.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ07_Item_descr: A package containing unknown merchandise, possibly meant for Hera.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ08_Item2_desc: A brand-new flash drive in pristine condition. From the looks of it, the device was purchased for the sole purpose of delivering information to an important customer.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ08_Item_descr: A suitcase featuring a small sticker that says “Fragile!” By the sound of it, there are several bottles inside.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ09_Item_descr: A lightweight, tightly closed suitcase. If you sniff it, you catch a whiff of medicine.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RSQ10_Item_descr: An ordinary suitcase. The sound suggests it contains some metal tools.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RichtersPlayer_d: The old player now only plays one song on repeat. The worn-out button suggests the owner never went anywhere without it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RookieVillage_Ma: A brand-new PDA. The owner’s whereabouts are unknown.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RookieVillage_Wo: The screen of this dusty PDA is covered in a spiderweb of cracks. If Wolf ever uses it, it’s only as a backup.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_RooseveltPDA_des: A PDA belonging to Roosevelt, kingpin of the Commissary. Formerly with Duty, he challenged fellow bandit bosses for leadership in Garbage – an unusual fate, even by Zone standards.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Rostok_NoteAgree: One of Myklukha’s many contracts that just happened to be out in the open. Normally, he keeps them hidden from prying eyes.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Rostok_NoteToShe: An ordinary sheet of paper with a list of goods on it. Each entry is meticulously written, indicating that the author thoroughly evaluated every item before adding it to the list.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Rostok_NoteToSul: A sheet with a list written in tidy handwriting. Deliberate and unhurried, the author gave careful consideration to every entry.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Rostok_PDAPolovi: This PDA contains the correspondence that set in motion the events that ultimately led to the sergeant’s death.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Rostok_PDA_Docto: There isn’t a scratch or a speck to be found on this PDA. The owner meticulously wipes the device with alcohol on a daily basis.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Rostok_PDA_Lost_: Trying to juggle numerous tasks at once, this device’s owner occasionally forgets about certain things. In this case, he left his PDA behind without even noticing.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Rostok_YarikChil: Left unattended, this PDA contains a discussion about a guide known for never staying in one place.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SEQ01_BanditPDA_: Stalkers aren’t the only ones willing to take risks to turn an easy profit. But it always ends the same way.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SEQ02_StalkerPDA: The state of this PDA implies that its owner had some serious anger management issues. Or maybe someone really got under his skin.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SEQ04_ScientistP: Typically, so-called “free scientists” opt for more reliable record-keeping devices than a stalker’s PDA. This poor guy must’ve grappled with some serious funding issues.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SEQ05_StalkerPDA: Anomaly exposure has wiped out most of the information on this PDA, and what’s left looks rather grim.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SEQ06_StalkerPDA: It looks like this PDA’s owner wasn’t too concerned about its condition. Hopefully, he was more diligent with his weapon.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SEQ08_StalkerPDA: The dents and scratches on the screen suggest that this PDA was frequently dropped, sometimes from a considerable height.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SEQ09_StalkerPDA: The fate of this PDA’s owner is probably best left a mystery. Sometimes a good night’s sleep without any nightmares is more valuable than any loot.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SEQ10_StalkerPDA: This PDA clearly belonged to someone from the Corps, and from the looks of it, they prefer to stay under the radar.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ01_GunAK74_ST_: A regular AKM-74S in perfect condition, stored in a hidden stash at the Water Tower. Valik Lummox never got the chance to make use of his assault rifle.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ01_ValenokPDA_: A PDA belonging to a stalker who tried to escape his debts. He didn’t even make it to the Water Tower.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ02_GunM16_ST_d: An AR416 assault rifle found in the Poppy Field. You could almost feel a faint smell of flowers on its metal.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ02_PomorKey_de: A small room key taken from Pomor, a stalker from the Poppy Field.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ04_SoloveiPDA_: A PDA belonging to a hunter from Zalissya. He was a jovial man, but, unfortunately, the Zone leaves little room for humor.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ05_GuronsGoods: A tightly sealed crate containing Huron’s shipment for the Brood.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ06_CargoNote_d: An old form. The text is still partially legible.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ06_MSOPAudiolo: It looks like an ordinary voice recorder, but the information it contains is rather useful.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ06_PDA_ZombieS: An old PDA belonging to a scientist. The owner’s bleak end leaves little room for imagination.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ06_PsiLampDest: A device resembling a lamp. It was a powerful source of psi-radiation, so I had to break it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ06_PsiLamp_des: A device with an unknown purpose, somehow linked to Monolith. Once activated, it produces radiation that’s harmful to the human nervous system.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_BrokenDash: Looks okay to be put up for sale, but only a merchant can tell whether it still works, or if I can only sell it for scrap.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_CircuitBoa: A complex board from an unknown device. A stalker would have no use for it, but it could be worth a lot.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_DashboardP: These haven't been around for about 40 years, but the scientists keep paying merchants to replace their worn-out ones.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_DeadDigger: One of the first PDA models that has seen some haphazard repairs. Looks like its previous owner didn't have enough money to go to a technician.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_DeaddropIn: A notebook page with instructions, written in the same handwriting as the markings on the map.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_Emitter_de: The Emitter that Diode needed so desperately. An open case with thin-film PCBs inside. A device like this can't be manufactured or repaired anywhere in the Zone.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_KeyCardX18: A reprogrammed magnetic card with X18 scratched into it. It takes a skilled technician to create a copy of the original key.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_Key_descri: Standard key to a door lock with an X18 inventory tag
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_Key_name: Key to the door to X18
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_MapNote_de: A notebook page with the code to the safe where the Emitter needs to be placed, quickly written in shaky handwriting.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_NestorMikh: A sheet of paper folded neatly into an envelope. A report on the operation of the Aggression Suppressor, written in tiny, sharp handwriting. On top of the text is Nestor's huge ‘resolution’.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_OldMonitor: The CRTs from these sell pretty well. There are plenty of rumors about what they're used for, but no merchant will let you in on the secret.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_Oscillosco: A Japanese wideband oscilloscope. Used to be a top-shelf model 30 years ago, but still sells well. "P.D. Stryzh" is written on the inventory tag.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_Powerbank_: An ancient model, as reliable and simple as they come. Any merchant would want it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_Voltmeter_: A precise voltmeter – a great tool for any technician. This one looks operational, and could be worth quite a lot of coupons.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ103_Voltpannel: This model is popular, and pretty expensive. A perfect match for sensitive equipment.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ10_BunchOfKeys: A set of keys providing access to the waste processing station’s facilities. Two keys stand out: one for the basement, and one for the shift supervisor’s office.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ10_DubniyPDA_d: A PDA belonging to Dubny, Strider’s right-hand man. Its owner is unlikely to appreciate the idea of someone else reading his correspondence.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ10_HogPDA_desc: This PDA belonged to a mercenary known as Hog. Its owner died as a result of his unwavering commitment to the job.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ10_JumperPDA_d: A PDA belonging to Jumper, a Noontider from the waste processing station. He put his life on the line to rescue his partner, but the Zone doesn’t always reward the brave.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ10_SeverNoteDu: A sheet of grayish paper with a report written in big letters. Who was this report intended for? It hardly matters now.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ10_TihijMonoli: A hastily scribbled message on a small piece of paper. The author must have been in a rush to make a speedy exit.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ13_PDA_Budnik_: This PDA was retrieved from a dead Warden at the Chemical Tanks. He died while helping his comrades escape from mutants.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ13_Soul_descri: An artifact found at the Chemical Tanks. According to some, a Soul is created when a human body is ensnared by an anomaly.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ18_KamysPDA_de: One of the bullets fired at the bandit became lodged in his PDA. The Ringmaster’s death was swift and less agonizing than those of his victims.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ18_KamysPaperN: A neatly folded piece of paper with a request from someone who wished to remain anonymous. Nevertheless, the recipient is well aware of the sender’s identity.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ47_DavidAkopan: A PDA belonging to the stalker held captive by Zakhar Babay’s thugs. Seduced by the promise of easy coupons, he ended up getting his ass kicked.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ47_LevaBorzoj_: A PDA belonging to a thug from Garbage, Zakhar Babay’s right-hand man and the scourge of the loners who walked into his ambush.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ50_SultanSuitc: The briefcase from the Sultan’s hidden stash aboard the Lviv. It seems surprisingly lightweight for an item of such value.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ86_GenijAK74_d: A customized variant of the standard model. The neatly etched name “Mitya” and a recent paint job suggest that the owner took excellent care of the weapon.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ86_SashkaBitok: A PDA found on a dead loner in the underground area beneath the Concrete Forest. Few stand a chance of survival when trapped between stalker greed and mutant ferocity.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ87_AdikPedalKe: This weathered metal key opens the door to the administrative building at the Fish Farm, where Adik Pedal held stalkers captive.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ87_AdikPedalPD: The notes in this PDA leave no doubt about the owner’s desire to overthrow the Sultan. It was his own ambition that led to his downfall. Found near the Fish Farm in Zaton.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ87_ZenaGlybaPD: A PDA found on the body of Zhenya Hulk at the Fish Farm. Even when confronted with a hopeless situation, the stalker refused to give up the fight for his life. Unfortunately, his struggle was futile.

A PDA found on the body of Zhenya Hulk at the Fish Farm. In spite of the warning, the stalker held onto his belief in the deal with the bandits. While they did come to his rescue in the end, it didn’t turn out well.

A PDA found on the body of Zhenya Hulk at the Fish Farm. The stalker paid Sultan for protection, but it didn’t save him from getting killed. Looks like the kingpin of Zaton needs to think long and hard about the quality of his services.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ88_GrebenNote_: This PDA contains a diary in which Crest documents his plan for revenge. The stalker was racing against time, striving to realize his plan before he succumbed to radiation sickness. Found on the stalker’s corpse in the Kindergarten.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ88_KuvaldaDiar: Sledgehammer’s diary chronicles his lucrative artifact trade with the IPSF, but the mysterious disappearance of his couriers alerted the veteran stalker. Found inside a store in Chornobyl-2.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ88_MacekPDA_de: This PDA contains correspondence between Machek and an unidentified stalker. Looks like their deal went off the rails. Discovered on the soldier’s corpse at a school in Chornobyl-2.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ88_NimbleToBea: Looks like Beard gave Nimble an errand to run - ask around where some fellow named Sledgehammer went. The result isn't promising - Sledgehammer took off to Chornobyl and won't be getting Beard any more artifacts.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ89_ZhgutPDA_de: Retrieved from a stalker’s body at the Pig Feedlot. Wisp and his partner were trying to compete with Sidorovich by establishing a trading post at the Tunnel Camp. Regrettably, their ambitious business plan was thwarted by a pack of hungry mutants.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ90_FreedomPDA_: This PDA details a plan for a Freedom assault on a bandit base. The carnage indicates that the Freedom squad didn’t expect to encounter any resistance there.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ90_GribPDA_des: A PDA belonging to a bandit from the Red Forest. In his correspondence with the gang leader, Mushroom snitches on his comrades, reporting that they got drunk, lured a mutant, and locked it inside a container. In response, the leader vividly outlines the consequences awaiting those found drinking on duty.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ90_KeyFromTunn: This key grants access to the tunnels beneath the bandit base.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ90_ParikPDA_de: The messages on this PDA belonging to the Red Forest gang leader’s lieutenant reference an informant at the Cement Factory. I can only guess how Duty members stay in the loop about Freedom’s activities.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ90_PseudoGiant: An oversized iron collar equipped with an unknown mechanism, retrieved from a pseudogiant in the Red Forest. The tag, somewhat preserved, identifies it as “Test Subject #19.”
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ90_SefPDA_desc: This PDA belonging to a gang leader contains messages exchanged with a Duty member who has been leaking information about Freedom’s plans. It seems someone has discovered a loophole in the treaty.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ90_ToropygaPDA: The messages stored on this PDA discuss a scheme to mine artifacts using other people’s labor. A neglected anomaly beneath the base has ignited the bandits’ “entrepreneurial spirit.”
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ92_MangustPDA_: Recovered from a Sparker’s body at the silo near the Chemical Plant, this PDA contains a conversation with a scientist who asked the deceased to test some equipment for him. The experiment resulted in a tragic outcome for Mongoose.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SQ92_VolkovPDA_d: In his exchange with a fellow soldier, the Warden’s anxiety about patrolling the silo was bordering on paranoia. But his fears turned out to be justified – payback for his past deeds had arrived in the shape of a pack of bloodsuckers.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Scanner_descript: The TOPAZ anomaly detection scanner, given to me by Hermann. This modification was used in artifact recharging experiments, but was discontinued due to safety issues. But at this point, I’ve got nothing left to lose.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_ShahPDA_descript: A PDA belonging to the Shah, kingpin of the Brood. He aimed to take over the Slag Heap, but ended up choking on his own blood. Greed, in the end, fails even the greedy.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Shevchenko_Camp_: Sporting numerous well-worn stickers on the back panel, this aged PDA apparently sees little downtime.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Shevchenko_NoteB: A brief shopping list. Based on the items on it, someone either caused trouble for Beard, or he was getting ready to stir up some trouble himself.
List of Equipment for the Shevchenko
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Shevchenko_NoteD: A intact page from a stalker’s diary, found on the Shevchenko. It offers a glimpse into the author’s life over the course of several days.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SkifGun_descript: Skif’s award PTM. A somewhat humiliating army reminder that became a comfortable, familiar weapon.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_SpoiledCannedFoo: A swollen can of food, expired long before the Zone came into being. Without a decent gas mask, the stench is unbearable.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_StalkerPDA_SQ103: A zombified stalker's PDA from the X18 laboratory. It's all covered in numbered gum wrappers. Missing just a few to complete the collection.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_StrangePDA_descr: An unusual PDA, distinct from the standard stalker equipment. Its last owner was part of the crew hunting for the Scanners and met his end at the hands of Varan’s bandits, much like the device itself.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Sultansk_Hub_PDA: The device is coated in dirt and blood, much like its lifeless owner. Whatever this stalker was looking for at the Cordon, it certainly wasn’t a bullet.
Dead Stalker’s PDA from the Cordon
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Sultansk_NoteAgr: This document has been carefully preserved against dirt and damage. The Sultan turns to it for a quick pick-me-up whenever he’s feeling blue.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Sultansk_NoteKal: The uneven handwriting on the paper betrays the author’s nervous state. On the other hand, the notation at the bottom looks like it was written in a steady, confident hand.
This sheet serves as Sonya Kalina’s appointment book. Her time is precious indeed – anyone who canceled a meeting with her would have a lot of explaining to do.
An ordinary 8x12 sheet outlining Kalina’s plans for the day. It’s packed with activities – there doesn’t seem to be a single moment of free time in her schedule.
A sheet of neatly laid-out text, leaving plenty of free space to accommodate the author’s ambitious plans.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Sultansk_NotePar: The scuffs on this sheet of paper indicate that it was passed around, and the ink stains confirm that the grocery list must have been a group effort.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Sultansk_NoteZlo: A small scrap of paper covered in scrawled handwriting. The author was clearly in a hurry.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Sultansk_PDAChil: This PDA is in good shape, indicating that its owner steers clear of situations that could result in damage to the device.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Sultansk_PDAKali: This device boasts abundant contacts, but very little correspondence. Its owner promptly deletes whatever she doesn’t want others to see.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Sultansk_PDARyhl: This PDA is in quite a battered state, yet its owner fared far worse.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Sultansk_PDASult: Outgoing messages are a rare sight on this PDA, and incoming messages are even rarer.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Sultansk_PDASych: This PDA has been through a lot, much like its owner. Only recent correspondence is still there – the rest has been deleted.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Terricon_Hub_Kis: Found in the catacombs beneath the Slag Heap, this PDA serves as a reminder to think twice before crossing its former owner.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Terricon_Hub_Mer: Abandoned without much thought by its owner, this PDA is covered in a surprisingly thick and even layer of dust. It seems like no one has picked it up for a very long time.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Terricon_Hub_Zor: Despite being chipped around the edges, this PDA still remains operational – unlike its former owner.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Terricon_NoteLis: A tattered handwritten note revealing a concise plan devised by four comrades from the Slag Heap. What could have happened to them?
Piece of Paper with a List
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Terricon_PDAAbou: If the message on this PDA is any indication, the owner has more pressing concerns than the prospect of losing the device.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_TestEQ_MoosePDA_: Обычный сталкерский КПК, изрядно потертый и поцарапанный.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_VaranPDA_descrip: A PDA belonging to Varan, the bandit boss. He wanted to be the kingpin of Garbage, but he wound up just another corpse.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_VargaPDA_descrip: A PDA belonging to Varga, stalker , who was defending the body of his friend from bandits
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_VartaDogtag_desc: A polished, handmade badge personally issued by Korshunov. The wearer of this badge holds the power to give orders as though they originated from the colonel himself.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_VortexDudePDA_de: Contains some poor bastard’s conversation with his buddy.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_VortexDudePDA_na: PDA of a Stalker Who Fell from the Sky
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Yanov_KostaBandu: A typical PDA, showing signs of use and containing plenty of contacts and messages. Unless the owner has left for Prypiat, there’s a chance he might come back for it.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Yanov_NoteHana_d: A small sheet of paper that has been hastily filled out. Apparently, the author is no stranger to compiling such lists.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Yanov_NoteOrder_: A sheet of paper in impeccable condition, carefully preserved for a special occasion.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Yanov_Note_ToDoL: A crumpled sheet of paper full of corrections, annotations, and crossed-out sections.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Yanov_PDA_Garpia: Despite having seen its share of repairs, this PDA is in excellent working condition. Its owner clearly has a knack for technology and is in no rush to retire the device.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Yanov_PDA_Nor_de: While there’s no apparent damage, the back panel of this PDA bears significant scuff marks, hinting that its owner tends to tap it on the table when nervous.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Yanov_SenaDymPDA: This PDA continues to receive messages, but there’s no one left to read them.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Zalesie_BatyaPDA: An ordinary stalker PDA. The inscription scratched on the back panel of the device says “The Gaffer.”
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Zalesie_HomakNot: A small handwritten note. The messy, uneven handwriting aptly capture the sender’s emotional state.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Zalesie_HomakPDA: This PDA is seldom quiet. Its owner is constantly barraged with job offers – or calls expressing a lack of interest.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Zalesie_KoldunNo: A brief, succinct message written on a scrap of paper.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Zalesie_KoldunPD: Typically, PDA owners either keep them hidden from prying eyes or erase all sensitive data on them. However, this particular device still contains an exchange that wasn’t deleted in time.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Zalesie_LenaPDA_: A rather battered PDA. Its owner traversed many miles across the Zone before discovering safer routes.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Zalesie_LinzaPDA: An ordinary piece of paper with a message for a buddy on it. The use of different inks in various sections suggests that the author didn’t write it all in one go.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_Zalesie_NoteFrom: A stack of hastily scribbled sheets. Only one note is actually legible amid the otherwise indecipherable chicken-scratchings.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_ZhukovskyPDA_des: A PDA belonging to a recruit from Zulu’s unit, discovered on a corpse in the Eastern Tunnel. The device’s screen is cracked and smeared with blood. A seemingly simple mission turned out to be its unfortunate owner’s last.
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_ZuzaPDA_descript: The PDA of Gonta's apprentice, who dreamt of glory. It seems Yaryk had his reasons to chase a vibrant life, no matter how little of it he had left."
ST_S2BaseGameLocalization.sid_questItemprototypes_d1paritypack_ANC: A sheet of paper with notes about missing people. It looks messy, as every page has different handwriting and ink color.
Notes about MIA Duty fighters
A paperback notebook with snipers' notes.
Observations notebook
A perfectly folded sheet of paper with a list of names, written carefully in block letters.
Target list
A device with a large crack in the screen and scratches on the back. The owner is not particularly careful with his equipment, or dedicated to his work.
Lone stalker's PDA
The PDA looks new, or the owner was very careful with it. There's nothing on it apart from work-related chats and a map.
Lone stalker's PDA
A PDA that has seen some skillful and not so skillful fixes. Looks like its owner had been through a lot before he ended up near the Duga.
Lone stalker's PDA
A small sheet of paper with handwritten text.
Folded note
A heavy log with neatly drawn columns and dozens of different types of handwriting.
Complaint and request log
A neatly folded sheet of paper with some kind of list of names. Looks like it belonged to a person who made a living delivering packages and finding all kinds of trinkets around the Zone.
Page from a notebook, number 35

A neatly folded sheet of paper with a list of someone's orders, written in a hurry. Looks like it belonged to a person who made a living delivering packages and finding all kinds of trinkets around the Zone.
Page from a notebook, number 31
A neatly folded sheet of paper with some kind of list of names. Looks like it belonged to a person who made a living delivering packages and finding all kinds of trinkets around the Zone.
Page from a notebook, number 32

A neatly folded sheet of paper with a list of someone's orders, written in a hurry. Looks like it belonged to a person who made a living delivering packages and finding all kinds of trinkets around the Zone.
